(وَاذْكُرْ عِبادَنا إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصارِ) The wāw is a conjunction; اذكر is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you", that is, "remember, O Muḥammad, their patience over what befell them and their steadfastness in their beliefs, and take them as an example"; عبادنا is a direct object; إبراهيم is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān; إسحاق and يعقوب are conjoined to إبراهيم; أولي الأيد, that is, "possessors of hands", is a direct object (the meaning of أولي الأيد will be discussed at length in the section on rhetoric); الأبصار is conjoined to الأيد.
(إِنَّا أَخْلَصْناهُمْ بِخالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ) The clause gives the reason for the highness of rank with which they were described and their elevation through knowledge and deed. إن and its noun, and the clause أخلصناهم is the khabar of إنا; بخالصة: the two are attached to أخلصناهم, and the باء is either causal, if أخلصناهم means "We made them pure", or for transitivity, if أخلصناهم means "We singled them out"; خالصة is an adjective of an omitted described noun, that is, "by a pure quality"; and ذكرى الدار may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ or a badal from خالصة. If خالصة is taken as implying the sense of sincerity (ikhlāṣ), then ذكرى is a direct object of خالصة; if it is a maṣdar with the sense of purity (khulūṣ), then ذكرى is its agent. That makes four aspects for it. As for the annexation of ذكرى to الدار, it is an annexation of the maṣdar to its object, that is, "their remembrance of the Hereafter". There are multiple readings here, to be consulted in the longer works.
(وَإِنَّهُمْ عِنْدَنا لَمِنَ الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ الْأَخْيارِ) وإنهم: إن with its noun; عندنا is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; the lām in لمن is the shifted lām; من المصطفين is the khabar of إنهم; الأخيار is an adjective. (وَاذْكُرْ إِسْماعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِنَ الْأَخْيارِ) واذكر is conjoined to what preceded; اذكر إسماعيل: a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; اليسع and ذا الكفل are conjoined to إسماعيل; كل is a mubtadaʾ, permissible to begin with because of the sense of generality it contains; من الأخيار is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
There is a kināya (allusion) in His words «أولي الأيد والأبصار», which is an allusion to righteous deed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Possessors of deeds and reflection, as if those who do not do the deeds of the Hereafter, do not strive in Allah's cause, do not reflect as the people of religions reflect, and have no insight, are in the position of the crippled who cannot use their limbs and of those robbed of their minds who have no insight." There is also in it the art of ta'rīḍ (indirect hint), that whoever is not among the workers for Allah and not among those with insight into Allah's religion deserves rebuke and the worst censure. Al-aydī is the plural of yad, which is the limb, so the allusion by it is because all deeds are performed with it; and if it is a plural of yad in the sense of favour, then it is a mursal trope (majāz mursal) whose relation is causality, which has been discussed before, since the hand is the cause of favour. The yāʾ was dropped in the script of the muṣḥaf, content with the kasra in its place. Some explained al-ayd in the sense of strength; though it is permissible in terms of language, the context weakens its use in this sense. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its explanation as al-ayd from al-taʾyīd (support) is unsettled and not possible."

dervis-irab:49-60.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ): women who restrain their gaze to their husbands and look at no one else.
(أَتْرابٌ): of equal age. They were so named as if the dust (turāb) had touched them at one time. Al-Bayḍāwī says: "atrāb for their husbands, lidāt for them, that is, equal to their husbands in age, for love among peers is firmer." Al-Zamakhsharī preferred that the equality be among themselves rather than with their husbands. In al-Qāmūs: "Al-tirb, with kasra, is the lida, the age, and the one born with you; she is my tirb, and tārabtuhā: she became her tirb." ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
أبرزوها مثل المهاة تهادى ... من خمس كواعب أتراب
(They brought her forth like a wild cow, walking gracefully, among five full-breasted girls of equal age.)
Someone has versified the meanings of this root, saying:
وضع تراب فوق صك ترب ... ضرب ترائب كذا والتّرب
مثلك سنا والتراب التّرب ... ترائب الشخص عظام الصدر
ومصدر لترب الشيء التّرب ... وجمع ترب الشخص في العمر التّرب وجمع تربة بضم التّرب ... أي قطعة من التراب فادر
(Putting dust over a document, tarraba; striking; the chest-bones, tarāʾib; likewise al-tirb, one equal to you in age; and al-turāb is al-tarb; the tarāʾib of a person are the bones of the chest; the verbal noun of tariba al-shayʾ is al-tarab; the plural of the tirb of a person in age is atrāb; and the plural of turba, with ḍamma, is al-turab, a piece of earth, so know it.) «[Translator's note: the verses are given as in the source, which is corrupt in places; the gloss follows the sense of the lexical items they list]»
(وَغَسَّاقٌ): what flows from the pus of the people of the Fire. In al-Qāmūs: "ghasaqa l-jurḥ: yellow water flowed from the wound." And it is said: the ḥamīm burns by its heat, and the ghassāq burns by its cold.

* I'rab:
(هذا ذِكْرٌ وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to announce the end of the preceding stories and the beginning of another subject. هذا is a mubtadaʾ and ذكر is a khabar; وإن: the wāw is resumptive, and إن is a particle resembling the verb; للمتقين is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām; حسن مآب is its postponed noun. (جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الْأَبْوابُ) جنات عدن is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān of حسن مآب; مفتحة is a ḥāl from جنات عدن, and its governor is the verbal sense contained in المتقين; لهم: the two are attached to مفتحة; الأبواب is the deputy agent of مفتحة since it is a passive participle. Al-Zamakhsharī said, on the i'rab of this verse: "مفتحة is a ḥāl and its governor is the verbal sense in للمتقين; in مفتحة is the pronoun of the gardens, and الأبواب is a badal from the pronoun, its implied form being 'opened, they, the doors', like their saying 'Zayd was struck, the hand and the foot', and it is a badal of inclusion. It was read جنات عدن مفتحة in the nominative, with جنات عدن as a mubtadaʾ and مفتحة its khabar, or both as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, 'it is gardens of Eden, they being opened for them'."
(مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيها يَدْعُونَ فِيها بِفاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ وَشَرابٍ) متكئين is a ḥāl from the هاء in لهم, and its governor is مفتحة; فيها: the two are attached to متكئين; the clause يدعون is either resumptive, to explain their state in it, or may be a ḥāl of what was mentioned; فيها is a ḥāl from the agent of يدعون, that is, "while they are in it"; بفاكهة: the two are attached to يدعون. Limiting it to fruit gives the intimation that their food there is not for nourishment and maintenance of the body but purely for pleasure and enjoyment; كثيرة is an adjective; شراب is conjoined to فاكهة. (وَعِنْدَهُمْ قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ أَتْرابٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; the adverbial is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; قاصرات الطرف is a postponed mubtadaʾ; أتراب is an adjective of قاصرات. (هذا ما تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ الْحِسابِ) The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and ما is a khabar; the clause توعدون is the ṣila; ليوم الحساب: the two are attached to توعدون; the lām is for reason, that is, "for the sake of the Day of Reckoning". I see that it is permissible to parse ما as a badal from the demonstrative, with ليوم الحساب as the khabar, and perhaps that is preferable.
(إِنَّ هذا لَرِزْقُنا ما لَهُ مِنْ نَفادٍ) إن and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; رزقنا is the khabar of إن; ما is negative, in the Ḥijāzī or the Tamīmī manner; له is a fronted khabar; من is a redundant preposition; نفاد is a noun genitive in form by من, in the position of the nominative as the postponed noun of ما, or a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(هذا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ) هذا is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, or a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the discourse is resumptive; its like was given shortly before. Ibn al-Athīr said: "This in this place belongs to faṣl (separation) which is better than waṣl (connection), and it is a firm tie between leaving one speech for another." The wāw is a conjunction and إن is a particle resembling the verb; للطاغين is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām; شر مآب is the postponed noun of إن. (جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَها فَبِئْسَ الْمِهادُ) A badal from شر مآب or ʿaṭf bayān of it, and the clause يصلونها is a ḥāl; it is an imperfect verb «[Translator's note: the source says "and it is a direct object of an imperfect" (وهو مفعول مضارع), apparently meaning يصلونها is an imperfect verb]», the wāw is the agent and the هاء a direct object; you may also parse جهنم as an object of an omitted verb indicated by يصلونها. The فاء is the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if you want to know the reality of Hell, it is a wretched resting place"; بئس is an inert verb for the composition of blame; المهاد is its agent; the one specified is omitted, its implied form being "it". (هذا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ) هذا is a mubtadaʾ, and حميم and غساق are its two khabars; the clause فليذوقوه is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya); the فاء is parenthetical; the lām is the lām of command; يذوقوه is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command, the wāw an agent and the هاء a direct object. The statements of the grammarians on this verse are much confused; the following is what Abū l-Baqāʾ said:
"هذا is a mubtadaʾ, and there are two aspects for the khabar. One is فليذوقوه, like your saying 'Zayd, strike him'; a group said this is weak because of the fāʾ, which is not in the sense of an apodosis like the one in «والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا». As for حميم on this aspect, it may be a badal from هذا, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, 'it is ḥamīm', or a second khabar. The second aspect is that حميم is the khabar of هذا, and فليذوقوه is parenthetical between them. It is also said that هذا is in the position of the accusative, that is, 'let them taste this', then he began anew and said حميم, that is, 'it is ḥamīm'. As for غساق, it is read with shadda like kaffār and ṣabbār, and with light sīn as a noun for the maṣdar, that is, 'possessing ghasaq', or fiʿāl in the sense of fāʿil."
(وَآخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ أَزْواجٌ) وآخر is conjoined to حميم and غساق; من شكله is an adjective of it; أزواج is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are", or an attribute of the three.
(هذا فَوْجٌ مُقْتَحِمٌ مَعَكُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صالُوا النَّارِ) The clause is the quoted speech of an omitted saying, that is, "and it will be said to them when they enter the Fire". هذا is a mubtadaʾ and فوج a khabar; مقتحم is an adjective of فوج; معكم is an adverbial attached to an omitted second adjective of فوج, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in مقتحم, or from فوج because it is described; لا is negative; مرحبا is accusative as a maṣdar; بهم: the two are attached to مرحبا. In the negated clause there are two aspects: one, that it is resumptive, delivered as a supplication against them for narrowness of place; or a ḥāl, that is, "this is a throng rushing in, it being said to them: no welcome to them". In al-Qurṭubī: "The leaders said: «لا مرحبا بهم», that is, may their dwellings in the Fire not be spacious. Al-raḥb is spaciousness, and from it comes raḥbat al-majd and others; it has the sense of a supplication, and for that reason is accusative." Abū ʿUbayda said: The Arabs say «lā marḥaban bika», that is, may the earth not be wide for you nor spacious. The clause إنهم صالو النار gives the reason for their deserving the supplication against them; إن and its noun, and صالو النار is its khabar.
(قالُوا بَلْ أَنْتُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ أَنْتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ لَنا فَبِئْسَ الْقَرارُ) قالوا is a verb and agent, and the pronoun refers to the followers; بل is a particle of retraction; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; لا مرحبا is the quoted speech of an omitted saying, which is the khabar, that is, "it is said to you"; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause قدمتموه is its khabar; قدمتموه is a past verb, the tāʾ an agent, the mīm the mark of the masculine plural, the wāw for filling out the ḍamma of the mīm, and the هاء a direct object; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قدمتموه. فبئس: the فاء is a conjunction; بئس is an inert past verb for the composition of blame; القرار is its agent; the one specified for blame is omitted, that is, "the Fire".

dervis-irab:12-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَوْتادِ) : In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«الوتد» with kasra on the tāʾ is in the dialect of the Ḥijāz and is the most eloquent; its plural is «أوتاد». With fatḥa on the tāʾ is a dialect. The people of Najd make the tāʾ quiescent and assimilate it after the conversion, so «ود» remains. «وتدت الوتد أتده وتدا» (from the bāb of waʿada) means I fixed it in a wall or in the ground, and «أوتدته» with an alif is a dialectal form." In al-Asās: "He drove the peg, «الودّ» and «الأوتاد» with the mallet. It is said «تد وتدك» and «أوتده», and «انتصب كأنه وتد» (he stood up as if he were a peg), and «أذل من وتد» (more abased than a peg), and «وتد واتد» means firm. Among the figurative uses: «وتد الله الأرض بالجبال» and «أوتدها» and «وتّدها»; the mountains are the pegs of the earth. A bedouin was asked: 'What is the naṭshān?' He said: 'The thirsty man pegs.' It is also reported: 'something with which we peg our speech.'" In al-Qāmūs: "«الوتد» with fatḥa, also with vowelling of the second letter, and like «كتف»: what is driven into the earth or a wall, of wood; and in prosody, what is of three letters like «على»; and the small protrusion in the front of the ear. The plural is «أوتاد»; «وتد واتد» is emphasis. The «أوتاد الأرض» are its mountains; of lands, their chiefs; of the mouth, its teeth."
(الْأَيْكَةِ) : The thicket and the tangled, clustered trees; it has been discussed at length before.
(فَواقٍ) : With fatḥa on the fāʾ or ḍamma, meaning a return. It was read with both, and it was said that they are two forms with one meaning, namely the interval between two milkings of the milker and two sucklings of the suckling young; the meaning is that it has no pause even for the length of the «فواق» of a she-camel. In the Ḥadīth: "A visit to the sick is the length of the fawāq of a she-camel." In al-Mukhtār: "«الفواق» is the time between two milkings, because she is milked, then left for an hour for the young to suckle her so that her milk flows, then milked. It is said: «ما أقام عنده إلا فواقا» (he stayed with him only a fawāq). In the Ḥadīth: «العيادة قدر فواق ناقة». And His words the Exalted «من فواق» is read with fatḥa, that is, 'it has no respite, rest or recovery'." The wording of al-Zamakhsharī in al-Kashshāf: "«ما لها من فواق». It was also read with ḍamma: it has no pause for the length of a fawāq, which is the interval between two milkings of the milker and two sucklings of the suckling young. He means that when its time comes it will not be delayed by this amount of time, as in His words the Exalted «فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة». From Ibn ʿAbbās: it has no return or repetition, from «أفاق المريض» when he returns to health; and the «فواق» of a she-camel is the hour in which the milk returns to her udder. He means that it is a single blast only, not to be repeated or returned." This root has wonderful features, in that it is distributed over diverse kinds of meanings, and here we quote for you a summary of what appears of it in al-Lisān and al-Asās: "«ما بقي في كنانتي إلا سهم أفوق» — an arrow in one of whose notches there is a break or a slant; «فوّق السهم» means he placed the bowstring in its notch when shooting. You say: «لا زالت للخير موفقا، وسهمك في الكرم مفوّقا». «فوّقه»: he made a notch for it; «فاقه»: he broke its notch; «فاق قومه»: he surpassed them; «رجل فائق في العلم» and he «يتفوق على قومه»; «فوقته عليهم»: I made him excel; «أفاق فلان من المرض» and «استفاق»; and so-and-so is an addict who does not recover from drink; «تفوّق الفصيل أمه»: the young suckled its mother fawāq by fawāq, and the herdsman «فوّقه». Among the figurative uses: «تفوقت الماء»: I drank it little by little; «تفوّقت مالي»: I spent it slowly. He said:
تفوّقت مالي من طريف وتالد ... تفوّقي الصهباء من حلب الكرم
(I drained my wealth, new and inherited, as one drains the red wine from the vine's pressing.) «تفوقت وردي»: I took it little by little; «أتيته فيقة الضحى وميعته»: I came to him at the early forenoon; «خرجنا بعد أفاويق من الليل»: we went out after some portions of the night; «مجت السحابة أفاويقها»; «أرضعني أفاويق بره»; «فوّقني الأماني»; and «ما أقام عنده إلا فواق ناقة وفيقة ناقة». Perhaps in this there is sufficiency.

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَعادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ ذُو الْأَوْتادِ) A resumptive statement introduced to affirm the conditions of the tyrants and to explain the fates of the obstinate. «كَذَّبَتْ» is a past verb; «قَبْلَهُمْ» is an adverbial attached to «كَذَّبَتْ»; «قَوْمُ نُوحٍ» is the agent; «عادٌ» is conjoined to «قَوْمُ نُوحٍ», and «فِرْعَوْنُ» is likewise conjoined; «ذُو الْأَوْتادِ» means the possessor of firmly established sovereignty, and the metaphor of the pegs will be mentioned in the section on Rhetoric. (وَثَمُودُ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ وَأَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ أُولئِكَ الْأَحْزابُ) Likewise conjoined. As for «أُولئِكَ الْأَحْزابُ», you may make the demonstrative a badal of what precedes and «الْأَحْزابُ» a badal of it, or you may make it an independent clause composed of a mubtadaʾ, the demonstrative, and a khabar, «الْأَحْزابُ». (إِنْ كُلٌّ إِلَّا كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ عِقابِ) «إِنْ» is negative and inoperative because the negation is broken by «إِلَّا»; «كُلٌّ» is a mubtadaʾ; «إِلَّا» is a particle of restriction, and the clause «كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ» is the khabar of «كُلٌّ». «فَحَقَّ»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, «حَقَّ» is a past verb, and «عِقابِ» is its agent, in the nominative with an implied ḍamma on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first person, to preserve the verse endings.
(وَما يَنْظُرُ هؤُلاءِ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً ما لَها مِنْ فَواقٍ) The wāw is resumptive and the discourse is resumptive, introduced to affirm the punishment of the disbelievers of Mecca after explaining the punishment of those who preceded them in error. «ما» is negative; «يَنْظُرُ» is an imperfect verb, meaning "awaits"; «هؤُلاءِ» is a demonstrative indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the nominative as agent; «إِلَّا» is a particle of restriction; «صَيْحَةً» is a direct object and «واحِدَةً» its adjective; «ما» is the Ḥijāzī or the Tamīmī negative; «لَها» is a fronted khabar; «مِنْ» is a redundant preposition, and «فَواقٍ» is a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, as the noun of «ما» or as a postponed mubtadaʾ.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ذو الأوتاد» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), meaning possessor of firmly established, secure sovereignty; its origin is in the steadiness of the tent drawn tight by its pegs. Al-Rufāda al-Awdī said:
البيت لا يبتني إلا على عمد ... ولا عماد إذا لم ترس أوتاد
(The tent is not built except on poles, and there are no poles unless pegs are set firm.) He says: a matter is not attained except through the availability of its means. He likened the dependence of the matter on its means, and the dependence of its means on something else, to the dependence of pitching a tent on the erection of the poles and the dependence of their erection on the setting of the pegs, tied with ropes. And after it:
فإن تجمع أسباب وأعمدة ... وساكن بلغوا الأمر الذي كادوا
(If ropes, poles and dwellers gather together, they attain the thing they strove for.) Then he said: if the ropes tied to the firm pegs are gathered, the poles are erected and the dweller is found, he reaches his aim; «ساكن» has the meaning of a plural, so the plural pronoun for it is correct. The meaning of «كادوا» is "they laboured": it is said «كاده كيدا» meaning he laboured over it, and the sense is "they attained the thing they strove to obtain". And al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said:
ماذا أؤمل بعد آل محرق ... تركوا منازلهم وبعد إياد
جرت الرياح على مقر ديارهم ... فكأنهم كانوا على ميعاد
ولقد غنوا فيها بأنعم عيشة ... في ظل ملك ثابت الأوتاد
فإذا النعيم وكل ما يلهى به ... يوما يصير إلى بلى ونفاد
(What can I hope for after the House of Muḥarriq, who left their dwellings, and after Iyād? The winds blew over the sites of their homes, as though they had made an appointment. They had lived in them in the most luxurious life, in the shade of a sovereignty with firm pegs. Then all luxury and everything that diverts passes one day to decay and extinction.) He says: I wish for nothing of this world after them. Muḥarriq is Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī al-Lakhmī. «الإياد» originally is soil gathered around a basin, and the house protects it from rain and floods; it comes from «الأيد», meaning strength, or what supports a thing in general, also the shelter and the fortified mountain; «إياد الجيش» are its two wings, its right and left flanks; «الأيّد» is the strong. Iyād here is the name of the son of Nizār ibn Maʿadd ibn ʿAdnān, so he is the brother of Muḍar and Rabīʿa, and by it in the verse he meant the tribe; it is also reported «وآل إياد» conjoined to «آل محرق». «غني بالمكان», like «رضي», means he stayed in it. «البلى» is wearing away, and «النفاد» is extinction. He says: «تركوا منازلهم»: this is a resumptive clause to explain the negation of hope, or parenthetical between the two conjoined elements; and the clause «جرت الرياح» is resumptive, introduced to describe the state of the two tribes. He says: they perished, so the winds blew over the places of their homes; the winds' blowing over the sites of homes is because of the collapse of the walls that used to hold off the winds, and that is a metonymy (kināya) for their death. He indicated that their perishing was swift, as though it came at once, by his words «فكأنهم كانوا على ميعاد واحد». They had lived a stretch of time in the most luxurious life, and he likened the sovereignty through which came their might and assault to a tent pitched over them; the shade is the embellishing element (tarshīḥ) and the pegs the imaginative element (takhyīl). «إذا» is the sudden «إذا», that is, it suddenly appeared that all luxury is certain to pass away.
It was also said that there is no metaphor in the verse, and that Pharaoh would fix four pegs for everyone with whom he was angry, bind his hands and feet to them and torture him until he died. But the first is better and more eloquent.

dervis-irab:16-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قِطَّنا) : Our share and portion of the punishment. It is originally from «قطّ الشيء», meaning he cut it, and from it comes «قط القلم» (cutting the pen). They said it in mockery, meaning "hasten for us a portion of what You promised us". «القط» is applied to a written sheet and a deed (ṣakk), because each is a piece, and a reward is called «قط» because it is a piece of a gift. Its plural is «قطوط», like «حمل» and «حمول», and «قططة», like «قرد» and «قردة» and «قرود», and in the small-number plural «أقططة», like «قدح» and «أقدحة» and «أقداح». In al-Qāmūs: "«القط»: cutting in general, or crosswise, or cutting something hard like the reed-case, like «الاقتطاط»; and short, curly hair, like «القطط» with vowelling; «قد قطط» like «فرح»; and «قطّ يقط» like «يمل», «قططا» with vowelling, and «قطاطة». «القطّاط» is the turner, the maker of reed-cases", until he says: "«والقط» with kasra is the share, the deed, the book of accounts, its plural «قطوط»; and the cat, its plural «قطاط» and «قططه»; and the hour of the night." Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: «القط» is the book with gifts. Al-Aʿshā said:
ولا الملك النعمان يوم لقيته ... بغبطته يعطي القطوط ويأفق
(Nor was it King al-Nuʿmān on the day I met him in his prosperity, giving the deeds of grant and excelling.)

* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْحِسابِ) A resumptive statement introduced to relate types of their evasion and mockery after His words the Exalted «فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه» (the verse) were revealed. «قالُوا» is a verb and an agent; «رَبَّنا» is a vocative muḍāf with the vocative particle omitted; «عَجِّلْ» is an imperative verb; «لَنا» is attached to it, and its agent is a necessarily latent pronoun whose implied form is "You"; «قِطَّنا» is a direct object; «قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْحِسابِ» is an adverbial attached to «عَجِّلْ» also, or to an omitted ḥāl. (اصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ ذَا الْأَيْدِ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ) «اصْبِرْ» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; «عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ» is attached to «اصْبِرْ»; the clause «يَقُولُونَ» is a ṣila and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "they say it". «اذْكُرْ» is conjoined to «اصْبِرْ», meaning "take comfort in the story of Dāwūd and restrain yourself from neglecting the matter of persevering against them and bearing their harm, lest he become a target of what he was targeted for"; «عَبْدَنا» is a direct object, «داوُدَ» a badal, and «ذَا الْأَيْدِ» an adjective of «داوُدَ», meaning possessor of strength; the explanation of «الأيد» has preceded. The clause «إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ» gives the reason for his being among the possessors of strength, that is, one who returns to the pleasure of Allah; inna with its noun and its predicate.
(إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا الْجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِشْراقِ) Inna and its noun; the clause «سَخَّرْنَا الْجِبالَ», of verb, agent and object, is the khabar of «إِنَّا»; the clause «يُسَبِّحْنَ» is circumstantial from «الْجِبالَ». The secret of turning from «مسبحات» to «يسبحن» will come in the section on Rhetoric. «بِالْعَشِيِّ» is attached to «يُسَبِّحْنَ»; «الْإِشْراقِ» is conjoined to «بِالْعَشِيِّ», that is, morning and evening. The report of Ibn ʿAbbās about «العشي والإشراق» will also come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَالطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً كُلٌّ لَهُ أَوَّابٌ) «الطَّيْرَ» is conjoined to «الْجِبالَ», or is a direct object of an omitted verb indicated by what precedes, that is, "and We subjugated the birds"; «مَحْشُورَةً» is a ḥāl, that is, gathered, glorifying Him. «كُلٌّ» is a mubtadaʾ, for which it is acceptable to begin because of the sense of generality in it, that is, each of the mountains and the birds. «لَهُ» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أَوَّابٌ», and «أَوَّابٌ» is the khabar of «كُلٌّ», meaning one who returns often, an intensive of «آئب», that is, returning to Him with glorification. (وَشَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ وَآتَيْناهُ الْحِكْمَةَ وَفَصْلَ الْخِطابِ) «شَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ» is a verb, an agent and a direct object, that is, "We strengthened it with troops and guards"; «آتَيْناهُ» is a verb, an agent and a first direct object; «الْحِكْمَةَ» is a second direct object, and «فَصْلَ الْخِطابِ» is conjoined to «الْحِكْمَةَ»; the meaning of «فصل الخطاب» will come in the section on Rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
These verses embrace several arts that dazzle the listeners, and here is the detail.
1- Shifting from the nominal form to the verbal:
In His words «يسبحن» there is a shift from the noun to the verb, and the point in it is to indicate renewal and occurrence, one thing after another and one state after another, as though the listener were present in that state hearing their glorification. Like it is the verse of al-Aʿshā:
لعمري لقد لاحت عيون كثيرة ... إلى ضوء باليفاع تحرق
(By my life, many eyes have been drawn to the light of a fire burning on the height.) Had he said «محرقة» it would not have had that effect.
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq):
In His words «بالعشي والإشراق» there is a wonderful antithesis between the evening prayer and the forenoon prayer. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "I used to pass this verse «بالعشي والإشراق» and not know what it was, until Umm Hāniʾ told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon her and asked for water for ablution, performed ablution, then prayed the forenoon prayer and said: 'O Umm Hāniʾ, this is the prayer of the ishrāq.'" From Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās as well, he said: "Do you find mention of the forenoon (al-ḍuḥā) in the Qur'an?" They said: "No." So he recited: «إنا سخرنا الجبال معه يسبحن بالعشي والإشراق». And from him also: "I did not know the forenoon prayer except by this verse."
3- The meaning of «فصل الخطاب»:
«الفصل» is distinguishing between two things, and speech that is clear was called «فصل», in the passive sense (bi-maʿnā al-mafʿūl). Its origin is that they say «كلام ملتبس» (confused speech), and «في كلامه لبس» (there is confusion in his speech), and the confused is the mixed, which is not clear because of its entanglement or its complexity; so its opposite was called «كلام فصل», that is, part of it separated from part. Its summary is that one does not err in the places of joining and separating; so in the word of testimony one does not stop on the thing excepted from, and one does not recite His words «ويل للمصلين» except joined to what follows it, nor «والله يعلم وأنتم» until one joins it to «لا تعلمون», and the like. The same applies to the places of conjunction and its omission, pronoun and overt noun, mention and omission, repetition and other arts, most of which have passed you in this book. It is also possible that «الفصل» be in the active sense (bi-maʿnā al-fāʿil), that is, the one that separates truth from falsehood, sound from corrupt, and the fat from the lean.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words: ﴿صۤ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ﴾: the readers read it with sukūn (jazm), except al-Ḥasan, who gave it kasra (khafḍ) without nūn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It is then like the reading of whoever read ﴿نُونَ والقلم﴾ and ﴿ياسينَ والقرآنِ الحَكيم﴾ [with fatḥa]: it was treated like a particle (adāt), as in the Arabs' saying: taraktuhu (ḥāthi bāthi) and (khāzi bāzi), which take kasra, because what precedes the last letter is an alif. So the kasra goes with the alif, and the fatḥa with other than alif; they say: taraktuhu ḥaytha baytha, and la-ajʿalannaka ḥayṣa bayṣa, when one is put in straits.
The poet said:
* لم يَلتحِصنى حَيْصَ بَيْصَ الحاصى *
(The one who squeezes did not force me into a tight spot.)
He means al-ḥāʾiṣ, and metathesized it, just as he said (ʿāqi) meaning ʿāʾiq.
And Ṣād, in its meaning, is like your saying: / 161 ب "It is binding, by Allah", "It has come down, by Allah", "It is true, by Allah". So it is the answer to His words ﴿والقرآن﴾, as you say: "It has come down, by Allah". Some have claimed that the answer to ﴿والقرآن﴾ is ﴿إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تخاصُمُ أَهْلِ النارِ﴾; but that is speech that comes very far after His words ﴿والقرآن﴾, with various stories running between them, so we do not find that sound in Arabic. And Allah knows best.
And it is said: His words ﴿وَالقرآنِ﴾ are an oath, before whose answer a speech intervened, so its answer became an answer for both the intervening speech and the oath. It is as if He meant: "By the Qurʾān possessing the Reminder, how many We destroyed!" When His words intervened — ﴿بل الذين كَفَرُوا فى عِزَّة وشقاق﴾ — (كم) became the answer both to "the arrogance" and to the oath. Similar is His word ﴿والشَمسِ وضُحَاهَا﴾: before the answer His words intervened ﴿ونَفْسٍ وما سَوَّاها فألْهَمهَا﴾, so ﴿قد أفلح﴾ became dependent on His words ﴿فألهمها﴾ and sufficed as the answer to the oath; it is as if it were: "By the sun and its morning brightness, indeed he has succeeded."

farraa:3-3.t:
His words: ﴿فَنَادَواْ وَّلاَتَ حِينَ مَنَاصٍ﴾: He says: it was not a time for fleeing. al-nawṣ in the speech of the Arabs is drawing back, and al-bawṣ is going ahead; [one says:] buṣtuhu.
Imruʾ al-Qays said:
أمِن ذكر ليلى إذ نَأَتكَ تَنُوص * وتَقْصُر عَنْهَا خُطوةً وتَبُوص
(Is it from remembering Laylā, now that she is far from you, that you draw back, falling short of her by a step and pushing forward?)
So manāṣ is of the pattern mafʿal, like maqām. Some Arabs put lāta in iḍāfa and so use the genitive. They recited to me:
* ... لات ساعةِ مَنْدَمِ *
(… it was not an hour for regret)
and I do not remember the first half of the verse. The normal usage is to make [the following noun] accusative with it, because it is in the sense of laysa. Al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
تذكّرَ حبّ ليلى لاَتَ حينا * وأضحَى الشيب قد قطعَ القرينَا
(He remembered his love for Laylā when it was no time for it, and grey hair had already cut the bond.)
This is the accusative. And someone recited to me:
طلبوا صُلحنا ولاَتَ أوانِ * فأجبنَا أن لَيْسَ حِينَ بقَاءِ
(They sought peace with us when it was no time for it, so we answered that it was not a time for sparing.)
He put (أَوانِ) in the genitive; this is the genitive.
Al-Farrāʾ said: I pause on (لاتَ) with tāʾ, while al-Kisāʾī pauses with hāʾ.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words: ﴿لَشَيْءٌ عُجَابٌ﴾: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (لشىء عُجَّابٌ). The Arabs say: hādhā rajulun karīmun, kurrāmun and kurāmun, and the meaning is all one. Similar are His words, the Exalted, ﴿وَمَكَرُوا مَكراً كُبَّاراً﴾, whose meaning is kabīran ("great"), and He doubled it. The poet said:
كحلفة من أبى رياح * يسمعها الهِمّةُ الكُبار
(Like an oath of Abū Riyāḥ, which the very old man hears.)
al-himm and al-himma are the decrepit old man.
Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
* يسمعها الله والله كبار *
(Allah hears it, and Allah is the Great.)
Another said:
وآثرت إدلاجى عَلى ليل حُرَّة * هَضيم الحَشَا حُسّانِة المَتجرَّد
(I preferred travelling by night over a night with a noble woman, slender of waist, very beautiful when unclad.)
Another said:
نحن بذلنا دونها الضِّرابَا * إنا وجدنا ماءها طُيّابَا
(We gave blows in defence of it; we found its water very good.)
He means ṭayyib. And he said of "tall" (ṭawīl): ṭuwāl al-sāʿidayn ashamm:
* طُوال الساعدين أشمّ *
(Long of forearms, proud of nose.)
Another said:
جاء بصيد عَجَب من العجب * أزيرق العينين طُوَّالِ الذَنَبْ
(He brought a wonder of a catch: blue-eyed, with a very long tail.)
So he doubled the wāw along the same pattern. Every adjective with which you describe a noun, masculine or feminine, that comes to you on the pattern fuʿʿāl, doubled or undoubled, is correct.

farraa:6-6.t: His words: ﴿وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلْمَلأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ ٱمْشُواْ﴾: they went off with this speech. So an is in the position of an accusative (naṣb) because it lacks the preposition [accusative by removal of the preposition]. It is as if you said: they went off, walking and going on 162 ا in your religion. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (وانطلق الملأ منهم يمشون أن اصبروا عَلى آلهتكم). And had (أن) not been there, it would have been correct, as He said ﴿والمَلاَئِكةُ باسِطُوا أيْدِيهِمْ أَخْرِجُوا﴾ and did not say "an akhrijū", because "saying" is implied in the intention.

farraa:7-7.t: His words: ﴿مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَـٰذَا فِى ٱلْمِلَّةِ ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾: He means Judaism and Christianity.

farraa:8-8.t: His words: ﴿أَأُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلذِّكْرُ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (أَمْ أنزِلَ عليه الذكر). This is part of what I described to you at the beginning of the book: that the question, when it comes in the middle of speech, is begun with the alif or with am; and when no speech precedes it, it is only with the alif or with hal.

farraa:10-10.t: His words: ﴿فَلْيَرْتَقُواْ فِى ٱلأَسْبَابِ﴾: He means: let them climb up in the heavens — and they are not able to do that; i.e. they did not believe you, and they are not able to climb up to the heavens, so what are they [worth]! Where then are they going?

farraa:11-11.t:
His words: ﴿جُندٌ مَّا هُنَالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِّن ٱلأَحَزَابِ﴾: He says: defeated, unable to ascend to the heaven. And (مَا) here is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant). The Arabs make (ما) a ṣila in places where its presence and absence are the same, and this is one of them.
His words ﴿عَمَّا قليلٍ لَيُصْبِحُنَّ نَادِمِينَ﴾ are of that kind.
And His words ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثَاقَهُمْ﴾ are of that kind, because its presence and absence do not change the meaning.
As for His words ﴿إِلاَّ الذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصَّالحَاتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَا هُمْ﴾, it may be in this sense.
It may also be that you make (ما) a noun and make (هم) the ṣila (relative clause) of mā; the meaning would then be: "and how few you will find them", so you direct (mā) and the noun toward the maṣdar (verbal noun). Do you not see that you say: qad kuntu arāka aʿqala mimmā anta ("I used to think you more intelligent than you are"), making (anta) the ṣila of mā; the meaning is: I used to think your intelligence greater than it is. Had you not meant the maṣdar, you would not use (mā) for people, because man is what is used for people and their like. The Arabs say: qad kuntu arāka aʿqala minka, and the meaning of the two is the same. Likewise their saying: qad kuntu arāhu ghayra mā huwa; the meaning is: I used to think him other than what I [then] saw of him.

farraa:14-14.t: His words: ﴿إِن كُلٌّ إِلاَّ كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (إِنْ كُلُّهُمْ لَمَّا كَذَّبَ الرُسُلَ).

farraa:15-15.t: His words: ﴿مَّا لَهَا مِن فَوَاقٍ﴾: [there is for it] no rest and no respite. Its origin is from ifāqa in suckling: when the young animal sucks its mother and then leaves her until she lets down some milk — that is the ifāqa, and fuwāq is without hamza. It has come from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Visiting the sick is the length of a fuwāq of a she-camel." Al-Ḥasan, the people of Medina and ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd read it (فَوَاق) with fatḥa, and it is a good and high dialect; while Ḥamza, Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī gave it ḍamma.

farraa:16-16.t: His words: ﴿عَجِّل لَّنَا قِطَّنَا﴾: al-qiṭṭ is the written sheet. They only said that when ﴿فأَمَّا مَنْ أُوُتِىَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ﴾ was revealed; they mocked it and said: "Hasten this record to us before the Day of Reckoning." And al-qiṭṭ in the speech of the Arabs is the deed (ṣakk), that is, writing and a document.

farraa:17-17.t: His words: ﴿ذَا ٱلأَيْدِ﴾: He means: possessor of strength.

farraa:19-19.t:
His words: ﴿وَٱلطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً﴾: They mentioned that whenever he glorified [Allah], the mountains answered him with glorification, and the birds gathered to him and glorified; that is their being gathered. Had it been wa-l-ṭayru maḥshūratun, in the nominative, since the verb does not appear with it, it would have been correct. It would be like His words ﴿خَتَم اللهُ عَلى قلُوبِهِمْ وعَلى سَمْعِهِمْ وعَلَى أبصارِهم غِشَاوَةٌ﴾. The poet said:
ورأيتُمُ لمجاشعٍ نَعَماً * وبنى أبيه جَامل رُغُب
(And you saw that Mujāshiʿ had cattle, and that his father's sons had a herd of camels, greedy grazers.)
He did not say jāmilan rughuban; the meaning is: and you saw that they had a herd of greedy camels. Since the verb did not appear, its nominative was permissible.

farraa:20-20.t:
His words: ﴿وَشَدَدْنَا مُلْكَهُ﴾: the readers agree on reading it without doubling; had a reader read ﴿وشَدَّدْنا﴾ with doubling it would be a good option. The meaning of the strengthening is that his sanctuary used to be guarded by thirty-three thousand.
His words: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ ٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَفَصْلَ ٱلْخِطَابِ﴾: al-Farrāʾ said: ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām related to me from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ ٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَفَصْلَ ٱلْخِطَابِ﴾; he said: witnesses and oaths. Some commentators said: faṣl al-khiṭāb is "ammā baʿd".

farraa:21-22.t:
His words: ﴿إِذْ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلْمِحْرَابَ﴾ ﴿إِذْ دَخَلُواْ﴾: idh may be used twice, (and) their meaning may be as one; as when you say: "I struck you when you came in upon me, when you were insolent", so the coming in is itself the insolence. It may also be that you take one of them in the way of lammā, as if He said: ﴿إذ تسَوَّرُوا المحرابَ لَمَّا دَخَلوا﴾. If you wish, you may make lammā the first. When lammā is first or last, it is after its companion [in time]; as you say: "I gave to him when he asked me" — the asking is before the giving whether it comes first or last.
His words: ﴿خَصْمَانِ﴾: you make it nominative by implying (نحن خصْمَان) ("we are two disputants"). The Arabs imply, for the speaker and for the one addressed, what makes the predicate nominative, and they hardly ever do that for anyone other than the addressee or the speaker. Of that is your saying to a man: "Going?", or the speaker saying: "Keeping in touch with you, if Allah wills, and doing good to you." That is because the speaker and the one addressed are present, so the meaning of their nouns is known when they are left out. It is most frequent in questions; they say: "Serious?", "Leaving?". It may also be outside questions; and His words (خَصْمَان) are of this kind. The poet said:
وَقولا إذا جاوزتمَا أرض عَامرٍ * وجاوزتما الحيَّيْنِ نَهداً وخَثْعما
نَزيعَانِ من جَرْم بن زَبَّان إنهم * أبوا أن يميرُوا فى الهزاهز مِحْجَما
(And say, when you two have passed the land of ʿĀmir and passed the two tribes, Nahd and Khathʿam: "[We are] two strangers from Jarm ibn Zabbān; they refused to supply even a cupping-glass's worth in times of upheaval.")
Another said:
تقول ابنَة الكَعبىّ يوم لقيتُها * أمُنْطلق فى الجيش أم متثاقِلُ
(The daughter of al-Kaʿbī said on the day I met her: "Setting out with the army, or lagging behind?")
And it has come in the traditions for one returning from a journey: "Repenting, returning, praising our Lord." And he said: among the proverbs of the Arabs is: "Doing good, so pour (muḥsinatun fa-hīlī)!"
Al-Farrāʾ said: A guest came to a woman with a bag of flour, and she began taking from his bag for herself; when he turned toward her, she took from her bag into his bag. He said: "What are you doing?" She said: "I am adding to you from my flour." He said: "Doing good, so pour", i.e. throw [it in]. And it has come in the traditions: "Whoever helps in killing a believer with half a word will come on the Day of Resurrection with written between his eyes: 'Despairing of the mercy of Allah.'" All of this is by implying what I have told you of.
Had it come in the Book: khaṣmayni baghā baʿḍunā, it would have been correct, by implying "we have come to you as two disputants", "we have come to you as two disputants, so do not fear us". Similar is the poet's saying:
وقالت أَلا يا اسمع نِعظك بخُطَّةٍ * فقلت سَميعاً فانطقى وأَصيبى
(She said: "Listen, we will admonish you with a plan", and I said: "[I am] listening — so speak and be right.")
163 ا i.e. "listening, I hear from you", or "listening [to what] you admonished". The nominative is permissible in it on the first explanations.
His words ﴿وَلاَ تُشْطِطْ﴾: He says: and do not be unjust. Some Arabs say: shaṭaṭta ʿalayya fī al-sawm ("you were excessive with me in bargaining"), but more common is ashṭaṭta. Had a reader read ﴿وَلاَ تَشْطِطْ﴾, it is as if he takes it in the sense of going far, and also ﴿تَشْطُطْ﴾. The Arabs say: shaṭṭat al-dār ("the dwelling became distant"), fa-hiya tashiṭṭu and tashuṭṭu.
His words ﴿وَٱهْدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ﴾: to the middle of the path. This is one of those [verbs] in which (ilā) may be included or omitted.
Allah said ﴿اهدِنَا الصراطَ المستقيم﴾, and He said ﴿وهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾, and He said ﴿إنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ﴾, and did not say (إلى); so ilā was omitted from all of these. Then He said in another place ﴿أَفَمَنْ يَهْدِى إلى الحَقّ﴾, and He said ﴿يَهْدِى إلىَ الحَقِّ وَإلى طَرِيقٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾. One also says: hadaytuka li-l-ḥaqq and ilayhi; Allah said ﴿الذِى هَدَانَا لِهَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لنَهْتَدِى﴾. It is as if His saying ﴿اهدنَا الصراط﴾ means "make the path known to us", and His saying ﴿اهدنا إلى الصّراط﴾ means "guide us to it". And Allah knows best about that.

farraa:23-23.t:
His words: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَآ أَخِي لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (كَانَ لَهُ). The Arabs sometimes put (kāna) on a permanent predicate that does not come to an end. Of this is Allah's word in more than one place ﴿وكان رَبُّك قديراً﴾ ﴿وكان الله غفوراً رحيماً﴾ — this is permanent. The clear meaning is to put (kāna) on every predicate that was and then ceased; as you say to a man: "You were well-off", and the meaning of this is: "you are now destitute".
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (نَعْجَةً أُنْثَى) ("a female ewe"). The Arabs emphasize the feminine with unthā, and the masculine likewise, so it is like a surplus in speech; this is of that kind. Of it is your saying of a man: "This, by Allah, is a male man." This enters only with a feminine whose femininity is in itself, like the woman and the man, the camel and the she-camel. If you go beyond that it is not permissible; so it is wrong to say: "this is a female house" or "a female wrap", because their femininity is in their name, not in their meaning. Build on this.
His words ﴿وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلْخِطَابِ﴾, i.e. he overcame me. Had it been read ﴿وَعَازَّنى﴾, meaning "he contended with me to overcome me", it would have been an acceptable option.

farraa:24-24.t:
His words: ﴿لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِ﴾: the meaning in it is: by his asking [for] your ewe; when you drop the hāʾ [the pronoun] from "asking", you attach the verbal noun (fiʿl) in iḍāfa to the ewe. Similar are His words ﴿لاَ يَسْأَمُ الإنْسَانُ مِنْ دعَاءِ الخَيْرِ﴾, whose meaning is: of his praying for good; when He dropped the hāʾ, He attached the verbal noun in iḍāfa to "the good" and dropped the bāʾ from "the good", as the poet says:
ولَسْتُ مُسَلِّماً ما دمتُ حَيّاً * عَلى زيدٍ بتَسليم الأمِير
(As long as I live I will not greet Zayd with the greeting [due to] the commander.)
Its meaning is only: with my greeting of the commander. It is not acceptable to mention the agent after the object in cases where you have dropped the preposition (ṣifa) from it. Whoever says: ʿajibtu min suʾāli naʿjataka ṣāḥibuka ("I marvelled at your companion's asking for your ewe") may not say: ʿajibtu min duʿāʾi al-khayri al-nāsu, because when you bring out the latter [noun] in the nominative, you make it nominative only with the intention of an faʿala or an yafʿalu, so the bāʾ and similar prepositions must appear. So the way to say that is: ʿajibtu min duʿāʾin bi-l-khayri Zaydun, and ʿajibtu min taslīmin ʿalā al-amīri Zaydun. It was permissible with the ewe because the verb falls upon it without a preposition: you say saʾaltuka naʿjatan, and you do not say saʾaltuka bi-naʿjatin. Build on this.
His words ﴿وَظَنَّ دَاوُودُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّاهُ﴾, i.e. he knew. Every ẓann that you put on a predicate may be made [to mean] knowledge, except that it is knowledge 163 ب of what is not seen with the eye.

farraa:31-31.t: His words: ﴿ٱلصَّافِنَاتُ ٱلْجِيَادُ﴾: He means the horses which Solomon son of David had taken as booty from an army that fought him, and he defeated it. When he had prayed the noon prayer he called for them, and he kept reviewing them until the sun set, and he did not pray the afternoon prayer. He was held in awe among them; nothing would be started until he ordered it, so they did not mention the afternoon prayer [to him]. That was not out of arrogance on his part. When he remembered it he said ﴿إنَّى أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الخَيْرِ﴾; he says: I preferred love of horses — and al-khayr in the speech of the Arabs is horses (al-khayl). And al-ṣāfināt — according to what al-Kalbī mentioned with his chain of transmission — are those standing on three legs, having set the other one on the edge of the hoof, whether a foreleg or a hind leg. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (صَوَافِنَ فإذَا وَجَبَتْ), meaning: hobbled on three. I have seen the Arabs apply al-ṣāfin to one standing otherwise than on three, and their poems indicate that it is standing specifically; and Allah knows best what is correct. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (إنّى أحببت) without (قال) ("he said"). Similar, among cases where "saying" is omitted in our reading and present in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, is ﴿وَإِذْ يَرْفَع إِبراهيمُ القَوَاعِدَ مِنَ البَيْتَ وإسْمَاعِيلُ ويَقُولاَنِ﴾, which is not so in our reading. And all is correct.

farraa:33-33.t: His words: ﴿فَطَفِقَ﴾: He means: he began wiping, i.e. striking their legs and necks. So the wiping is cutting.

farraa:34-34.t: His words: ﴿عَلَىٰ كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَداً﴾: He means an idol. And it is said: a devil.

farraa:35-35.t: His words: ﴿لاَّ يَنبَغِي لأَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِيۤ﴾: He means the subjection of the wind and the devils.

farraa:36-36.t: His words: ﴿رُخَآءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ﴾: al-rukhāʾ is the gentle wind that does not blow violently. His words ﴿حَيْثُ أَصَابَ﴾: wherever he wished.

farraa:39-39.t:
His words: ﴿هَـٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا فَٱمْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾.
He says: bestow it, i.e. give, or withhold — that is up to you. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (هذا فامنن أو أمسك عطاؤنا بغير حساب), with transposition (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr).

farraa:41-41.t:
His words: ﴿بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ﴾.
The readers agree on ḍamma on the nūn of (نُصبٍ) with the ṣād unvowelled. They mentioned that Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read (بنَصَبٍ وعذابٍ), with fatḥa on the nūn and the ṣād. Both are the same in the commentary.
They mentioned that it is the illness and the hardship that befell him in it. al-nuṣb and al-naṣab are like al-ḥuzn and al-ḥazan, al-ʿudm and al-ʿadam, al-rushd and al-rashad, al-ṣulb and al-ṣalab: when it is light, its first letter takes ḍamma and is not made heavy, because they put them in two patterns: when they gave the first letter fatḥa they made it heavy [vowelling the second], and when they gave the first letter ḍamma they made it light. He said: and one of the Arabs recited to me:
لئِن بعثت أم الحُميدَينِ مَائِرا * لقد غنِيت فى غير بؤسٍ ولا جُحْد
(If the mother of the two Ḥumayds has sent someone to fetch provisions, she has lived in no misery and no hardship.)
The Arabs say: jaḥida ʿayshuhum jaḥadan when it becomes straitened and hard; when he said juḥd with ḍamma on the first letter, he made it light. So build on what you have seen of these two dialect forms.

farraa:44-44.t: His words: ﴿ضِغْثاً﴾: al-ḍighth is whatever you gather of something, like a bundle of fresh fodder; whatever stands on a stalk and grows tall, and you then gather it, is a ḍighth.

farraa:45-45.t:
His words: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ عِبَادَنَآ﴾: the readers read ﴿عِبَادَنَا﴾, meaning Abraham and his offspring. Ibn ʿAbbās read: (واذكرعَبْدَنا إبراهيم) and said: Only Abraham was mentioned, then his offspring were mentioned after him. Similar is ﴿قالُوا نَعْبُدُ إلهَكَ وإِلهَ أبِيك﴾ on this approach, in the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, while the majority read ﴿آبائِكَ﴾; and all is correct.
His words ﴿أُوْلِي ٱلأَيْدِي وَٱلأَبْصَارِ﴾: He means: possessors of strength and insight in Allah's affair. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (أولِى الأيْدِ) without yāʾ, which may have two explanations. If he meant al-aydī and dropped the yāʾ, it is correct, like ﴿الجوَارِ﴾ and ﴿المُنادِ﴾ and the like. And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it may be from strength, from taʾyīd ("strengthening").

farraa:46-46.t:
His words: ﴿إِنَّآ أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى ٱلدَّارِ﴾: He made ﴿ذِكْرَى ٱلدَّارِ﴾, which is definite, refer back to (خَالِصَةٍ), which is indefinite [as a badal (substitute)]. It is like the reading of Masrūq (بِزِينةٍ الكواكب). Similar are / 164 ا His words ﴿هَذَا وإنَّ لِلطَّاغين لشَرَّ مَآبٍ جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا﴾, where He made "Jahannam", which is definite, refer back to ﴿شرّ مآبٍ﴾, which is indefinite. Likewise His words: ﴿وإنّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مآبٍ جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُفَتَّحة﴾. The nominative is permissible in all the definite nouns, as a mubtadaʾ (subject). One of the Arabs recited to me:
لعمرك مانخلى بدارِ مَضِيعَةٍ * وَلاَ ربُّهَا إن غاب عَنْهَا بخائف
وإن لها جارين لن يغدِرا بهَا * رَبِيبُ النَّبِىِّ وابنُ خير الخلائف
(By your life, my palm-grove is not in a place of neglect, nor does its owner, if absent from it, have cause to fear; it has two neighbours who will never betray it: the Prophet's stepson and the son of the best of caliphs.)
He made it nominative as a subject.
The people of the Ḥijāz read (بخالصَةِ ذِكْرَى الدار), putting it in iḍāfa, and that is a good option. Of it is: ﴿كَذَلكَ يَطْبَعُ اللهُ على كُلّ قَلْب مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبّارٍ﴾; and whoever says ﴿قلبٍ متكبّرٍ﴾ makes the heart itself the arrogant one.

farraa:48-48.t:
His words: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَٱلْيَسَعَ﴾: the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it with doubling [wa-l-layasaʿa]. The common people read ﴿الْيَسَعَ﴾ without doubling. The first is closer to being correct and to the names of the prophets of the Children of Israel. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Taymī related to me from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, that he read (واللَّيْسَع) with doubling. As for their saying ﴿والْيَسَع﴾: the Arabs do not put the alif and lām on [a name of the form] yafʿalu when it is in the sense of a proper name. They say: hādhā Yasaʿ, hādhā Yaʿmar, hādhā Yazīd. So this is the eloquent form of speech. But someone recited to me:
وجدنا الوليد بن اليزيد مباركاً * شديداً بأَحناء الخِلاَفة كَاهلُهْ
(We found al-Walīd son of al-Yazīd blessed, his shoulders strong under the burdens of the caliphate.)
When he mentioned al-Walīd at the beginning of the verse with alif and lām, he made Yazīd follow it with alif and lām. And all is correct.
His words ﴿وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ﴾: it is said that he was called Dhū al-Kifl because a hundred of the Children of Israel escaped from being killed, and he gave them refuge and took charge of them (kafalahum). And it is said that he pledged something to Allah and fulfilled it. al-kifl in the speech of the Arabs is fortune and lot; had he been praised by that, it would be a [third] option, other than the first two.

farraa:50-50.t:
His words: ﴿جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُّفَتَّحَةً لَّهُمُ ٱلأَبْوَابُ﴾: You make ﴿الأبواب﴾ nominative because the meaning is: "opened for them, their gates". The Arabs make the alif and lām a substitute for the iḍāfa (genitive construct), so they say: marartu ʿalā rajulin ḥasanatin al-ʿaynu qabīḥin al-anfu, the meaning being: his eye beautiful, his nose ugly. Of this is His word ﴿فَإِنّ الجَحيمَ هِىَ المَأْوَى﴾; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: his refuge. Similar is the poet's saying:
ما ولدتكم حيَّةُ بنة مالك * سِفَاحاً ومَا كانتْ أحاديث كاذب
ولكن نرى أقدامنا فى نعالكم * وآنفُنَا بين اللحى والحواجب
(Ḥayya daughter of Mālik did not bear you in fornication, nor were [the reports] a liar's tales; rather, we see our feet in your sandals and our noses between the beards and the eyebrows.)
Its meaning is: we see our noses between your beards and your eyebrows, in resemblance. And had He said ﴿مُّفَتَّحَةً لَّهُمُ ٱلأَبْوَابَ﴾ [in the accusative], making "opened" in wording belong to the gardens and in meaning to the gates, it would be like the poet's saying:
ومَا قومى بثعلبة بن سَعْدٍ * ولا بفزارة الشُعْر الرقابَا
(My people are not Thaʿlaba ibn Saʿd, nor Fazāra, hairy of necks.)
and [it is also read] al-shuʿrā riqāban; it is also transmitted: al-shuʿri al-riqābā.
And ʿAdī said:
مِن ولىٍّ أوْ أخى ثِقَةٍ * والبعيد الشاحِط الدّارا
(Whether a close friend, or a trustworthy brother, or the distant one whose dwelling is far.)
Likewise you take the meaning of "the gates" in its accusative, as if you meant: "opened of gates (mufattaḥata al-abwābi)", then you gave it tanwīn and so put [the gates] in the accusative.
The verse of al-Nābigha is recited:
ونأخذ بعده بذُناب دَهرٍ * أجَبَّ الظهرَ ليسَ له سَنَامُ
(And after him we will hold on to the tail end of a time, flat of back, having no hump.)
and also ajabbi al-ẓahri.

farraa:52-52.t:
/ 164 ب His words: ﴿وَعِندَهُمْ قَاصِرَاتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ أَتْرَابٌ﴾ is nominative because ﴿قاصرات﴾ is indefinite, even though it is in iḍāfa to a definite noun; do you not see that the alif and lām are good in it, as the poet says:
من القاصرات الطَرْفِ لو دَبّ مُحْوِل * من الذَرّ فوق الإتْب منها لأثَّرا
(One of those of restrained glance: if a year-old ant were to crawl over her shift, it would leave a mark.)
(al-itb is the waist-wrapper.) When the alif and lām are good in a case like this and you then drop them, the noun is indefinite. Sometimes the Arabs liken its wording to a definite noun because it is in iḍāfa to [a noun with] alif and lām, and so they put its adjective in the accusative when it is indefinite; they say: hādhā ḥasanu al-wajhi qāʾiman wa-dhāhiban. If you put in place of "going" and "standing" an indefinite word containing praise or blame, you would prefer agreement (itbāʿ), and say: hādhā ḥasanu al-wajhi mūsirun, because wealth is praise. Similar is the poet's saying:
ومَن يُشوِه يوم فإن وراءه * تِبَاعة صَيّاد الرّجالِ غَشُومِ
(Whoever is struck by a day [of misfortune], behind him is the pursuit of a hunter of men, unjust.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: (wa-man yushwihi) means: [whoever] takes his choicest parts and best portions. He put "unjust" (al-ghashūm) in the genitive because it is praise; and had it been accusative, since its wording is indefinite while the wording of what it describes is definite, it would have been correct; as they said: hādhā mithluka qāʾiman, and mithluka jamīlan.

farraa:57-57.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ﴾: you make "scalding water" (al-ḥamīm) and "pus" (al-ghassāq) nominative by hādhā, placed before or after. The meaning is: "This is scalding water and pus, so let them taste it." If you wish, you may make it a fresh start (mustaʾnaf), and make the speech before it self-sufficient; as if you said: "This — let them taste it", then said: "Of it is scalding water and of it is pus"; as the poet says:
حَتّى إذا مَا أضَاء الصُّبحُ فى غَلَسٍ * وغودر البقلُ مَلْوِىّ ومحصودُ
(Until, when the dawn shone in the last darkness, and the herbage was left [some of it] withered and [some] cut.)
And (هذا) may be in the position of a nominative or of an accusative. Whoever makes it accusative implies before it something that governs the accusative, as the poet says:
زيادتَنا نُعمان لا تَحْرِمَنَّهـَا * تَقِ اللهَ فينَا والكتابَ الذى تتلو
(Our increase, Nuʿmān — do not deny it to us; fear Allah regarding us, and the Book that you recite.)
And whoever makes it nominative makes it nominative by the hāʾ in His words ﴿فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ﴾, as you say in speech: al-layla fa-bādirūhu and al-laylu ("the night — hasten to [use] it").
al-Ghassāq: its sīn is pronounced doubled and undoubled. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and the generality of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh doubled it, and the people afterwards read it undoubled. They mentioned that al-ghassāq is a cold that burns as the scalding water burns. And it is said that it is what oozes (yaghsiqu) and flows from their pus and their skins.

farraa:58-58.t: His words: ﴿وَآخَرُ مِن شَكْلِهِ أَزْوَاجٌ﴾: the people read (وَآخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ), except Mujāhid, who read (وَأُخَرُ) [plural], as if he thought that "kinds" (azwāj) could not be [the predicate] of a single described thing. But when the noun is a verbal noun (fiʿl), it may be described with two and with many; as you say in speech: "So-and-so's punishment is various kinds" and "two different kinds". This is clear. And if you wish, you may make "kinds" an adjective (naʿt) of the scalding water, the pus and "another", so they are three; but making it a description of one is closer. What Mujāhid said is permissible, but I do not favour it, in order to follow the majority and because of its clarity in Arabic.

farraa:59-59.t:
His words: ﴿هَـٰذَا فَوْجٌ مُّقْتَحِمٌ مَّعَكُمْ﴾: it is one community entering the Fire after another community.
Then He said: ﴿لاَ مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ﴾. The speech is connected, as if it were one person's speech, but His words ﴿لاَ مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ﴾ are only from the speech of the people of the Fire. It is like His word: ﴿كُلَّمَا دَخَلَتْ أُمَّةٌ لعَنَتْ أُخْتَهَا﴾. In its connectedness it is like His words: ﴿يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُم بسحره فمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾, where Pharaoh's speech was connected to the speech of his companions.

farraa:61-61.t: His words: ﴿قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا مَن قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا﴾: its meaning is: whoever laid it down for us and made it a practice, ﴿فَزِدْهُ عَذَاباً ضِعْفاً فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾.

farraa:63-63.t: His words: ﴿أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سِخْرِيّاً﴾: Zuhayr said from Abān, from Mujāhid — al-Farrāʾ said: and I did not hear it from Zuhayr — ﴿اتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سخريّاً﴾ ("we took them as a laughing-stock"), while they were not so. The companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it without the interrogative, while al-Ḥasan, ʿĀṣim and the people of Medina used the interrogative. It is of the kind of question whose meaning is wonder and rebuke, so it is permissible with the interrogative and without it.

farraa:70-70.t:
His words: ﴿إِن يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ إِلاَّ أَنَّمَآ أَنَاْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾: If you wish, you may put (أنّما) in the position of a nominative, as if you said: "nothing is revealed to me but the warning". And if you wish, you may make the meaning: "it is revealed to me only because I am a warner and a prophet"; when you drop the lām, the position of (أَنَّما) is accusative. In this place it could also be: "nothing is revealed to me except that you are a clear warner", because the meaning is reported speech (ḥikāya), as you say in speech: "They told me that I am an evildoer" and "He told me that you are an evildoer". It is like his saying:
رَجْلاَن من ضَبّةَ أخبرانَا * أنّا رأَينا رجلاُ عُرْيانَا
(Two men of Ḍabba told us: "We saw a naked man.")
the meaning being: they told us that they had seen; this was permissible because its origin is reported speech.
His words: ﴿بِيَدَيَّ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ﴾: the readers agree on the dual. Had a reader read ﴿بيدِى﴾, meaning a single hand, it would have been correct [Translator's note: the source prints «صَداباً», a misprint for «صواباً» "correct"]; as the poet says:
أيها المبتغى فناء قريشٍ * بيد الله عُمرهَا والفناء
(O you who seek the destruction of Quraysh: in the hand of Allah are its life and its destruction.)
The single one of these suffices for the two; likewise the two eyes, the two legs and the two hands: one of them suffices for the other, because their meaning is one.

farraa:84-84.t:
His words: ﴿قَالَ فَٱلْحَقُّ وَٱلْحَقَّ أَقُولُ﴾: al-Ḥasan and the people of the Ḥijāz read the accusative in both. Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim — and greater than them, Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid — read the nominative in the first and the accusative in the second.
Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Bihrām related to me — he was an elder who taught the Qurʾān in the Mosque of al-Maṭmūra and the Mosque of the Shaʿbīs — from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Mujāhid, that he read (فالحقُّ منى والحقَّ أقولُ) ("the truth is from Me, and the truth I say"), i.e. "and I say the truth". That is one option; and its nominative may be by implying: "so it is the truth".
It is mentioned of Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "I am the Truth, and I say the truth." Its nominative may also be by interpreting [what follows] as its answer, because the Arabs say: al-ḥaqqu la-aqūmanna ("the truth is, I will certainly stand"), and they say: ʿazmatun ṣādiqatun la-ātiyannaka ("a firm resolve: I will certainly come to you"), because it bears the interpretation: "a firm resolve that I will come to you".
This is made clear by His words: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ﴾; do you not see that His words ﴿بَدَا لَهُمْ﴾ must have an implied nominative, so in meaning it may be nominative or accusative. The Arabs recite the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فقلتُ يَمينُ الله أبرحُ قاعداً * ولو قطَّعوا رَأْسِى لديكَ وَأوصَالى
(I said: "By the oath of Allah, I will not cease sitting here, even if they cut off my head and my limbs beside you.")
The accusative in yamīn is more frequent. The nominative is on what I have told you about implying (an), and on your saying: ʿalayya yamīnun ("an oath is upon me"). They recited to us:
فإنّ علىّ اللهَ إنْ يحملوننى * عَلَى خُطّة إلا انطلقت أَسيرها
(For I owe it to Allah: if they put me to some plan, I will set out and carry it through.)
and it is also transmitted: lā yaḥmilūnanī.
If you dropped inna, you would say: ʿalayya Allāhu la-aḍribannaka, i.e. this oath is upon me. And it may be: ʿalayya Allāhu an aḍribaka, making (Allāh) nominative by the answer. Making it nominative by ʿalā is dearer to me. Whoever makes (al-ḥaqqa wa-l-ḥaqqa) accusative does so in the sense of your saying: ḥaqqan la-ātiyannaka ("truly, I will come to you"); the alif and lām and their omission are the same. It is like your saying ḥamdan li-llāh and al-ḥamda li-llāh. And had someone put the first al-ḥaqq in the genitive, making it Allah the Exalted — I mean in the i'rab — and swearing by it, it would have been correct. The Arabs drop the wāw of the oath and keep the genitive; we have heard them say: Allāhi la-tafʿalanna ("By Allah, you will certainly do [it]"), and / 165 ب the one answering says: Allāhi la-afʿalanna ("By Allah, I will certainly do [it]"), because the meaning is in common use, and in what is commonly used omission is permitted; as one says to a man: "How are you this morning?" and he says: "khayrin" ("well"), meaning bi-khayrin; since it was frequent in speech, [the preposition] was omitted.

farraa:88-88.t:
His words: ﴿وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ﴾: the tidings of the Qurʾān, that it is true, and the tidings of Muḥammad ﷺ, that he is a prophet.
His words: ﴿بَعْدَ حِينِ﴾: He says: after death, and before it: when the matter became manifest they knew it, and whoever died knew it with certainty.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; «القرآن» is the thing sworn by, and the preposition [phrase] is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb «أقسم» ("I swear"). «ذي»: naʿt (adjective) of «القرآن». The answer to the oath is implied, i.e.: you are indeed among the messengers.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: (بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «كم» is predicative (khabariyya), mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The preposition «من قرن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كم». The clause «فنادوا» is conjoined to the clause «أهلكنا». «لات» is a negating particle acting like «ليس»; its noun, «الحين», is omitted, and «حينَ» is its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «أن» is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition (من), i.e.: and they wondered at the coming. The clause «وعجبوا» is conjoined to the clause «نادوا». The clause «جاءهم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī). The clause «وقال الكافرون» is conjoined to the clause «عجبوا».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «أجعل» is resumptive within the scope of the speech; «إلها» is a second object. The clause «إن هذا لشيء» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «وانطلق الملأ» is conjoined to the clause «قال» in verse (4). The preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الملأ». «أن» is explicative (mufassira), and the clause after it is explicative; what is meant by "setting off" is the setting off of their tongues with this speech. The clause «إن هذا لشيء» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «ما سمعنا» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إن هذا ...»; «إنْ» is the negating one, and «إلا» is for restriction.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition «من بيننا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «عليه». The clause «بل هم في شك» is resumptive. The preposition «من ذكري» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «شك». «لما» is jussive-making; «عذاب» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ. The clause «لما يذوقوا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «العزيز الوهاب»: two naʿts (adjectives). «أم» is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning «بل» plus the hamza.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «أم» is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) one. «ما»: a relative noun conjoined to «السماوات». The adverb «بينهما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause). The clause «فليرتقوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they claim that, then let them ascend; the lām is the jussive-making lām of command.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «جند»: khabar (predicate) of a concealed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: they are a host. «ما» is added (redundant). «هنالك»: a demonstrative, an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «جند». «مهزوم»: a second naʿt of «جند». The preposition «من الأحزاب» is attached to a third naʿt of «جند».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «إنْ» is negating, «كل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «كذَّب» is the khabar (predicate). The clause «فحق عقاب» is conjoined to the clause «كذَّب»; «عقاب» is the fāʿil (agent), nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the omitted yāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «وما ينظر هؤلاء» is conjoined to the clause {إِنْ كُلٌّ إِلا كَذَّبَ}. «صيحة»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «ما لها من فواق» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «صيحة»; «فواق» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «وقالوا» is resumptive. «ربنا»: the one addressed, in a construct (munādā muḍāf), accusative. «قبل»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عجّل».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «ما» is maṣdar-forming. «داود»: badal (substitute). «ذا»: naʿt (adjective), interpreted as a derived word. The clause «إنه أواب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «داود».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «إنَّا سخَّرنا» is resumptive. The clause «يسبِّحن» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الجبال». His words «معه»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يسبحن», and likewise «بالعشي».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: His words «والطير محشورة» conjoin an accusative object to an accusative object, and a ḥāl (circumstantial) to a ḥāl; but the second ḥāl is a noun, to indicate that their gathering was all at once, which points more strongly to [Allah's] power. The clause «كل له أواب» is a ḥāl from «الجبال والطير»; beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it denotes generality. The preposition «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أواب».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «وشددنا» is conjoined to the clause {سَخَّرْنَا}; «الحكمة» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The interrogative clause is resumptive. «إذ»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أتاك».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, badal (substitute) of the preceding «إذ», and the clause «دخلوا» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). The clause «ففزع» is conjoined to the clause «دخلوا». The clause «قالوا» is resumptive. «خصمان»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: we are two disputants; the clause is resumptive within the scope of the speech. The clause «بغى بعضنا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «خصمان». The clause «فاحكم» is conjoined to the clause «بغى». The preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «احكم».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «إن هذا أخي» is resumptive. The clause «له تسع» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن». «نعجة»: tamyīz (specification). The clause «فقال» is resumptive, and the yāʾ and the hāʾ are two objects. The clause «عَزَّنِي» is conjoined to the clause «قال».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The preposition «إلى نعاجه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) (سؤال), which is made to carry (mudammin) the sense of joining, i.e.: he wronged you by joining your ewe so that it is [added] to his ewes; for that reason it is made transitive with «إلى». The clause «وإن كثيرا ...» is conjoined to the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl). The preposition «من الخلطاء» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا», and the preposition «على بعض» is attached to «يبغي». «الذين»: excepted. The wāw in «وقليل» is parenthetical; «قليل» is a khabar (predicate) placed first, «هم» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida); the clause is parenthetical between the two conjoined [clauses], because the clause «وظنَّ داود» is conjoined to the clause «قال». «أنَّ» and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar that takes the place of the two objects of «ظن». The clause «فاستغفر» is conjoined to the clause «ظن». «راكعا»: ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «فغفرنا» is conjoined to the clause «استغفر». The clause «وإن له عندنا ...» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun «نا» in «غفرنا»; the lām is for emphasis. The adverb «عندنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «خليفة»: second object; the preposition «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «خليفة». The clause «فاحكم» is conjoined to the clause «جعلناك», and the preposition «بالحق» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «فاحكم». The fāʾ in «فيضلك» is causal (sababiyya), and the verb is accusative by an implied «أن»; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e.: let there be no following [of desire], and so [no] leading astray. The clause «لهم عذاب» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن». «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the maṣdar (بنسيانهم) is attached to a second naʿt of «عذاب».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «وما خلقنا» is resumptive. «باطلا»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its adjective having taken its place, i.e.: a vain creating. The clause «ذلك ظن» is resumptive, and the clause «فويل للذين» is conjoined to the clause «ذلك ظن»; beginning with the indefinite noun «ويل» is permitted because it denotes a supplication. The preposition «من النار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «أم» is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) one, for turning away (iḍrāb). The clause «نجعل» is resumptive. The preposition «كالمفسدين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «نجعل»; and the parsing of what follows it is likewise.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «كتاب»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: this. The clause «أنزلناه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب». The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليدبَّروا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنزلناه». «مبارك» is a naʿt of «كتاب»; a non-explicit adjective [i.e. a clause] may come before an explicit one.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «ووهبنا» is resumptive. The one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e.: Sulaymān. The clause «نعم العبد» is resumptive, and the clause «إنه أواب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «العبد».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb whose implied form is «اذكر» ("remember"). «الصافنات»: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and «الجياد» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The clause «عُرض» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «فقال» is conjoined to the clause {عُرِضَ}. «حُبَّ»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The preposition «عن ذكر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the tāʾ in «أحببت», meaning: distracted from remembrance. The fāʿil (agent) of «توارت» is the pronoun of the sun, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن توارت) is genitive, attached to «أحببت».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «رُدُّوها» is resumptive within the scope of the speech. The clause «فطفق» is conjoined to an implied resumptive [clause], i.e.: so they returned them, and he began. «مسحا»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e.: stroking a stroking (يمسح مسحا); assuming the verb is necessary because the khabar (predicate) of «طفق» can only be an imperfect verb. The preposition «بالسوق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb.

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The clause «ولقد فتنَّا سليمان» is resumptive, and «جسدا» is the object of «ألقينا».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «قال» is resumptive. The clause «لا ينبغي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مُلكا». The clause «إنك أنت الوهاب» is resumptive; «أنت» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «فسخَّرنا» is conjoined to the clause {قَالَ} in the preceding verse. The clause «تجري» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الريح». The preposition «بأمره» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «تجري». «رخاء»: ḥāl from «الريح». «حيث»: an adverb of place attached to «تجري», and the clause «أصاب» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: His words «والشياطين»: a noun conjoined to {الرِّيحَ}. «كل»: badal (substitute) of «الشياطين»; the intensive form was used because it is in the context of conferring favour.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: His words «وآخرين»: conjoined to {كُلَّ}, so it falls under the ruling of the badal (substitute). «مقرنين»: naʿt (adjective). The preposition «في الأصفاد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مقرنين».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «فامنن» is conjoined to the clause «هذا عطاؤنا». The preposition «بغير حساب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of the two verbs «امنن أو أمسك».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The clause «وإن له عندنا لزلفى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). «عندنا»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «واذكر» is resumptive. «أيوب»: badal (substitute). «إذ»: a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «أيوب». The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from «أن» and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition (the bāʾ). The preposition «بنصب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مسَّني».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The preposition «برجلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اركض». The clause «اركض برجلك» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied, resumptive speech, i.e.: We said. The clause «هذا مغتسل» is resumptive within the scope of the implied speech.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «ووهبنا» is resumptive. «معهم»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مثلهم». «رحمة»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the preposition «منا» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «رحمة». The preposition «لأولي» is attached to a naʿt of «ذكرى».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause (وقلنا له) «خذ» is conjoined to the clause «وهبنا», and the clause «خذ» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of the implied [speech]. The clause «إنَّا وجدناه» is resumptive, and «صابرا» is a second object. The clause «نعم العبد» is resumptive, the clause «إنه أواب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «واذكر» is resumptive. «إبراهيم»: badal (substitute). «أولي»: naʿt (adjective) of those mentioned before.

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The clause «وإنهم عندنا لمن المصطفين» is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ}. The adverb «عندنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «المُصْطَفَيْن». «الأخيار»: naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «واذكر» is resumptive. The clause «وكل من الأخيار» is conjoined to the clause «اذكر»; beginning with the indefinite noun «كل» is permitted because it denotes generality.

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The clause «وإن للمتقين لحسن مآب» is resumptive. The preposition «للمتقين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: «جنات»: badal (substitute) of «حُسْن». «مفتحة»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جنات»; the preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مفتحة»; «الأبواب» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «مفتحة», which is a passive participle.

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: «متكئين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in {لَهُمُ}; the preposition «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متكئين». The clause «يدعون» is a second ḥāl from the pronoun in {لَهُمُ}.
