﴿إن الذين يضلون عن سبيل الله لهم عذاب شديد بما نسوا يوم الحساب﴾: the clause gives the reason for the prohibition of following desire; إن is an abrogating particle, and الذين is its noun; the clause «يضلون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position. «عن سبيل»: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يضلون»; the word of majesty: muḍāf ilayhi; لهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar placed first; عذاب: a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later, and the nominal clause is the khabar of inna; شديد: a naʿt of عذاب; the bāʾ: a preposition; ما: maṣdariyya (infinitival), interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar, genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "because of their forgetting" (بسبب نسيانهم); يوم: the mafʿūl bihi of «نسوا», or an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted second adjective (ṣifa) of His saying «لهم عذاب شديد», i.e. "theirs is a severe punishment, being on the Day of Resurrection, because of their forgetting" (لهم عذاب شديد كائن في يوم القيامة بسبب نسيانهم). And الحساب: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما باطلا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ما is negating; خلقنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); السماء: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الأرض: conjoined to السماء; ما: a relative noun, also conjoined; بين: an adverb of place, accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position. The hāʾ: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and باطلًا: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a vain creation" (خلقًا باطلًا), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of خلقنا, i.e. "acting in vain" or "possessors of vanity" (مبطلين أو ذوي باطل).
﴿ذلك ظن الذين كفروا فويل للذين كفروا من النار﴾: ذلك: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām denotes distance, and the kāf is for address. It points to their being created in vain; ظن: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; الذين: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «كفروا»: the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. فويل: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ويل: a mubtadaʾ; للذين: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of «ويل»; the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. And «من النار»: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ويل.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿أم نجعل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كالمفسدين في الأرض﴾: أم: the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) am, meaning "rather" plus the interrogative hamza, the interrogative being for disapproval; نجعل: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن ("We"); الذين: the first object of نجعل; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. آمن: a past verb, and the wāw: the fāʿil; «وعملوا الصالحات»: conjoined to «آمنوا»; «كالمفسدين»: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «نجعل»; and «في الأرض»: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to المفسدين.
﴿أم نجعل المتقين كالفجار﴾: conjoined to what preceded; «أم»: the disconnected am, meaning "rather" plus the interrogative hamza, the interrogative being for disapproval; نجعل: an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil being a latent pronoun, its implied form being نحن; المتقين: the first object of نجعل; and «كالفجار»: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of «نجعل».

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
[ص] with the dāl unvowelled, because these are letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf al-tahajjī), and the best treatment according to Sībawayh is to leave them unvowelled. They are not inflected, because their rule is to be paused upon. The reading of al-Ḥasan is صادِ, with a kasra on the dāl and without nunation, and his reading has two interpretations. One is that it is from صادى يصادي, when one confronts; from it is فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى [ʿAbasa: 6]. So the meaning is: "confront the Qurʾān with your deeds", that is, match it with them. This interpretation is reported from al-Ḥasan — that he explained his reading by it — in a sound report from him: that the meaning is "recite it and turn yourself to its reading". The other interpretation is that the dāl takes a kasra because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters. The reading of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar is (صادَ) with a fatḥa on the dāl, and there are three interpretations of it:
The first is that it means "recite ṣād". The second is that it is given a fatḥa because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters, the fatḥa being chosen for vowel harmony. The third is that it is accusative as an oath without the particles [of the oath]. The reading of Ibn Abī Isḥāq is (صادٍ) with a kasra on the dāl and nunation, on the basis that it is genitive with the particle of the oath omitted. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is far-fetched, even though Sībawayh permitted something like it. It may also be likened to sounds and other words that are not fully nominal. When you make صاد the name of the sūra, it is a diptote, just as when you name a feminine with a masculine word it is a diptote even if its letters are few. وَالْقُرْآنِ is genitive by the wāw of the oath, which substitutes for the bāʾ. ذِي الذِّكْرِ is a naʿt (adjective), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ. It is a weak noun, and its original is ذَوَيٌ on the pattern فَعَلٌ.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). فِي عِزَّةٍ is its khabar (predicate), that is, in arrogance and refusal to accept the truth, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ بِالْإِثْمِ [al-Baqara:
206]. وَشِقاقٍ is from شاقّ يشاقّ, when one opposes; its derivation is that he has come to be on one side (شقّ) other than the other side.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
كَمْ is in the position of the accusative by أهلكنا. فَنادَوْا: Qatāda said: they called out when it was no time for calling. Abū Jaʿfar said: its meaning, by his statement, is "at a time when calling saves no one", as al-Ḥasan said: they called out with repentance when it was no time for repentance and deeds were of no benefit. This is al-Ḥasan's explanation of His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَلاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ; he said: it is not the time. As for Isrāʾīl, it is transmitted from him, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَلاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ — he said: it is not a time for leaping or fleeing. He said: ضبط القوم جميعا «[Translator's note: so in the source; the phrase is obscure, perhaps "the people were all held fast".]». Abū Jaʿfar said:
Its origin is from ناص ينوص, when one draws back; and one also says ناص ينوص when one goes forward. As for «ولات حين», the grammarians have discussed it and how to pause on it, and Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām wrote at length about it in «Kitāb al-Qirāʾāt», and everything he brought on it, except a little, is to be rejected. Sībawayh said: لات is likened to ليس, and its noun is implied in it, that is: our times are not a time of escape. It is reported that some of the Arabs use the nominative with it, saying وَلاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ «[Translator's note: i.e. حِينُ; the source prints the standard vowelling.]», and it is reported that the nominative is rare; the khabar (predicate) is then omitted, just as the noun was omitted with the accusative, that is: ولات حين مناص لنا. The pause on it according to Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ ] «[Translator's note: a stray bracket stands here in the source.]» — and it is the view of Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān and Abū Isḥāq — is ولات, with the tāʾ, and then you resume with حين مناص. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: the view is as Sībawayh said, because he likened it to ليس; just as you say ليست, you say لات. The pause on it according to al-Kisāʾī is with the hāʾ: ولاه. This is the view of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, as ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported to us from him; and it is reported from him that the argument for that is that it is «لا» to which the hāʾ was added to make the word feminine, as one says ثمّة and ربّة. As for Abū ʿUbayd, he said: the scholars differed about it. Some of them said: لات, then you resume and say حين. Then he mentioned no view of the scholars other than this one, while his own words require something else. Then he mentioned their argument that it is so in all the muṣḥafs, and then said: this would be a proof, were it not that there are proofs that refute it. Then he mentioned proofs none of which is sound — we shall mention them, if Allah the Exalted wills, and make clear what refutes them. He said: the pause in my view is without the tāʾ [ولا], then you resume with حين مناص «[Translator's note: on Abū ʿUbayd's view the tāʾ would join the following word, i.e. تحين مناص.]». Then he mentioned the proofs, saying: the first of them is that we have not found لات in the speech of the Arabs; it is only «لا». Abū Jaʿfar said: even if there were nothing in refutation of this except the agreement of the muṣḥafs on what he denied [it would suffice] — so how much more when the opposite of what he said has been reported by all the grammarians mentioned, Basrans and Kufans? Sībawayh said: «لات» is likened to ليس. And al-Farrāʾ said, from al-Kisāʾī — I think — that he asked Abū al-Sammāl: how do you pause on ولات? and he paused on it with the hāʾ. Abū ʿUbayd said: the second proof is that Ibn ʿAbbās's interpretation indicates that, because Ibn ʿAbbās said: ليس حين نزو ولا فرار. Abū Jaʿfar said: Ibn ʿAbbās's interpretation indicates that what is correct is other than his view; had it been according to his view, Ibn ʿAbbās would have said: ليس تحين مناص, and no one has transmitted this. Abū ʿUbayd said: the third proof is that we have not found the Arabs adding this tāʾ except to حين, أوان and الآن; and he recited, by Abū Wajza al-Saʿdī: [al-Kāmil] 374-
العاطفون تحين ما من عاطف ... والمطعمون زمان أين المطعم
(They are the ones who turn back [to help] when there is none who turns back, and the ones who feed people at a time when [one asks]: where is the feeder?)
And he recited, by Abū Zubayd al-Ṭāʾī: [al-Khafīf] 375-
طلبوا صلحنا ولات أوان ... فأجبنا أن ليس حين بقاء
(They sought peace with us when it was not the time, so we answered that it was no time for sparing.)
And he recited: [al-Khafīf] 376-
نولّي قبل يوم بيني جمانا ... وصلينا كما زعمت تلانا
(Grant us your favour, Jumāna, before the day of my parting, and keep ties with us now, as you claimed.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: the recitation of all the people of language is different from what he said. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
377-
تذكّر حبّ ليلى لات حينا ... وأضحى الشّيب قد قطع القرينا
(He remembered his love for Laylā when it was no time [for it], and grey hair had come to sever the bond.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: as for the first verse, which he recited as by Abū Wajza, the scholars of language read it in four ways, all different from how he recited it, and in one of them there are two implied constructions. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd transmitted it as «العاطفون ولات ما من عاطف». The second version is «العاطفون ولات حين تعاطف». The third version, transmitted by Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān, is «العاطفونه حين ما من عاطف»: he made it a hāʾ in pause and a tāʾ in continuous speech, and claimed that it is for showing the vowel, likened to the feminine hāʾ. The fourth version is «العاطفونه حين ما من عاطف». In this version there are two implied constructions. One of them, the doctrine of Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq, is that the hāʾ is in the position of the accusative, as you say الضاربون زيدا, and when you use a pronoun you say الضاربوه; Sībawayh permitted الضاربونه in poetry, so Ismāʿīl took the verse according to Sībawayh's doctrine in permitting the like of it. The other construction is «العاطفونه» with the hāʾ for showing the vowel, as you say مر بنا المسلمونه in pause, and then it is treated in continuous speech as it is treated in pause — as the people of Medina read ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ [al-Ḥāqqa: 29].
As for the second verse, he has no proof in it, because one pauses on ولات أوان, except that there is something difficult in it, since it is transmitted as «ولات أوانٍ» with the genitive, whereas what follows لات can only be nominative or accusative. And although it is reported from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar that he read ولاتِ حينِ مناص with a kasra on the tāʾ of «لات» and the nūn of «حين», what is established from him is that he read وَلاتِ حِينَ مَناصٍ «[Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowelling; the description indicates لاتِ with kasra and حينَ with fatḥa.]», making لات indeclinable on a kasra and putting حين in the accusative. As for «ولات أوان», there are two implied constructions in it. Al-Akhfash said: something is implied in it, that is, ولات حين أوان.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is clearly mistaken. The other construction is from Abū Isḥāq, who said its implied form is:
ولات حين أواننا; the muḍāf ilayhi was omitted, so it had to be uninflected, and he gave it a kasra because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd recited «ولات أوانٌ» with the nominative.
As for the [third] verse, it is a post-classical (muwallad) verse whose author is unknown, and no proof is valid by it; besides, Muḥammad ibn Yazīd transmitted it as «كما زعمت الآن». Others said: the meaning is كما زعمت أنت الآن, and he dropped the hamza of أنت and the nūn. As for his argument from the ḥadīth of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar — when he mentioned to the man the merits of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "Take them now (تلان) to your companions" — there is no proof in it, because the narrator transmits this only according to the sense. The evidence for this is that Mujāhid transmitted this ḥadīth from ʿAmr ibn ʿUmar «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "from Ibn ʿUmar".]» and said in it: "Go, and do your utmost", and another transmitted it as: "Take them now (الآن) with you." As for his argument that he found it in the Imām [muṣḥaf] as «تحين», there is no proof in it, because the meaning of "the Imām" is that it is the leader of the muṣḥafs; if it differed from them, it would not be their leader, and in all the muṣḥafs it is ولات. Even if there were nothing in this but this argument, it would be sufficient. The plural of مناص is مناوص.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
وَعَجِبُوا أَنْ: [أن] is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is: "at [the fact] that there came to them".
أَجَعَلَ الْآلِهَةَ إِلهاً واحِداً: two objects.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: وَانْطَلَقَ: [أَنِ امْشُوا «[Translator's note: the source attaches the remark to وانطلق, but it concerns أَنِ امْشُوا.]»] is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is: "with [the words] walk on". الْمَلَأُ are the nobles. They have been named, in the report of Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq: they were Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, Shayba and ʿUtba the two sons of Rabīʿa ibn ʿAbd Shams, Umayya ibn Khalaf, al-ʿĀṣī ibn Wāʾil and Abū Muʿayṭ. They came to Abū Ṭālib and said to him: "You are our chief, so give us justice regarding our people and ourselves, and spare us the affair of your nephew and the fools with him, who have abandoned our gods and attacked our religion." Abū Ṭālib sent for the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: "Your people are calling you to equity and fairness." He ﷺ said: "I call them to one word." Abū Jahl said: "And ten [words]!" He said: "They should say: there is no god but Allah." So they stood up and said: أجعل الآلهة إلها واحدا — the verses. Abū Jaʿfar said: it has also been said that the meaning is: the nobles among them went off and said to the common people: امْشُوا وَاصْبِرُوا عَلى آلِهَتِكُمْ, that is, in the worship of your gods. إِنَّ هذا لَشَيْءٌ يُرادُ: that is, this which Muḥammad, upon him be peace, has brought is surely a thing by which is intended the removal of a people's blessings and changes that befall them.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t: [إِنْ هذا إِلَّا اخْتِلاقٌ]: that is, falsehood and invention. One says خلق and اختلق, that is, he invented; and "Allah created the creation" (خلق الله الخلق) is from this, that is, He brought them into being without a prior model. Then He made clear that they were envious, by their saying: أَأُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِنْ بَيْنِنا. بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْ ذِكْرِي, which is the Qurʾān. بَلْ لَمَّا يَذُوقُوا عَذابِ: the original is with the yāʾ retained [عذابي], and the omission is permissible because it is the end of a verse.

nahhas-irab:9-10.t: It has been said: or do they have this, so that they may withhold from Muḥammad ﷺ what Allah has bestowed on him? Likewise أَمْ لَهُمْ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما: if they claim that, فَلْيَرْتَقُوا فِي الْأَسْبابِ, that is, in the means [of ascent] of the heavens; and it has been said: in the means mentioned, which belong only to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. The original is فلِيرتقوا; the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness. One says رقي يرقى and ارتقى يرتقي when one climbs; and رقى يرقي رقيا, like رمى يرمي رميا, is from الرقية (incantation). Then Allah promised His Prophet victory, and He, exalted be His mention, said: جُنْدٌ ما هُنالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الْأَحْزابِ; and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, routed the confederates (al-aḥzāb) as He had promised him. «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis. Al-Farrāʾ interpreted the meaning of مهزوم as: prevented from ascending to the heaven.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ: «قوم» is treated as feminine in the sense of a group (jamāʿa); had it come as masculine, it would be permissible in the sense of a collective (jamīʿ). نوح is declinable (fully inflected) even though it is foreign, because it consists of three letters and so is light. فِرْعَوْنُ is a diptote because it exceeds three letters; it is not declined because of its foreignness and because it is definite. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq claimed that Pharaoh's name was al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab; he said: and it has been said that his name was Muṣʿab ibn al-Rayyān. Others said: whoever ruled Egypt was called Firʿawn, just as whoever ruled Yemen was called Tubbaʿ — they are the Tabābiʿa — and whoever ruled Persia was called Kisrā (Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Kasrā, with a fatḥa on the kāf), and whoever ruled Byzantium was called Qayṣar and Hiraql. وذُو الْأَوْتادِ is a naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: إِنْ كُلٌّ means "not every …" (ما كلّ). إِلَّا كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ عِقابِ: the original has the yāʾ retained; it was dropped because it is the end of a verse, and the kasra indicates it.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
وَما يَنْظُرُ هؤُلاءِ means "they do not wait for" (ما ينتظر); from it is انْظُرُونا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ [al-Ḥadīd:
13]. إِلَّا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: there has never been a cry in the heaven except out of wrath from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, upon the people of the earth. ما لَها مِنْ فَواقٍ is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; and من فُواق with a ḍamma on the qāf «[Translator's note: so in the source; the ḍamma is on the fāʾ, i.e. فُواق.]» is the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. The soundest thing said about them is that they are two dialectal forms with one meaning; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ reported that.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا: among the best of what has been said about its meaning is what Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said:
They said: our Lord, hasten for us our share in the Hereafter before the Day of Reckoning. It is derived from قططت الشيء, that is, I cut it. So the share is a portion cut off for a person, and it is well known in the speech of the Arabs to say قطّ for a share; and a document written for a gift is called قطّ, as al-Aʿshā said: [al-Ṭawīl] 378-
ولا الملك النّعمان يوم لقيته ... بإمّته يعطي القطوط ويأفق
(Nor King al-Nuʿmān, the day I met him in his splendour, giving out gift-writs and excelling.)
«بإمّته» means in his favour and his lofty state; «يافق» means "puts right"; «القطوط» is the plural of قطّ, which is the writ for a gift. Its plural is also قططة, and for a small number أقطّ and أقطاط.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ ذَا الْأَيْدِ: a naʿt (adjective). الأيد and الآد [mean strength], as one says العيب and العاب; from it is رجل أيّد (a strong man). إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, one who turns back (ثواب) «[Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps توّاب, "oft-repenting".]». It is reported from others that whenever he remembered his sin or it crossed his mind, he sought forgiveness for it, as the Prophet ﷺ said: «I seek forgiveness in a day and a night a hundred times». One says آب يؤوب when one returns, as [the poet] said: [Mukhallaʿ al-Basīṭ] 379-
وكلّ ذي غيبة يؤوب ... وغائب الموت لا يؤوب
(Everyone who is absent returns, but the one absent through death does not return.)

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا الْجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ: [يسبّحن] is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is reported that they used to answer him with glorification; and it has been said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, subjected them so that they moved with him, and that is their glorification, because they point to the transcendence of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, above any likeness to created beings. بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِشْراقِ: from أشرقت الشمس, when the sun shines and becomes clear. From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) is mentioned in the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty — and he recited «يسبّحن بالعشيّ والإشراق».

nahhas-irab:19-20.t: إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا «[Translator's note: so in the source; the remark concerns وَالطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً.]» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الجبال. Al-Farrāʾ said: if it were read (والطّيرُ محشورةٌ) it would be permissible, because the verb is not expressed; and likewise if it were read (وشددنا ملكه) «[Translator's note: the source does not show what variant is meant.]». وَآتَيْناهُ الْحِكْمَةَ: two objects «[Translator's note: the source has "فعولان", read مفعولان.]». وَفَصْلَ الْخِطابِ is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَهَلْ أَتاكَ نَبَأُ الْخَصْمِ, and after it إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا الْمِحْرابَ [in the plural], because الخصم stands for a plural; it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), from خصمته خصما. Its true sense in Arabic, when you say القوم خصم له, is "people of dispute"; then you put the muḍāf ilayhi in place of the muḍāf. One may also say خصوم, as one says عدول.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلى داوُدَ: إذ comes twice because they are two acts. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that one of them means «لمّا». Another view is that the second and what follows it is an explanation of what precedes it. قالُوا لا تَخَفْ: the ḍamma was dropped from the fāʾ for the jussive, and the alif changed from wāw was dropped so that two unvowelled letters would not meet. خَصْمانِ — and before this إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا الْمِحْرابَ [in the plural] — because two is a plural. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said:
As you say نحن فعلنا (we did) when you are two. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is plural while it was a narration; when the narration ended and the address came, the two spoke about themselves, saying «خصمان». Abū Isḥāq said: that is, we are two disputants. Others said: the verb of saying is omitted, that is, two disputants say. Abū Isḥāq said: had it been accusative, خصمين, it would be permissible, that is, we have come to you as two disputants. بَغى بَعْضُنا عَلى بَعْضٍ: al-Kisāʾī said: had it been بغى بعضهما على بعض, it would be permissible. Others said: بغى بعضنا may be meant to refer to David ﷺ. فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَنا بِالْحَقِّ وَلا تُشْطِطْ: al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read وَلا تُشْطِطْ with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and a ḍamma on the first ṭāʾ «[Translator's note: i.e. تَشْطُطْ; the source prints the standard vowelling.]». Abū Ḥātim said: this is not known in the language. Abū Jaʿfar said: one says أشطّ يشطّ when one is unjust in judgement or speech; and شطّ يشِطّ and يشُطّ when one goes far. So يشطط «[Translator's note: i.e. تُشْطِطْ]» in the verse is clearer, and يشطط «[Translator's note: i.e. تَشْطُطْ]» is permissible, that is, do not go far from the truth, as [the poet] said: [al-Mutaqārib] 380-
تشطّ غدا دار جيراننا ... وللدّار بعد غد أبعد ]
(Tomorrow the home of our neighbours will be far, and the day after tomorrow the home will be farther still.)

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: Al-Ḥasan read تَسع وتَسعون نعجة with a fatḥa on the tāʾ in both; it is an anomalous dialectal form, and it is the sound report of al-Ḥasan's reading. The Arabs allude to a woman with "ewe" (نعجة) and "sheep" (شاة). From ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read وعازّني في الخطاب.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: قالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلى نِعاجِهِ: it is said that this was the error of David ﷺ, because he said "he has wronged you" without establishing proof, without the opponent's admission, and without asking his opponent whether this was so or not. This is one view. As for the view of the earlier scholars whose word is not to be rejected — among them ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on them — they said: David ﷺ did no more than say to the man: give up your wife [to me]. Abū Jaʿfar said: so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, reproached him for this and alerted him to it. This is not one of the major sins; and whoever goes beyond this in attributing error brings only what is not soundly reported from any scholar, and incurs great sin in it. بِسُؤالِ نَعْجَتِكَ is a figurative iḍāfa, that is, by asking for your ewe. وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ الْخُلَطاءِ: the plural of خليط, which is a partner. This plural [فُعَلاء] is formed from what has no wāw [as its middle radical]; one may not say طولاء for طويل, because of the heaviness of the vowel on the wāw. وَظَنَّ داوُدُ أَنَّما فَتَنَّاهُ: Abū ʿUmar «[Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps Abū ʿAmr.]» and al-Farrāʾ said: ظنّ means "was certain", except that al-Farrāʾ explained it by saying that it is not permissible in [rational] meanings for ظنّ to mean certainty «[Translator's note: so in the source.]». From ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he read أَنَّما فَتَّنَّاهُ «[Translator's note: the source prints فَتَنَّاهُ.]» with doubling of the tāʾ and the nūn, for intensification; and from Qatāda that he read it إنما فتناه with both lightened. فَاسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُ وَخَرَّ راكِعاً: [راكعا] as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: فَغَفَرْنا لَهُ ذلِكَ: [ذلك] is in the position of the accusative by غفرنا; it may also be in the position of the nominative, that is, the matter is that. وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى: Mujāhid said, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmar, who said: الزلفى is nearness to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, on the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: يا داوُدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْناكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ: that is, We have established you so that you command what is right and forbid what is wrong, and so succeed the prophets and righteous leaders who were before you. إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, without disagreement; it is an intransitive verb, and if you gave the yāʾ a ḍamma it would be transitive. بِما نَسُوا يَوْمَ الْحِسابِ: that is, they abandoned deeds. One says نسي الشيء when one abandons it.

nahhas-irab:27-28.t: The explanation of this is that they used to say: there is no punishment there and no Fire; so the disbeliever and the sinner are happy with pleasures and seizing property, and the wronged one is wretched, because both end up in the same thing. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, refuted this for them, in that He did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain, because what they claimed is false and that is their supposition. He, Majestic and Mighty, made that clear with His saying: أَمْ نَجْعَلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ كَالْمُفْسِدِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ. In this there is a refutation of the Murjiʾa, because they say: it is possible that the corrupter be like the reformer, or of higher rank than him. And after it also: أَمْ نَجْعَلُ الْمُتَّقِينَ كَالْفُجَّارِ.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: كِتابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ إِلَيْكَ means "this is a Book". مُبارَكٌ is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ: [العبد] is nominative by نعم.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: الْجِيادُ is the plural of جواد, said of a horse when it is a strong runner, as a person is called جواد when he is quick and abundant in giving; except that one says قوم أجواد (generous people) and خيل جياد (swift horses). It has been said that جياد is the plural of جائد; whoever says this argues that if it were the plural of جواد one would say جواد, like طويل and طوال. As plurals of جواد one says جوداء, أجوداء, جُوْد with the wāw unvowelled, and جُوُود with it vowelled with a ḍamma.

nahhas-irab:32-33.t:
فَقالَ إِنِّي أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ: al-Farrāʾ construes it as an object, that is, I have preferred the love of horses; others construe it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and he takes الخير to mean الخيل (horses). Others say: the meaning of أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ is that he was in prayer, and horses that had been taken as spoils were brought to him to be paraded before him; he pointed to them with his hand, because he was praying, until the horses were hidden and the walls of the stables concealed them. When he finished his prayer he said: رُدُّوها عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحاً, that is, he set about stroking them. There are two views on its meaning. One is that he set about stroking their legs and necks with his hand, honouring them, and to show that it is not unseemly for an eminent man to do such a thing with his horses.
The proponent of this view said: how could he kill them, when that involves wasting wealth and punishing what has no guilt? It has also been said: المسح here means cutting; he was permitted to kill them. السّوق is the plural of ساق, like دار and دور, and for the smallest number أسوق. ساق is feminine.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمانَ: that is, We tested him with what weighed upon him. وَأَلْقَيْنا عَلى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَداً: it has been said that by it is meant a dead child of his. That is, he went round his slave-women and said: I hope that each one of them «[Translator's note: the source has the masculine منهم.]» will bear a male child. In the ḥadīth, he did not say "if Allah wills", so only one of them conceived, and the child died and was cast upon his throne, as a trial concerning the love of this world, desire for it and seeking children, and [to show] that it should not be so. ثُمَّ أَنابَ: that is, he turned back from what he had been doing. It has also been said: the body of a devil.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: قالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي: it has been said: there is no proof in this that that act of his was a sin, because he may seek forgiveness for what he did before prophethood, or seek forgiveness for what occurs to him.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (40) وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى: that is, a قرين (companion) «[Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps قربى, "nearness".]». وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ: that is, a place of return.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا أَيُّوبَ: [أيوب] as a badal (substitute). إِذْ نادى رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذابٍ: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (إنّي) with a kasra on the hamza. Al-Farrāʾ said: the readers agreed on reading «بنُصْب» with a ḍamma on the nūn and the light [unvowelled ṣād]. This is a mistake, and it is also counted a self-contradiction, because he said the readers agreed on this, and then after it reported that they mentioned from Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ that he read (بنَصَب) with a fatḥa on the nūn and the ṣād. He made a mistake about Abū Jaʿfar: Abū Jaʿfar read only (بنُصُب) with a ḍamma on the nūn and the ṣād, as Abū ʿUbayd and others reported; and it is transmitted from al-Ḥasan. As for (بنَصْب) «[Translator's note: the source does not vowel the variants in brackets; the vowelling given here follows the descriptions in the text and the known readings.]», it is the reading of ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī and Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī, and this reading is also transmitted from al-Ḥasan. And (بنصب) has also been reported [in another form]. All of this, according to most grammarians, means النَّصَب (fatigue). نُصْب and نَصَب are like حُزْن and حَزَن. It is also possible that نُصُب is the plural of نَصَب, like وَثَن and وُثُن; and it is possible that نُصْب means نُصُب with the ḍamma dropped from it. As for وَما ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ [al-Māʾida: 3], it has been said that it is the plural of نصاب, and نَصْب is on the pattern of the original maṣdar (verbal noun). It has been said about the meaning of مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذابٍ that it is what befell him of his whispering, nothing else; and Allah knows best.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: ارْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ: al-Kisāʾī said: that is, We said [to him]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: الرّكض is moving; and for this reason al-Aṣmaʿī said: one says ركضت الدابة (I spurred the mount), but one does not say ركضت هي (it ran), because الركض is only its rider's moving his feet, and the animal has no action in that. Sībawayh reported: ركضت الدابة فركضت هي, like جبرت العظم فجبر (I set the bone and it mended) and حزنته فحزن (I grieved him and he grieved).

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ: Mujāhid interpreted this to mean that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, restored his family to him and gave him the like of them in the Hereafter, so that he had his family in this world and the like of them with them in the Hereafter. As for what is reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd — when it reached him that Marwān said: he was only given a replacement for his family, and was not given them themselves — he said: it is not as he said; rather, he was given his family and the like of them with them. Some scholars interpreted this saying to mean that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, restored to him those of his family who were absent, and there were born to him the like of those who had died, and he was given from their offspring the like of them. رَحْمَةً is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Isḥāq said: it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). وَذِكْرى is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الرحمة. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of وَذِكْرى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ is that a person of intelligence, when he is afflicted, remembers the affliction of Job ﷺ and is patient.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثاً: that is, and We said to him: and take in your hand a ضغث. He said: it is a bundle of grass and the like.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
وَاذْكُرْ عِبادَنا إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ: as a badal (substitute). The reading of Ibn ʿAbbās is واذكر عبدنا, with a sound chain; Ibn ʿUyayna transmitted it from ʿUmar «[Translator's note: so in the source; probably ʿAmr (ibn Dīnār).]» from ʿAṭāʾ from him, and it is the reading of Ibn Kathīr. On this reading إِبْراهِيمَ is a badal for عبدنا, and إسحاق and يعقوب are conjoined. The reading with the plural is clearer. The explanation of this in Arabic is that when you say: رأيت أصحابنا زيدا أبين «[Translator's note: the source repeats a phrase here by dittography: "رأيت أصحابنا زيدا أبين، وشرح هذا من العربية أنك إذا قلت".]», the explanation of this in Arabic is that when you say: رأيت أصحابنا زيدا وعمرا وخالدا (I saw our companions, Zayd, ʿAmr and Khālid), Zayd, ʿAmr and Khālid are a badal for them; [but if you say "our companion"], Zayd alone is the badal, and he is the companion, while ʿAmr and Khālid are conjoined to "our companion" and are not included in the companionship except by some other evidence — except that it is known that His saying, Majestic and Mighty, «وإسحاق ويعقوب» is included in servanthood. أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصارِ: as for وَالْأَبْصارِ, there is agreement on its interpretation: it is insight in religion. As for الْأَيْدِي, there is disagreement on its interpretation. The exegetes say:
It is strength in religion. Some say: الأيدي is the plural of يد, which is favour, that is, they are possessors of favours, that is, those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour. It has also been said: they are possessors of favours and beneficence, because they did good and sent forward good.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: ذِكْرَى is in the position of the genitive, except that it has the feminine alif; its genitive is by the iḍāfa [بخالصةِ ذكرى]. The reading of the Kufans is بِخالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ, as a badal (substitute); and this is a badal of a definite noun for an indefinite one. أَخْلَصْناهُمْ: We made them sincere (mukhliṣīn) and purified (mukhlaṣīn) from defilements; they made their deeds sincerely for Allah, Majestic and Mighty, remembering the abode, which is the Hereafter, and remembering it not intending thereby this world or affected effort for its people.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t:
That is, of those whom We have chosen [and purified] from defilements. مصطفين is the plural of مصطفى: you added to مصطفى an unvowelled yāʾ and a nūn, while the alif of مصطفى is unvowelled; the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters, and it was the more suited to dropping because a fatḥa precedes it. الأخيار is the plural of خيّر, as though it were pluralised with the extra letter dropped, as if you pluralised خَيْر, just as you say ميّت and أموات. One says رجل خيِّر and خَيْر, as one says:
هيِّن and هَيْن, ليِّن and لَيْن.

nahhas-irab:49-50.t:
هذا ذِكْرٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). The meaning is: this is a fine remembrance in this world. وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ: that is, together with this fine remembrance in this world, a good place of return on the Day of Resurrection. Then He made it clear with His saying, Majestic and Mighty: جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ. العدن in the language is residing; one says عدن بالمكان when one resides in a place. However, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: the Garden of ʿAdn is a palace in the Garden; it has five thousand gates, at every gate five thousand excellent ones (khayyira); none enters it except a prophet, a truthful one (ṣiddīq) or a martyr. مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الْأَبْوابُ: الأبواب is nominative because it is the noun of what has no named agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). Al-Farrāʾ permitted «مفتحةً لهم الأبوابَ», on the basis that مفتّحة refers to the gardens, and he and Sībawayh recited: [al-Wāfir] 381-
وما قومي بثعلبة بن سعد ... ولا بفزارة الشّعر الرّقابا
(My people are not [of] Thaʿlaba ibn Saʿd, nor of Fazāra, the hairy-necked.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, مفتحةُ الأبوابِ; then you bring the nunation and put it in the accusative. And Sībawayh recited: [al-Wāfir] 382-
ونأخذ بعده بذناب عيش ... أجبّ الظهر ليس له سنام ]
(And after him we shall hold on to the tail-end of a life, flat-backed, having no hump.)

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيها is accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of the gardens.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t:
[أتراب] is a naʿt (adjective) of قاصرات, because قاصرات is indefinite even though it is in construct with a definite noun; the evidence for that is that the definite article enters it, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 383-
من القاصرات الطّرف لو دبّ محول ... من الذّرّ فوق الإتب منها لأثّرا
(Of those with restrained glances: if a year-old ant crawled over her shift, it would leave a mark.)
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the meaning is مفتّحة لهم أبوابها, and that the definite article stands in place of the hāʾ and alif [the pronoun ـها]; and he permitted مررت برجل حسنة العين, meaning حسنة عينه. Abū Isḥāq said: it is not permissible for the definite article to stand in place of the hāʾ and lām «[Translator's note: so in the source; read "the hāʾ and alif".]», because the definite article is a particle that comes for a meaning, while the hāʾ and alif are a noun, and it is impossible for one of them to stand in the place of the other. The meaning is only: مفتّحة لهم الأبواب منها (the gates of them opened for them).

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: هذا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ: the implied form is "the matter is this". لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ is the noun of إن.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: جَهَنَّمَ is a badal (substitute) for شرّ.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
هذا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is حميم, by way of fronting and postponement, that is: this is boiling water and pus, so let them taste it. It may also be that «هذا» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and فليذوقوه is in the position of the khabar. It may also be that the meaning is "the matter is this", and حميم and غساق, if you do not make them a khabar, are nominative in the sense of "it is boiling water and pus". Al-Farrāʾ puts them in the nominative in the sense of هو حميم وغساق, and recited:
[al-Basīṭ] 384-
حتّى إذا ما أضاء الصّبح في غلس ... وغودر البقل ملويّ ومحصود
(Until, when morning shone in the last darkness, and the herbage was left, [some] twisted and [some] mown.)
It may also be that هذا is in the position of the accusative with an implied verb, as you say: زيدا أضربه; and the accusative in this is preferable. وَغَسَّاقٌ with the light form is the reading of the people of Medina, the people of Basra and some Kufans; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read وَغَسَّاقٌ with doubling «[Translator's note: the source prints both with doubling.]». As for its meaning, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said — and about it — it is thick pus; if any of it fell in the East, it would make those in the West stink, and if any of it fell in the West, it would make those in the East stink.
Mujāhid said: غسّاق is cold. From others than Mujāhid: it burns with its cold as the boiling water burns with its heat.
Qatāda said: it is what flows from between their skins and their flesh. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: one says غسقت عينه when it runs, so غسّاق with doubling is preferable, as you say:
سيّال. Abū Jaʿfar said: others among the leading grammarians disagreed with him on this, because when one says
غسّاق [with doubling] one makes it a naʿt (adjective) of something not specifically known, and this is far-fetched in Arabic; whereas when one says غَساق [light] it is a noun, and that is preferable to putting the adjective in place of the qualified noun and omitting the qualified noun.

nahhas-irab:59-60.t:
هذا فَوْجٌ مُقْتَحِمٌ مَعَكُمْ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), that is, rushing into the Fire with you. The implied form is: it is said to them:
this is a troop entering the Fire with you; and those who are in the Fire say: لا مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ. «مرحبا» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and means "may you not find spaciousness (رحبا)", that is, room. The troop says: بَلْ أَنْتُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ أَنْتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ لَنا, that is, you called us to disobedience. فَبِئْسَ الْقَرارُ: that is, our abiding.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
قالُوا رَبَّنا مَنْ قَدَّمَ لَنا هذا: al-Farrāʾ said: that is, who laid down this for us and made it a practice. Others said:
That is, who sent forward this punishment for us by calling us to sins. فَزِدْهُ عَذاباً ضِعْفاً فِي النَّارِ: that is, a punishment for his disbelief and a punishment for his calling us, so that it becomes double.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: وَقالُوا ما لَنا لا نَرى رِجالًا: (ما) is in the position of the nominative, and لا نَرى is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: أَتَّخَذْناهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا with a ḍamma on the sīn [سُخريّا] is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir, as a question; the connective alif fell away because it was no longer needed. Ibn Kathīr, al-Aʿmash, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read اتّخذناهم, taking it as a connective alif in اتّخذناهم; «اتخذناهم» is then a naʿt (adjective) of الرجال. Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim incline to this reading, and both argued that those who said this knew that they had taken them in mockery, so how could they ask — فالا «[Translator's note: so in the source; the word is garbled, perhaps "فلا", "so no"]» — when the question has already come before? Abū Jaʿfar said: this argument is not binding; if it were necessary, it would be necessary in مالنا [لا نرى رجالا]. Rather, the question here is as al-Farrāʾ said about it; he said: it is in the sense of rebuke and wonder. الرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخاءً حَيْثُ أَصابَ «[Translator's note: so in the source; this quotation (Ṣād: 36) is out of place, and the remark that follows concerns أَمْ زاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ الْأَبْصارُ.]»: if you read it with the question, أم is for equivalence (taswiya); and if it is without a question, it means "or rather" (أبل).

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: [تَخاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ] means "it is the disputing"; it may be a badal (substitute) for الحقّ; it may be a khabar after a khabar (predicate); and it may be a badal for ذلك according to its position.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: قُلْ إِنَّما أَنَا مُنْذِرٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); «ما» has restrained «أنّ» «[Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has إنّ.]» from operating. وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: «من» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis. Abū Isḥāq said: were it read in the accusative, إِلَّا اللَّهَ الْواحِدَ الْقَهَّارَ «[Translator's note: the source prints the nominative vowelling.]», it would be permissible as an exception (istithnāʾ).

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: [رَبُّ السَّماواتِ] is a naʿt (adjective); and if you put the first in the accusative, you put [this] in the accusative. It is also permissible to put the first in the nominative and what follows it in the accusative, as praise (ʿalā al-madḥ).

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: That is, the Qurʾān is a momentous report. It has also been said: the meaning is "of great benefit". Abū Isḥāq said: this report is momentous news.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: That is, you do not accept it.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have explained its meaning.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: «أنّ» is in the position of the nominative because it is the noun of what has no named agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). It may also be in the position of the accusative, meaning "except because" (إلّا لأنّما).

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: فَإِذا سَوَّيْتُهُ: إذا turns the past into the future, because it resembles the particles of condition, and its apodosis is like theirs. ساجِدِينَ as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ is by way of rebuke; whoever reads it with a connective alif makes it a statement. أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْعالِينَ: Ibn ʿAbbās said: he was, in the knowledge of Allah, among the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: قالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ said: some Arabs say أنا أخير منه وأشرّ منه. This is the original, except that the alif was dropped from it because of frequent use.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t: قالَ فَاخْرُجْ مِنْها: it has been said: meaning from the Garden. فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ: that is, stoned with the stars and meteors.

nahhas-irab:79-81.t: قالَ رَبِّ فَأَنْظِرْنِي إِلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ, which is the Day of Resurrection; but that was not granted, and he was given respite إِلى يَوْمِ الْوَقْتِ الْمَعْلُومِ, which is the day on which creation dies. He was given respite until it out of contempt for him, and because he reaches nothing but whispering, and he corrupts only one who would not be righteous even if he did not whisper to him. «[Translator's note: the source reads "إلّا لي الوسوسة", read "إلى الوسوسة".]»

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: That is, I will surely call them to the sins on account of which they go astray, that is, fail.

nahhas-irab:84-87.t:
قال الحقّ والحقّ أقول «[Translator's note: i.e. with both in the accusative, فَالْحَقَّ وَالْحَقَّ.]» — this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, the people of Basra and al-Kisāʾī. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read قالَ فَالْحَقُّ وَالْحَقَّ أَقُولُ, with the first in the nominative and the second with a fatḥa. Al-Farrāʾ permitted «قال فالحقِّ والحقَّ أقول» with the first in the genitive. There is no disagreement about the second, that it is accusative by أقول. The first is accusative by way of incitement (ighrāʾ), that is: so follow the truth and listen to the truth. It has also been said: in the sense of "I make it true", that is, I do it. Al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd permitted الحقّ to be accusative in the sense of "truly" (حقّا) [governed by] لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ; but according to a group of grammarians that is a mistake: زيدا لأضربنّ is not permissible, because what follows the lām is cut off from what precedes it. Whoever puts الحق in the nominative makes it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: I am the Truth, or: the truth is from Me — both are reported from Mujāhid. The implied form may also be: this is the truth. On the genitive there are two views. One is that it is with the particle of the oath omitted; this is al-Farrāʾ's view, who said: as you say: الله لأفعلنّ. Sībawayh permitted something like this, and Abū al-ʿAbbās faulted it, and permitted only the accusative, because the particles of the genitive are not implied. The other view is that the fāʾ substitutes for [the particle of] the oath, as they recited:
[al-Ṭawīl] 385-
فمثلك حبلى قد طرقت ومرضع ... فالهيتها عن ذي تمائم محول
(Many a one like you, pregnant or nursing, have I visited by night, and distracted her from her year-old child wearing amulets.)
Masrūq transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: whoever is asked about what he does not know, let him say "I do not know" and not affect [knowledge], for his saying "I do not know" is knowledge. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said to His Prophet ﷺ: قُلْ ما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ وَما أَنَا مِنَ الْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t:
وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ: that is, [you will know that] the news of the Qurʾān is true, after a while. Abū Isḥāq said: that is, after death.
Al-Farrāʾ said: after death and before it, that is, that will become clear.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُ ذَلِكَ وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَـآبٍ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿لَزُلْفَىٰ﴾ means a lofty rank.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-zulfā in the language means nearness (al-qurba), and from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ الآخَرِينَ﴾, and from it is the poet's saying:
مَرَّ اللَّيالِي زُلَفَاً فَزُلَفَا * سَمَاوَةَ الهِلاَلِ حتَّى احْقَوقفا
(The passing of the nights, hour upon hour, over the crescent's form until it grew bent.)
That is, one hour drawing near to another.
Then He said ﴿وَحُسْنَ مَـآبٍ﴾; al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, a goodly place of return.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰدَاوُودُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It is said that it is from this that it became permissible to speak of "caliphs" (khulafāʾ).
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدُ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوْمَ ٱلْحِسَابِ﴾.
﴿بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوْمَ ٱلْحِسَابِ﴾ means: they abandoned working for it, and were forgetful of it; this is the view of al-Suddī.
ʿIkrima said: this is a case of fronting and postponing (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr), i.e. "for them, on the Day of Reckoning, is a severe punishment" ﴿بِمَا نَسُواْ﴾, i.e. because they abandoned the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and judging with justice.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بَاطِلاً ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾.
That is: when they said, "There is no reckoning, no Garden and no Fire," this was said to them.
So He informed that He will punish them for that.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ﴾.
It is on the implication of "this" (i.e. "This is a Book…").
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿لِّيَدَّبَّرُوۤاْ آيَاتِهِ﴾, i.e. so that they reflect on the outcomes of what comes from it, ﴿وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾, i.e. [those of] intellects.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لِدَاوُودَ سُلَيْمَانَ نِعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ﴾.
There are seven views on it:
a- Ibn al-Sayyib [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably Ibn al-Musayyib] said: ﴿الأَوَّابُ﴾ is the one who sins and then repents, then sins and then repents.
b- Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: ﴿الأَوَّابُ﴾ is the one who glorifies [Allah].
c- Qatāda said: the obedient one.
d- ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: the one who remembers his sin in private and seeks forgiveness for it.
e- It is said: the merciful one.
f- It is said: the repentant one.
g- The linguists said: the one who returns often, who returns to repentance.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِٱلْعَشِيِّ ٱلصَّافِنَاتُ ٱلْجِيَادُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿ٱلصَّافِنَاتُ﴾ among horses are those that raise one of their forelegs and stand on three.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-ṣāfin is the one standing.
And this is what is well known in the speech of the Arabs.
Mujāhid said: al-jiyād are the swift ones.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَالَ إِنِّيۤ أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ ٱلْخَيْرِ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّي﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-khayr (good) and al-khayl (horses) are one and the same in the speech of the Arabs.
Abū Jaʿfar said: in the noble ḥadīth: (Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection).
So it is as if they were called "good" for this reason.
And in the ḥadīth: (When Zayd al-Khayl came as a delegate to the Prophet ﷺ, he said to him: You are Zayd al-Khayr).
He is "Zayd ibn Muhalhil", the poet.
Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is: I have preferred the love of good.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the best that has been said on this is that the meaning is: I have loved the love of good with a love [Translator's note: i.e. ḥubba is taken as an absolute object], and it distracted me from the remembrance of my Lord.
Qatāda said: from the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr).
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتْ بِٱلْحِجَابِ﴾.
One of the two [views] [Translator's note: the text announces two views; the second is introduced below with "It is said"]: that the meaning is "until the sun was hidden", the meaning of the pronoun being already understood, as the poet said:
عَلَى مِثْلِها أَمْضِي إذَا قالَ صَاحِبِي * أَلاَ لَيْتَنِي أَفْديكَ مِنْهَا وأَفْتَدي
(On the like of her I press on when my companion says: Would that I could ransom you from it and ransom myself.)
That is, "from it", meaning from the desert, though it had not been mentioned.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: when He said ﴿بالعَشِيّ﴾, the meaning was "after the sun's decline", so the pronoun was brought on that basis.
And Abū Isḥāq narrated from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The prayer that Sulaymān neglected was the afternoon prayer."
And it is said: "until they were hidden behind the veil", meaning the horses.
And Saʿīd ibn Masrūq narrated from ʿIkrima, who said: the horses with which Sulaymān was occupied were twenty thousand horses, and he cut them down.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحاً بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلأَعْنَاقِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَطَفِقَ مَسْحاً بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلأَعْنَاقِ﴾: he cut their legs and their necks, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, gave him in their place something better than them.
And it is said that the meaning of ﴿فَطَفِقَ مَسْحاً﴾ is: he set about stroking them with his hand, without killing, as Ibn Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He says: he began stroking the manes of the horses and their hocks, out of love for them.
And whoever said "he killed them" holds that it was a ritual slaughter, or that this was permitted, just as it is narrated of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that a slave pleased him, so he freed him.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَانَ وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَىٰ كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَداً ثُمَّ أَنَابَ﴾.
Reports have been narrated about this:
a- Among them, that a devil seized his kingdom for some days.
b- And among them, that the devils killed his son, fearing that he would rule over them after him, and cast him on his throne; and Allah knows best what happened of that.
And the wording entails that his kingdom was removed, and another sat on his throne.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكاً لاَّ يَنبَغِي لأَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِيۤ﴾.
That is: give me a distinction and a rank, as Ibrāhīm said: ﴿رَبِّ أَرِني كَيْفَ تُحْيِي المَوْتَى﴾?

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ ٱلرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخَآءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ﴾.
Qatāda said: al-rukhāʾ is the gentle [wind].
Al-Ḥasan said: al-rukhāʾ is neither tempestuous nor feeble, but in between.
And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿رُخَآءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ﴾: he said: obedient wherever he wished.
Al-Aṣmaʿī related [the saying]: "He aimed at (aṣāba) the right point, but missed the answer."
That is, he intended the right point; and its literal sense in the language is "he aimed", from their saying: aṣabta, i.e. you aimed and did not miss.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلشَّيَاطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّآءٍ وَغَوَّاصٍ﴾.
That is: those who built for him sanctuaries and statues, and those who dived into the sea and brought out ornaments.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي ٱلأَصْفَادِ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, in the fetters.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says ṣafadtu al-rajul when you have bound him, and aṣfadtuhu: I gave him.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا فَٱمْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿هَـٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا﴾ is the kingdom, so give and withhold.
And Qatāda said: these are the devils, so confine whom you wish and release whom you wish.
And from Ibn ʿAbbās: he had three hundred wives and nine hundred concubines: "This is Our gift."
Abū Jaʿfar said: the most fitting of these is the first, because the first comprises everything that was given, and it comes right after those things.
And Sufyān narrated from his father, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَٱمْنُنْ﴾ means give, ﴿أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ means withhold, for there is no reckoning upon you.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ means without blame.
And al-Ḥasan said: there is no one upon whom a blessing is bestowed but he will be called to account for it, except Sulaymān; then he recited ﴿هَـٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا﴾, i.e. without stinting [Translator's note: the text has «نقتير»; presumably «تقتير», stinting].
And it may mean: he will not be called to account for it.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, a goodly destination.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ، إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ، أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ﴾.
And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan, al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Jaʿfar [that they read] ﴿بِنَصَبٍ﴾ with fatḥa on the nūn and the ṣād; according to most linguists the two have one meaning, just as one says ḥuzn and ḥazan, except that al-Qutabī related that Abū ʿUbayda said: al-nuṣb is evil, and al-naṣab is exhaustion.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says anṣabahu, yunṣibuhu when he tormented and harmed him, and from it is:
* "كِلِينِي لِهَمٍّ يا أُمَيْمَةُ نَاصِبِ" *
(Leave me, O Umayma, to a tormenting care.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: the best that has been said on the meaning of ﴿أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ﴾ is what Yūsuf ibn Mihrān narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
"When the affliction befell Ayyūb ﷺ, Iblīs took a chest and sat by the road treating people. Ayyūb's wife came to him and said: Will you treat a man who has such-and-such an illness? He said: Yes, on one condition: that when I cure him, he says to me: 'You cured me.' I want no other payment from him than this.
So Ayyūb's wife came to Ayyūb and told him, and he said to her: That is the devil. By Allah, if I recover I shall strike you a hundred [lashes]. When he recovered, he took a date-stalk with a hundred [twigs] on it and struck her with it a single blow."
Abū Jaʿfar said: so the meaning of al-nuṣb on this [account] is what he put to him, i.e. it is something he whispered.
As for the view of whoever said that "al-nuṣb" is what afflicted him in his body, and "al-ʿadhāb" is what afflicted him in his wealth, it is far-fetched.
Mujāhid said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: he struck her with rushes.
Qatāda said: he took a stick on which there were ninety-nine sticks, it making the hundred complete, and struck her with it.
Mujāhid said: this is specific to him.
And ʿAṭāʾ said: this is for all people.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what is evident from this is that it is specific, because He said ﴿وَلاَ تَحْنَثْ﴾, thus lifting the breach of oath from him; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said ﴿فَاجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً﴾, and whoever is lashed with a date-stalk bearing a hundred [twigs] has only been lashed a single lash.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ عِبَادَنَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَإِسْحَاقَ، وَيَعْقُوبَ، أُوْلِي ٱلأَيْدِي وَٱلأَبْصَارِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿أُوْلِي ٱلأَيْدِي﴾: he said: strength and worship; ﴿وَٱلأَبْصَارِ﴾: he said: understanding in the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the singular of "al-aydī" is yad (hand), and "hand" is used for strength.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿أُوْلِي ٱلأَيْدِي﴾ without the yāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. «الأَيْدِ»; the text reproduces the standard spelling].
And this is clear from their saying: ayyadahu, when he strengthened him.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّآ أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى ٱلدَّارِ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, they remind [people] of the Hereafter and of obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a clear view, i.e. they make [people] renounce this world and desire the Hereafter, and so too the prophets, may Allah bless them and grant them peace.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, by fear of the Hereafter.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning on this view is that they remember the Hereafter, desire it, and renounce this world.
And this view is the apparent meaning of the word.
And it may also be among their qualities to make [others] desire the Hereafter.
These two interpretations are according to the reading of whoever read with tanwīn.
And whoever read it as a genitive construct (iḍāfa) said its meaning is: We purified them with the best of what is in the Hereafter.
This is the view of Ibn Zayd.
And the meaning on this view is that they remind [people] of the Hereafter, make them desire it, and make them renounce this world.
And on the reading with iḍāfa there is another view, that of Mujāhid, the meaning being: We purified them by Our mentioning the Garden to them.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ عِندَنَا لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصْطَفَيْنَ ٱلأَخْيَارِ﴾.
That is: they are chosen [and kept clear] of sins and impurities.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَٱلْيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلأَخْيَارِ﴾.
Al-Ashʿarī said: he was called "Dhū al-Kifl" because he took charge of (kafala) the work of a righteous man who used to pray a hundred prayers every day, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, praised him for the excellence of his guarantee; and he was not a prophet.
And it is said: he guaranteed the Garden to one of the kings, and wrote him a document to that effect.
And al-kifl in the language is the share and the portion.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا ذِكْرٌ، وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾.
﴿هَـٰذَا ذِكْرٌ﴾ means honour, and a good mention in this world.
Then He said ﴿وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾, i.e. they have, along with the good mention in this world, a goodly return in the Hereafter.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
Then He explained that, saying ﴿جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُّفَتَّحَةً لَّهُمُ ٱلأَبْوَابُ﴾.
That is, its gates.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعِندَهُمْ قَاصِرَاتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ أَتْرَابٌ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: they restrict their gaze to their husbands and do not desire others.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and the linguists recited:
مِنَ القَاصِرَاتِ الطَّرْفِ لَوْدَبَّ مُحْوِلٌ * مِنَ الذَرِّفَوْقَ الأِتْبِ مِنهَا لأَثَّرا
(Of those who restrain their glance; were a year-old ant to creep over her garment, it would leave a mark.)
Al-itb is the skin [Translator's note: so in the text; al-itb is usually glossed as a kind of garment].
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿أَتْرَابٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: of one age.
Mujāhid said: that is, alike.
And al-Suddī related: affectionate to one another as sisters, neither hostile to one another nor jealous of one another.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَرِزْقُنَا مَا لَهُ مِن نَّفَادٍ﴾.
That is, cessation.
Al-Suddī said: whenever something is taken from it, the like of it returns.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ﴾.
The meaning may be: This is scalding water and ghassāq, so let them taste it.
And the meaning may be: This — let them taste it; of it is scalding water and of it is ghassāq, as the poet said:
لهَا مَتَاعٌ وأَعْوَانٌ غَدَوْنَ لَهَا * قِتْبٌ، وَغَرْبٌ إِذَا مَا أُفْرِغَ انْسَحَقَا
(She has gear and helpers who set out for her: a saddle-frame, and a great bucket that, when emptied, gushes away.)
Qatāda said: we used to be told that al-ghassāq is what flows from between the skin and the flesh.
Al-Farrāʾ said — and it is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk —: it is said that al-ghassāq is something cold that burns, as the scalding water burns.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Qatāda's view is more fitting, because one says ghasaqat ʿaynuhu when it flowed.
And Ibn Zayd said: al-ḥamīm is the tears of their eyes, collected in the pools of the Fire, which they are given to drink.
And al-ghassāq is the pus that comes out of their skins.
And the preferred [reading] on this basis is ﴿غَسَّاقٌ﴾ [with doubling], so that it is like sayyāl (flowing).

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآخَرُ مِن شَكْلِهِ أَزْوَاجٌ﴾.
Mujāhid and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read ﴿وَأُخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ﴾.
Abū ʿAmr rejected ﴿آخرُ﴾ because of His saying ﴿أَزْوَاجٌ﴾, i.e. a single thing is not given a plural as its predicate (khabar).
And ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī rejected ﴿وَأُخَرُ﴾, saying: had it been ﴿وأُخَرُ﴾, it would have been "min shaklihā".
Abū Jaʿfar said: neither of the two objections is binding, because if one reads ﴿وأُخَرُ منْ شَكْلِهِ﴾, the meaning may be: and others of the kind of what We mentioned;
and others of the kind of the scalding water;
and others of the kind of the ghassāq;
or the meaning may be: and others of the kind of the whole.
And whoever reads ﴿وَآخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ﴾, his reading is good, because the meaning pertains to the action, and when the meaning pertains to the action, a singular may be given a dual or plural predicate, as you say: "So-and-so's punishment is of two kinds", and "his punishment is of various kinds."
And ﴿أَزْوَاجٌ﴾ may refer to the scalding water, the ghassāq and the other.
Qatāda said ﴿مِنْ شَكْلِهِ﴾: of its sort.
Yaʿqūb [ibn al-Sikkīt] said: al-shakl is the like, and al-shikl is coquetry.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: ﴿وَآخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ أَزْوَاجٌ﴾ is the bitter cold (al-zamharīr).
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Zaʿfarānī narrated to us: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Abū Rajāʾ, from al-Ḥasan concerning His saying ﴿أَزْوَاجٌ﴾: he said: varieties of punishment.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا فَوْجٌ مُّقْتَحِمٌ مَّعَكُمْ لاَ مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صَالُواْ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
﴿هَـٰذَا فَوْجٌ﴾ means a group and a party; ﴿مُّقْتَحِمٌ مَّعَكُمْ﴾ means one after another; ﴿لاَ مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صَالُواْ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
[﴿لاَ مَرْحَباً﴾ in the sense of: may you not find raḥb, i.e. spaciousness, meaning: may their dwellings in the Fire not be spacious.]
Al-Farrāʾ holds that the speech is parenthetical (muʿtariḍ), and that the meaning is: they said, "No welcome to them."

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا مَن قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا فَزِدْهُ عَذَاباً ضِعْفاً فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: meaning the snakes and the vipers.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَا لَنَا لاَ نَرَىٰ رِجَالاً كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَشْرَارِ. أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سِخْرِيّاً﴾ [verses 62, 63].
And it is read ﴿أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ﴾? as a question.
And on the first reading [Translator's note: i.e. with the connecting hamza, «اتَّخذناهم», as a statement] there are two views:
One of them, the view of al-Farrāʾ: that it is by way of rebuke and wonder; he said: the Arabs bring the interrogative in rebuke and wonder, and also omit it.
And the other view, that of Abū Ḥātim, is that the meaning is: "And they said, Why do we not see men whom we took as an object of ridicule?", making it a naʿt (adjective) of "the men".
And the meaning of «سُخْرِي» and «سِخْري» according to most linguists is the same, except Abū ʿAmr, who claimed that ﴿سِخْرِيّاً﴾ means they mock them, and ﴿سُخْرِيّاً﴾ means they subject them to forced service and humiliate them.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ زَاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ ٱلأَبْصَار﴾.
Layth narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿وَقَالُوا مَا لَنَا لاَ نَرَى رِجَالاً﴾: he said: Abū Jahl and al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra said ﴿مَا لَنَا لاَ نَرَى رِجَالاً﴾? He said: they said: Where is Salmān? Where is Khabbāb? Where is Bilāl? Where is ʿAmmār?
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سِخْرِيّاً﴾ and so were we mistaken, or are they in the Fire and our eyes have swerved from them?
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a good view, because "am" is for equivalence (taswiya), so the meaning according to his view becomes: were we mistaken, or were we not mistaken?
And it is said: it is in the sense of "bal" (rather).
And the reading with the connecting alif is clear and good.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ نَبَأٌ عَظِيمٌ. أَنتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: meaning the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِيَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ بِٱلْمَلإِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: meaning the angels; they disputed — as the Exalted informed about them in His saying — ﴿إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلاَئِكَةِ إِنِّي خَالِقٌ بَشَراً مِن طِينٍ﴾.
That is, when He created Ādam, peace be upon him, with His hand.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and in the ḥadīth: "They dispute about the expiations: they are performing ablution thoroughly in difficult conditions, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer."
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-malaʾ in the language means the nobles and the eminent, as if they were fully capable (malīʾūn) of what is entrusted to them.
And it has been said: it may be that by "the highest assembly" here He means the angels, and ﴿إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾ means Quraysh, because among them were those who said: the angels are the daughters of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed the Prophet ﷺ of that, and informed him that they are His servants, and that they ﴿لاَ يسْتكبِرُون عن عبادَتِه ولا يَسْتَحسِرون﴾.
And it is said: it may be that by "the highest assembly" here the nobles of Quraysh are meant, when they disputed among themselves, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed that to the Prophet ﷺ; and Allah knows best what He intended.
And the most fitting of what has been said on it is what Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī and Qatāda said: that the highest assembly here is the angels, who disputed about the matter of Ādam, peace be upon him, when he was created, and said: "Will You place on earth a vicegerent?"

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ إِلاَّ أَنَّمَآ أَنَاْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
The meaning may be: [nothing is revealed to me] except a warning.
Or the meaning may be: except that I am only a clear warner [Translator's note: i.e. with an implied preposition «بأنما»].

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَجَدَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ كُـلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ. إِلاَّ إِبْلِيسَ ٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Iblīs was among the nobles of the angels; he was the keeper of the gardens, and he was entrusted with the lowest heaven and the earth and whoever is in them. He became pleased with himself and considered that he had superiority over the angels, and no one knew of that except Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded the angels to prostrate to Ādam, he refused and his arrogance became manifest.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ فَٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ. وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِيۤ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of ﴿إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ﴾ is: until the day on which people are requited for their deeds.
The exegetes said: ﴿رَجِيمٌ﴾ means accursed, and the meaning is: stoned (marjūm) with the curse.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنظَرِينَ. إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْوَقْتِ ٱلْمَعْلُومِ﴾.
Its meaning is: until the day of the known time, which no one knows but Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ فَٱلْحَقُّ وَٱلْحَقَّ أَقُولُ. لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
And it is read with the first [ḥaqq] in the accusative.
And al-Farrāʾ related that the genitive is permissible in the first.
Abū Jaʿfar said: its nominative is on three meanings:
a- It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: "For I am the Truth."
b- And Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from al-Ḥakam from Mujāhid, who said: "The truth is from Me, and I speak the truth."
c- And the third view, according to the school of Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, in the sense of: "the truth is: I will surely fill Hell", meaning "the truth is that I fill Hell."
And Sībawayh says likewise about His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوْا الآيَاتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ﴾.
And the accusative is in the sense of: "the truth I said, and I speak the truth."
And Abū Ḥātim said: the meaning is: "the truth: I will surely fill", i.e. "truly, I will surely fill."
And he gave another view, namely that the meaning is: "I speak the truth, and truly I will surely fill."
And the most fitting [view] on the accusative is the first view, and it is the position of Abū ʿUbayda.
And the genitive is in the sense of an oath (qasam): the wāw was omitted, and al-Ḥaqq [the Truth] is then [a name] of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And Sībawayh permitted "Allāhi laʾafʿalanna" (By Allah, I shall surely do), except that this is better than that, except that the fāʾ here is a substitute for the wāw, just as it is a substitute for the wāw [Translator's note: so in the text; in the verse the fāʾ stands in for wāw rubba] in his saying:
فَمِثْلُكِ حُبْلَى قَدْ طَرَقْتُ ومُرْضِعٍ * فأَلْهَيتُها عن ذِي تَمَائِمَ مُحْوِلِ
(Many a one like you, pregnant or nursing, have I visited by night, and distracted her from her year-old child wearing amulets.)

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ مَآ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ وَمَآ أَنَآ مِنَ ٱلْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ﴾.
Ibn Zayd said: that is, I do not make conjectures, nor take upon myself what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has not commanded me.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "Whoever would like to know the decree of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, regarding His creation, let him read Sūrat al-Ghuraf."
Mujāhid said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: it is Meccan except for three verses of it, which were revealed in Medina concerning "Waḥshī", the killer of Ḥamza — the blessings of Allah be upon Ḥamza. He embraced Islam and entered Medina, and the Prophet ﷺ could not bear to look at him, so he imagined that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, had not accepted his faith; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿قُلْ يٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُواْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ لاَ تَقْنَطُواْ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ to the end of the three verses.
[Translator's note: this entry, filed under 38:88, is in fact the introduction to Sūrat al-Zumar, which is also called Sūrat al-Ghuraf.]

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Of that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿صۤ﴾.
With sukūn on the dāl, because it is one of the letters of the alphabet; and it is [also] read ṣāda.
According to Sībawayh the best [reading] of it is with sukūn, and it is not declined, because its rule is to be paused upon; so it is like the letters of the alphabet ﴿الۤم﴾ and ﴿المۤر﴾.
And ﴿صۤ﴾, if you make it a name for the sūra, is a diptote.
Mujāhid said: it is the opening of the sūra.
[Qatāda said: it is one of the names of the All-Merciful.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: it is the key to the names of Allah, Exalted is He, "Ṣamad" and "Ṣādiq al-waʿd" (true to the promise).]
It is related that al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿صَادْ﴾: Allah has spoken the truth (ṣadaqa).
And the reading of al-Ḥasan: ﴿صَادِ﴾ with kasra on the dāl; its meaning is: confront (ṣādi) the Qurʾān with your deeds.
One says "ṣādaytuhu", i.e. I faced him; and this is well known among the lexicographers.
And it may have been given kasra for the meeting of two sukūns.
And the fatḥa is on three grounds:
a- It has been said that one of them is that it is an oath: "[By] Allah, I will surely do".
b- Another is that it means: recite Ṣād and the Qurʾān.
c- Another is that it was given fatḥa for the meeting of two sukūns.
The reading with kasra on the dāl and with tanwīn is a solecism (laḥn) according to most grammarians — even though Ibn Abī Isḥāq was among the great grammarians — except that some grammarians permitted it, on the basis that it is in the genitive by the oath; Sībawayh permitted that. [Translator's note: the source has «لنحويَّينَ» for «النحويين».]
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ذِي ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾.
Sufyān related from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, and Misʿar from Abū Ḥuṣayn, concerning the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ذِي ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾ — that is, possessing eminence.
And this is like His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ﴾.
And it has been said: the meaning of ﴿ذِي ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾ is: in it is the mention of the nations and others.
As for the jawāb (answer) of the oath, it has been said that it is in His saying ﴿إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ
تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ﴾; but this is very far-fetched, because narratives and reports intervene.
And it has been said: the answer is in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ
قَرْنٍ﴾.
The meaning [then] is: "surely how many (la-kam) We destroyed", and the lām was omitted, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿قَدْ
أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاهُّا﴾; and this is the view of al-Farrāʾ.
And it has been said: the answer is ﴿إِنْ كُلٌّ إلاَّ كذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ﴾.
And it has been said: the answer is omitted, i.e. "the matter is not as these unbelievers say".
This is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا في عِزَّةٍ
