One: that it is His saying {إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ} [Ṣād: 64]; al-Zajjāj and the Kufans other than al-Farrāʾ said it. Al-Farrāʾ said: "We do not find it sound, because it is very far from His saying «والقرآن»." The second: that it is His saying «كم أهلَكْنا»; the original is «لكم أهلَكْنا», and he omitted the lām as he omitted it in His saying {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا} [al-Shams: 9] after His saying {والشمس}, when the speech became long. Thaʿlab and al-Farrāʾ said it. The third: that it is His saying {إِن كُلٌّ إِلاَّ كَذَّبَ الرسل} [Ṣād: 14]; al-Akhfash said it. The fourth: that it is His saying «صاد», because the meaning is "By the Qur'an, Muḥammad has spoken truly." Al-Farrāʾ and Thaʿlab also said it. This is a construction on their part on the permissibility of fronting the answer to the oath, and that this letter is cut off from a sentence which it indicates. Both are weak. The fifth: that it is omitted. They disagreed on its estimation. Al-Ḥūfī said: / its estimation is "the truth has come to you," and the like. Ibn ʿAṭiyya estimated: "the matter is not as they claim." Al-Zamakhsharī: "it is miraculous (inna-hu la-muʿjiz)." And the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān]: "you are among the messengers (innaka la-min al-mursalīn)." He said: "because it is the parallel of {يس * والقرآن الحكيم * إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ المرسلين} [Yā Sīn: 1-3]." Al-Zamakhsharī has here an extremely ugly expression. It is: "If you say: His saying «ص والقرآنِ ذي الذكر بل الذين كفروا في عِزَّةٍ وشِقاقٍ» is a speech whose apparent sense is self-contradictory and unstructured, what is the way of its structure? I say: there are two ways. That He mentioned the name of this letter of the alphabet by way of challenge and a pointer to inimitability, as passed at the beginning of the Book, then followed it with the oath with its answer omitted because the challenge indicates it, as if He said: 'By the Qur'an possessing the Reminder, it is an inimitable speech.' The second: that «صاد» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, on the basis that it is a name of the sūra, as if He said: 'This is Ṣād,' meaning this sūra that rendered the Arabs incapable, 'and by the Qur'an possessing the Reminder,' as you say 'This is Ḥātim, by Allah,' meaning: he is the one famed for generosity, by Allah; and likewise when He swears by it, as if He said: 'I swear by Ṣād and by the Qur'an possessing the Reminder that it is inimitable.' Then He said: 'Nay, those who disbelieve are in pride and arrogance against submitting to that and acknowledging it, and in opposition to Allah and His Messenger.' And if you make it that sworn by, and conjoin to it {والقرآن ذِي الذكر}, it is permissible for you to mean by 'the Qur'an' the whole revelation, and to mean the particular sūra. Its meaning: 'I swear by the noble sūra, and by the Qur'an possessing the Reminder,' as you say: 'I passed by the generous man and the blessed soul (nasama),' not meaning by 'nasama' other than the man.'"

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {بَلِ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: an iḍrāb (turning away) of transition from one story to another. Al-Kisāʾī in the transmission of Sawra, Ḥammād ibn al-Zibriqān, Abū Jaʿfar and al-Jaḥdarī read «في غِرَّةٍ» with a dotted ghayn and rāʾ. It has been reported that Ḥammād the transmitter read it so by misreading, and when it was rejected to him he said: "I did not think the disbelievers were in ʿizza." This is a delusion of his, because the ʿizza referred to is the zeal of pre-Islamic ignorance. The indefiniteness in «عزَّة وشِقاق» indicates their intensity and aggravation.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {أن جاءكم}: that is: "min an" ("because"), and there is the well-known disagreement about it.
And His saying: «وقال الكافرون» is of the category of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, as a testimony against them with this ugly description.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {عُجَابٌ}: an intensive of «عجيب», as they say rajul ṭuwāl and amr surāʿ; both are more intensive than ṭawīl and sarīʿ. ʿAlī, al-Sulamī, ʿĪsā and Ibn Miqsam read «عُجَّاب» with tashdīd on the jīm, which is more intensive than the former, so it is like rajul karīm, kurām with light and kurrām with tashdīd. Muqātil said: "ʿujāb, meaning the light one, is the dialect of Azd Shanūʾa." This reading, I mean with tashdīd, is like His saying {وَمَكَرُواْ مَكْراً كُبَّاراً} [Nūḥ: 22]; it is more intensive than kubār, and kubār is more intensive than kabīr.
And His saying: «أجَعَلَ», that is: "Did he turn them into one god," in his saying and his claim.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {أَنِ امشوا}: «أنْ» may be maṣdarī, that is: "they went off with their saying: 'Walk!'"; and it may be explicative (mufassira): either of «انطلق», because it was made to include the meaning of saying. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "because those who go off from a meeting of dispute / must speak and exchange views about what happened to them." End. It was also said: rather it explains an omitted sentence in the position of a ḥāl, its estimation: "and they went off conversing, saying 'Walk!'" It may be maṣdarī, governed by this omitted element. It was also said: al-inṭilāq here is the rush into saying and speech, as in inṭalaqa lisānuhu, so «أنْ» explains it without inclusion or omission. As for al-mashy, the apparent is that it is the well-known one. It was also said: rather it is a prayer for abundance of livestock; this is invalid in wording and meaning. As for the wording, from this meaning one says only amshā l-rajulu, with alif, when his livestock became abundant, that is: he became an owner of livestock; so on this it should have been read «أَمْشُوا» with a hamzat qaṭʿ with fatḥa. As for the meaning, it is not intended at all, and what meaning is there in that!
However, al-Zamakhsharī mentioned a view that is sound in terms of the craft and nearer in meaning than the preceding, saying: "It is possible that they said: 'imshū,' that is: 'multiply and gather,' from mashat al-marʾa, when her childbearing became abundant; from it comes al-māshiya, as a good omen." End. And if one stops at «أنْ» and begins with what follows it, one should begin with kasra on the hamza, not with ḍamma, because the third letter is with kasra by estimation, as the original is imshiyū, and then it was altered by omission. This is like beginning with ḍamma on the hamza in your saying «اغْزِي يا امرأةُ» (O woman, raid!), even though the zāy is with kasra, because it is with ḍamma in the original, the original being ighzuwī like ukhrujī, and it was altered by omission.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {فِى الملة}: there are two views on it. One: that it is attached to «سَمِعْنا», that is: "we have not heard in the latter religion of this that you have brought." The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl from «هذا», that is: "we have not heard of this, as existing in the latter religion," that is: we did not hear from the soothsayers nor from the People of the Books that the oneness of Allah would arise in the latter religion; and this is of the extremity of their lying.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {أَأُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذكر}: the ruling on these two hamzas has preceded at the beginning of Āl ʿImrān, and the fact that what occurs of it in the Qur'an is in three places. The iḍrābs (turnings) in this verse are clear, and «أم» is munqaṭiʿa (disconnected).

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {فَلْيَرْتَقُواْ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This is a speech construed on the meaning, that is: 'if they claim that, let them ascend.'" So he made it the apodosis of an implied condition, and al-Zamakhsharī often does that.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {جُندٌ}: two views are permissible in it. One, and it is the apparent: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are a host." And «ما» has two views: one, that it is redundant; the second, that it is an adjective of «جُنْدٌ», by way of magnification, or to mock them, or for belittlement, for the descriptive «ما» is used for these two meanings. Like it is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
3850 - ... and a talk, whatever, for all its brevity
This has already preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. And «هنالك» has three views: one, that it is the khabar of «الجند», «ما» is redundant and «مَهْزُوم» is an adjective of «جُنْد»; Makkī mentioned it. The second: that it is an adjective of «جند». The third: that it is accusative by «مهزوم». And «مهزوم» also has two views: one, that it is a second khabar of that implied mubtadaʾ; the second, that it is an adjective of «جُنْد», except that on this view it is better not to make «هنالك» an adjective but attached to it, so as not to require that a non-explicit description precede an explicit one. «هنالك» points to the place of the dispute and the passing over of the preceding words, which is Mecca, that is: "they will be routed in Mecca," and this is a report of the unseen. It was also said: it points to the support of the idols. It was also said: to the digging of the trench, meaning: to the place of that. The second of the first two views: that «جندٌ» is a mubtadaʾ and «ما» redundant, «هنالك» an adjective and «مهزوم» its khabar; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "There is remoteness in it because of its breaking away from the preceding speech."
I say: this view reported from Abū al-Baqāʾ was preceded by Makkī.
His saying: «من الأحزاب»: it may be an adjective of «جُند» and it may be an adjective of «مهزومٌ». Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that it be attached to it. There is remoteness in it, because what is meant by al-aḥzāb are the routed ones themselves.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {ذُو الأوتاد}: this is an eloquent metaphor, in that he likened sovereignty to a hair tent (bayt al-shaʿr), and the hair tent holds only by pegs and ropes, as al-Afwah said:
3851 - The tent is built only on posts, and there are no posts unless pegs are fixed
So it is borrowed for the firmness of might and sovereignty and the settledness of the affair, as in the saying of al-Aswad:
3852 - ... in the shade of a kingdom firm of pegs
/ Al-awtād is the plural of watid. It has dialects: watid with fatḥa on the wāw and kasra on the tāʾ, which is the most eloquent; watad with two fatḥas; and wadd with assimilation of the tāʾ into the dāl. He said: 3853 - She brings out the peg when she has ... and hides it when she ...
And «watt» by replacing the dāl with tāʾ and then assimilating the tāʾ into it. This is irregular, because the original is replacing the first for the second, not the reverse. Something like this has preceded in Āl ʿImrān at the saying of Allah the Exalted: {فَمَن زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النار} [Āl ʿImrān: 185]. One says: watid wātid, that is: strong, firm, which is like the figurative saying shughl shāghil. Al-Aṣmaʿī recited:
3854 - She found at the water a firm (wātid) tree-stump, and he would not fail her in the appointments
It was also said: the pegs here are literal, not metaphorical. In tafsīr: that he had pegs to which he tied people, torturing them thereby. The disagreement about al-Ayka has preceded in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {أولئك الأحزاب}: it may be resumptive with no position, and it may be a khabar. The mubtadaʾ, Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "from His saying «وعادٌ»; it may be from «ثمود»; and it may be from His saying «وقومُ لوط»." I say: the apparent is the conjunction of «عادٌ» and what follows it to «قومُ نوحٍ», and the resumption of the sentence after it. On what Abū al-Baqāʾ said, it would also be permissible that the mubtadaʾ be «وأصحابُ الأَيْكَة» alone.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {إِن كُلٌّ}: «إنْ» is negative and has no operation here at all, not even in the dialect of the one who said:
3854 - bi-in huwa mustawliyan ʿalā aḥadin ... [incomplete in the source]
nor on the reading {إِنَّ الذين تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ الله عِبَاداً}, because the negation is broken by «إلاَّ»; for its being broken in the case of the original, which is «ما», invalidates it, so how with its derivative? It has preceded that it may be an answer to the oath.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {مَّا لَهَا مِن فَوَاقٍ}: «لها» may govern «مِنْ فَواق» as agent in the nominative, relying on the negation; and it may be a sentence of a mubtadaʾ and khabar. On both estimations the negated sentence is accusative in position as an adjective of «صَيْحةً», and «مِنْ» is redundant. The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «فُواق» with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa. It was said that they are two dialects with one meaning, namely the time between two milkings of the milker and two suckings of the suckler; the meaning: "it has no pause of the length of a fuwāq of a she-camel." In the ḥadīth: «العِيادَةُ قَدْرَ فُواقِ ناقة» (the visit to the sick is the length of a fuwāq of a she-camel), and this in meaning is like the saying of Allah the Exalted: {فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لاَ يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً} [al-Aʿrāf: 34]. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "It has no return." From afāqa l-marīḍ: when he returned to his health. The ifāqa of the she-camel is the moment when the milk returns to her udder. One says: afāqat al-nāqa tufīqu ifāqatan: she returned, and the fīqa gathered in her udder. The fīqa is the milk that gathers between the two milkings, and its plural is afwāq. As for afāwīq, it is the plural of the plural. One says: nāqa mufīq and mufīqa. It was also said: fawāq with fatḥa is the ifāqa and rest, like jawāb from ajāba. Muʾarrij al-Sadūsī and al-Farrāʾ said it, and among the commentators Ibn Zayd and al-Suddī. As for the one with ḍamma, it is a noun, not a maṣdar. The well-known view is that they have one meaning, like qiṣāṣ [al-shaʿr] and quṣāṣ, and ḥamām al-makkūk and ḥumām.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {قِطَّنَا}: that is: "our share and portion." Its origin is from qaṭṭa l-shayʾa, that is: he cut it; from it qaṭṭa l-qalam (he cut the pen). The meaning: a cut from what You promised us. For this reason it is applied to a document and a deed, qiṭṭ, because they are two pieces cut off. A prize is also called qiṭṭ, because it is a piece of the gift. Al-Aʿshā said:
3855 - Nor was al-Nuʿmān the king, on the day you met him in his felicity, giving the qiṭāṭ (grants) and ...
And its most frequent use is for the written document. Umayya said:
3856 - A people who have the courtyard, the land of Iraq, and what is collected to them in it, and the qiṭṭ and the pen
Its plural is quṭūṭ as preceded, and qiṭaṭa, like qird, qirada and qurūd. In the paucal, aqiṭṭa and aqṭāṭ / like qadaḥ, aqdiḥa and aqdāḥ, except that afʿila in the pattern fiʿl is irregular.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {دَاوُودَ}: a badal or ʿaṭf bayān, or accusative by an implied "I mean." And «ذا الأيْدِ» is an adjective of it. Al-ayd is strength. One says: rajul ayd and ayād.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {يُسَبِّحْنَ}: a circumstantial clause from «الجبال». He brought it as an imperfect verb rather than an active participle, not saying musabbiḥāt, to indicate renewal and occurrence bit by bit, as in the saying of al-Aʿshā:
3857 - By my life, many eyes have been drawn to the light of a fire on a height, being burned
that is: being burned bit by bit. Had he said muḥarraqa, it would not have indicated this meaning.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {والطير مَحْشُورَةً}: the majority read both in the accusative: an object conjoined to an object and a ḥāl to a ḥāl, as you say: "I struck Zayd bound and ʿAmr free." He brought the ḥāl as a noun because he did not intend that the action took place bit by bit, since gathering them all at once is a stronger indication of power, and the gatherer is Allah the Exalted. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Jaḥdarī read both in the nominative, making them an independent sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar.
His saying: «كُلٌّ له»: that is: each of the mountains and the birds, for Dāwūd, that is: for the sake of his glorification, is a glorifier; so he put «أوَّاب» in place of musabbiḥ. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the Creator, the Exalted, and what is meant is that each of Dāwūd, the mountains and the birds is a glorifier and one who turns back to Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {وَشَدَدْنَا}: the majority read «شَدَدْنا» without tashdīd, that is: "We strengthened," like «سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بأخيك». Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Ḥasan read «شَدَّدْنا» with tashdīd, which is an intensive of the reading of the majority.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {نَبَأُ الخصم}: it has already preceded that al-khaṣm is in origin a maṣdar, so it suits the singular and the masculine and their opposites, and it may also agree [in number]. From it: {لاَ تَخَفْ خَصْمَانِ} [Ṣād: 22] and {هذان خَصْمَانِ} [al-Ḥajj: 19]. What is meant by al-khaṣm here is a plural, by the evidence of His saying «إذ تَسَوَّرُوا» and His saying «إذ دَخَلُوا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It occurs for the singular and the plural, like al-ḍayf. He the Exalted said: {حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ المكرمين} [al-Dhāriyāt: 24] because it is in origin a maṣdar. One says khaṣamahu yakhṣimuhu khaṣman, as you say ḍāfahu ḍayfan. If you say: this is a plural and His saying «خصمان» is a dual, how is that sound? I say: the meaning of khaṣmān: two parties, two adversaries, and the evidence for it is the reading of those who read «[خَصْمَانِ] بغى بَعْضُهُمْ على بَعْضٍ»; like it is the saying of the Exalted {هذان خَصْمَانِ اختصموا}. If you say: what do you do with His saying {إِنَّ هَذَآ أَخِي}, which is evidence of two? I say: this is the saying of one of them, and what is meant is {بَعْضُنَا على بَعْضٍ}. If you say: there has come in the report that two angels were sent to him? I say: its meaning is that the dispute for judgment was between two angels, and that does not prevent others accompanying them. If you say: how did He name them all 'adversary' in His saying «نَبَأ الخَصْمِ» and «خَصْمان»? I say: since each of the two litigants was accompanied in the form of an adversary, naming by it is sound."
His saying: «إذ تَسَوَّروا»: on what governs «إذ» there are several views. One: that it is governed by «النبأ» when the story is not meant by it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Makkī held this; that is: "Has there come to you the news that occurred at the time of their climbing into the prayer chamber?" Some have rejected this: the news occurring at that time cannot have come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and if the story is meant by the news, it would not be a governor. The Shaykh said it. The second: that the governor is «أتاك», and it is rejected by what rejected the first. Al-Zamakhsharī explicitly rejected these two views, saying: "If you say: by what is «إذ» put in the accusative? I say: it cannot but be put in the accusative by «أتاك», or by «النبأ», or by an omitted element. It is not permissible to put it in the accusative by «أتاك», because the coming of the news to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ occurs only in his time, not in the time of Dāwūd; nor by «النبأ», because the news occurred in the time of Dāwūd, so its coming to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is not sound. And if you mean by the news the story itself, it would not be a governor. So it remains that it is accusative by an omitted element, its estimation: 'and has there come to you the news of the litigation of the adversaries when'." So he chose that it be governed by an omitted element. «[Translator's note: the source text as it stands lists the first, second and fourth views; the third is not present.]» The fourth: that it be put in the accusative by «الخصم» because of the sense of the verb in it.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {إِذْ دَخَلُواْ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a badal from the first «إذ». The second: that it is accusative by «تَسَوَّرُوا». The meaning of tasawwarū: they climbed / to the top of the sūr, which is the wall, not hamzated, as in your saying tasannama l-baʿīr, that is: he reached its hump (sanām). The pronoun in «تَسَوَّروا» and «دخلوا» refers to the khaṣm because it is a plural in meaning as preceded, or on the basis that it is a dual, and the dual is a plural in meaning; the disagreement about this has already been verified.
His saying: «خَصْمان»: the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "we are two adversaries"; for this reason He said «بَعْضُنا». Whoever read «بعضهم» in the third person may permit estimating it so, having regard to the wording of «خَصْمان», and may permit estimating "they are two adversaries" for agreement. It is reported from al-Kisāʾī «خِصْمان» with kasra on the khāʾ. It has preceded that he read it so in al-Ḥajj.
His saying: «بَغَى بَعْضُنا»: a sentence that may be explicative of their state, and may be a second khabar.
His saying: «ولا تُشْطِطْ»: the majority read with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the shīn and kasra on the first ṭāʾ, from ashṭaṭa yushṭiṭu ishṭāṭan, when he transgressed the truth. Abū ʿUbayda said: "shaṭaṭtu fī l-ḥukm and ashṭaṭtu fīhi, when I was unjust"; so it is among those in which faʿala and afʿala coincide. He uncontracted it on one of the two permissible ways, as in «مَنْ يَرْتَدِدْ», and its verification has preceded. Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «تَشْطُط» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, from shaṭṭa in the sense of ashaṭṭa as preceded. Qatāda read «تُشِطَّ», from the quadriliteral ashaṭṭa, except that he assimilated, which is one of the two permissible ways, like the reading of those who read {مَن يَرْتَدَّ مِنكُمْ}; and from him also «تُشَطِّطْ» with fatḥa on the shīn and kasra on the ṭāʾ with tashdīd, shaṭṭaṭa yushaṭṭiṭu; the intensification in it is for increase. Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh read «تُشاطِطْ», of the pattern mufāʿala.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا}: «كم» is the object of «أهلَكْنا», «مِنْ قَرْنٍ» is a tamyīz, and «مِنْ قبلِهم» is for the beginning of the range.
His saying: «ولات حين»: this sentence is accusative in position as a ḥāl from the agent of «نادَوْا», that is: they cried for help, while there was no escape and no deliverance.
The majority read «لاتَ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and «حينَ» in the accusative, and there are several views on it. The first, which is the school of Sībawayh: «لا» is negative in the sense of laysa, and the tāʾ is added to it, as it is added in rubba and thamma; it operates only on times in particular, such as lāta ḥīna and lāta awāna, as in the saying:
3830 - They sought our peace, and it was no time (lāta awānin), so we answered that it is not a time for survival
and the saying of another:
3831 - The aggressors regretted, and it was no hour of regret (lāta sāʿata mandami); and aggression is a pasture whose seeker is unwholesome
Most often its nominative is omitted, its estimation being: "wa-lāta l-ḥīnu ḥīna manāṣin." Sometimes the accusative is omitted and the nominative retained; some read here so, as in the saying: 3832 - Whoever turned away from their fires, I am the son of Qays, there is no leaving (lā barāḥ), that is: "there is no leaving for me." It does not operate on other than times, according to the well-known view, but some have clung to its operating on other than times by the saying:
3833 - Nawār yearned, and it was not the place (lāta hannā) to yearn; and what Nawār had hidden appeared
For «hannā» is among the adverbs of place. There is irregularity in it in three respects: one, its operating on a demonstrative, which is definite, while it operates only on indefinites; the second, its being non-declinable; the third, its not being a time. Some have rejected this: «hannā» has departed from place and been used for time, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: {هُنَالِكَ ابتلي المؤمنون} [al-Aḥzāb: 11] and the saying of the poet:
3834 - ... for there they confess: where is the refuge?
as preceded in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb; but the other two irregularities remain. Some interpreted the line in another way: that «lāta» here is disregarded and does not operate, and «hannā» is an adverbial, a fronted khabar, / and «ḥannat» is a mubtadaʾ by interpretation with the maṣdarī «an» omitted, its estimation: "an ḥannat," like «تَسْمَعُ بالمُعَيْدِيِّ خيرٌ مِنْ أَنْ تَراه». In this there is strain and remoteness, except that it has relief from the mentioned irregularities, or two irregularities.
In stopping on it there are two schools. The well-known one among the Arabs and the majority of the Seven Readers is with the extended tāʾ, following the written form of the noble copy. Al-Kisāʾī alone of the Seven stops with hāʾ. The first is the school of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Zajjāj, al-Farrāʾ and Ibn Kaysān; the second is the school of al-Mubarrad. Abū ʿUbayd was strange, saying: one stops at «لا» and the tāʾ is attached to «حين», so they say: qumtu taḥīna qumta, and taḥīna kāna kadhā faʿaltu kadhā. He said: "I saw it in the imām [the Uthmānic codex] so: «ولا تحين» connected." He also recited as evidence the saying of the poet:
3835 - Those who show kindness at the time (taḥīna) when there is no one showing kindness, and the feeders in the time when there is no feeder
But the codices are only «ولاتَ حين». The majority took what he saw as one of the irregularities of the orthographic norm, like its parallels that have passed.
As for the line, it was said: it is irregular and no attention is paid to it. It was also said: when the ḥīn annexed to the sentence containing «lāt» is omitted, it is permissible that «lā» alone be omitted and be dispensed with by the tāʾ. The original: "al-ʿāṭifūna ḥīna lāta ḥīna lā min ʿāṭifin," so the first «ḥīn» and «lā» alone were omitted, just as the annexation of «ḥīn» to it is explicit in the saying of another: 3836 - And that was when it was no time (ḥīna lāta awāna) for forbearance ... [incomplete in the source]
Ibn Mālik mentioned this view, and it is very forced. The annexation of «ḥīn» to it may also be estimated without omission of it, as in the saying:
3837 - He remembered the love of Laylā, it being no time (lāta ḥīnā) ... [incomplete in the source]
that is: "ḥīna lāta ḥīn." Also, what would Abū ʿUbayd do with his saying:
3838 - ... [incomplete in the source] and it was no hour of regret (wa-lāta sāʿata mandami)
[and his saying]:
3839 - ... lāta awāna ... [incomplete in the source]
for the tāʾ has been found with «lā» without «ḥīn»?
The second of the preceding views: that it operates as «inna» operates, meaning that it is a negator of the genus, so «ḥīna manāṣin» is its ism and its khabar is implied, its estimation: "wa-lāta ḥīna manāṣin lahum," as you say lā ghulāma safarin laka; and its ism is declined because it is an annexed noun.
The third: that after it there is an implied verb putting «ḥīna manāṣ» in the accusative, that is: "lāta araā ḥīna manāṣin lahum," meaning "I do not see that," and like it: {لاَ مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ} and "lā ahlan wa-lā sahlan," that is: they did not come to a welcome, nor meet a family, nor tread an easy ground. Al-Akhfash held these two views and they are weak. The implying of the verb here is not like its implying in the saying:
3840 - Would that there were a man, may Allah reward him well ... [incomplete in the source]
of necessity, because its ism, a single indefinite, is indeclinable on fatḥa; so when we saw this declined, we estimated a verb for it. This is contrary to al-Zajjāj, who permits its tanwīn in poetic necessity, and claims that its fatḥa is for declension, and that the tanwīn was omitted only for lightness, and argues by the line mentioned; its verification has preceded.
The fourth: that this «lāt» is not «lā» to which the tāʾ of feminine is added, but is rather «laysa», with the sīn replaced by tāʾ; they replaced it in places: they said al-nāt, meaning al-nās. From it also sitt, the original being sids. He said:
3841 - May Allah fight the sons of al-Saʿlāt, ʿAmr ibn Yarbūʿ, the worst of the people (al-nāt), they are neither good nor shrewd (akyāt)
It was also read irregularly «قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النات» to the end. He meant: shirār al-nās, and lā akyās, so he replaced. When he replaced the sīn with tāʾ, he feared its confusion with the particle of wishing, so he turned the yāʾ into alif, leaving «lāt»; this is of the category of sufficing with the letter of weakness, because the weak letter turns into alif only under conditions, among them that it has a vowel and what precedes it has fatḥa. So «ḥīna manāṣ» is its khabar, the ism being omitted as preceded, and the operation here is by right of originality, not derivation.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read {وَّلاَتِ حِينِ مَنَاصٍ} with kasra on the tāʾ and genitive «ḥīn», and this reading is / very problematic. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «lāt» governs the genitive, and recited:
3842 - ... and you will surely regret, and it will be no hour of regret (wa-lāta sāʿati mandami)
and another recited:
3843 - They sought our peace, and it was no time (wa-lāta awānin) ... [incomplete in the source]
the line. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Like it is the saying of Abū Zubayd al-Ṭāʾī: 'They sought our peace', the line. He said: If you say, what is the reason for the genitive in «awān»? I say: it is likened to «idh» in the saying:
3844 - ... and you, at that time (idhin), are healthy
in that it is a time from which the annexed noun was cut off and tanwīn was given in exchange for it, for the original is 'wa-lāta awāna ṣulḥin.' If you say: what do you say about «ḥīna manāṣin», while the annexed noun is present? I say: he treated the cutting of the annexed noun from «manāṣ» (because its origin is ḥīna manāṣihim) as the cutting of it from «ḥīn», because of the unity of the muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi, and made its tanwīn a compensation for the omitted muḍāf; then he made the ḥīn indeclinable for being annexed to a non-declinable." End.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] derived it from the implying of «min», the original being: "wa-lāta min ḥīni manāṣ," so «min» was omitted and its operation remained, like their saying: ʿalā kam jidhʿin banayta baytaka? that is: min jidhʿ, in the sounder of the two views. There is another view in it: that the genitive is by annexation, and like it is the saying:
3845 - Would that there were a man (alā rajulin), may Allah reward him well ... [incomplete in the source]
they recited it with the genitive of «rajul», that is: "alā min rajulin."
I say: it may be supported by its appearance in the saying:
3846 - ... and he said: Indeed, there is no way (lā min sabīl) to Hind
He said: "And the position of «min ḥīni manāṣ» is nominative as the ism of «lāt» in the sense of laysa, as you say laysa min rajulin qāʾiman, and the khabar is omitted; on this is the saying of Sībawayh. And on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar omitted, on the saying of al-Akhfash. Al-Akhfash derived «ولاتَ أَوانٍ» on an omitted muḍāf, meaning: the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi remained genitive as it was. The original is: wa-lāta ḥīnu awānin."
Makkī rejected this view: the muḍāf ilayhi should have stood in its place in i'rab and been put in the nominative. I say: the remaining of the muḍāf ilayhi in the genitive has occurred. It is of two kinds: little and much. The much is that there be in the wording one like the muḍāf, such as:
3847 - Do you reckon every man a man, and many a fire kindled by night a fire?
that is: "and every fire." The little is that there be not, like the reading of those who read {والله يُرِيدُ الآخرة} with genitive on «al-ākhira»; let this be of it. Though al-Mubarrad reported it in the nominative, by putting it in place of the muḍāf.
Al-Zajjāj said: "The original: wa-lāta awānanā, so the muḍāf ilayhi was omitted, so it must not be declined, and its kasra is for the meeting of two sukūns." The Shaykh said: "This is the view that al-Zamakhsharī established, taking it from Abū Isḥāq." I say: he means the first view, namely his saying: wa-lāta awāna ṣulḥin.
This is what concerns the genitive of «ḥīn».
As for the kasra of the tāʾ of «lāt», it is on the basis of the meeting of two sukūns, like jayri, except that a feminine tāʾ is known only with fatḥa.
ʿĪsā also read with kasra on the tāʾ only, and the accusative «ḥīn» like the majority. He also read «ولات حينُ» in the nominative, «مناصَ» with fatḥa. This is a very problematic reading, not far from error on the part of its transmitter from ʿĪsā, for he is of a standing in knowledge that would prevent him from such a reading. Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī derived it in his «Lawāmiḥ» on fronting and delaying, and that «ḥīn» was treated like qabl and baʿd in being indeclinable on ḍamma when cut off from annexation, by the common ground between it and them in temporal adverbiality. And «manāṣa» is its ism, indeclinable on fatḥa, separated from it by «ḥīn» cut off from annexation. / The original: wa-lāta manāṣa ḥīni kadhā, then the muḍāf ilayhi «ḥīn» was omitted and made indeclinable on ḍamma, and fronted as a separator between «lāt» and its ism. He said: "It may be that there is a meaning in that which I do not know." It has been reported of the tāʾ of «lāt»: fatḥa, kasra and ḍamma.
And His saying: «فنادَوْا» has no object, for the intention is that they performed calling, without intending a particular one called. Al-Kalbī said: "When they fought and were forced, they would call to one another: 'manāṣ,' that is: 'take to flight'; so when the punishment came to them, they said: 'manāṣ.' Then Allah the Exalted said to them: 'wa-lāta ḥīna manāṣin'." Al-Qushayrī said: "On this the estimation is: 'so they called out: manāṣ,' and it was omitted because what follows indicates it." I say: so the called one is omitted, which is some of them, and what they called with, which is "manāṣ," that is: they called one another with this expression. Al-Jurjānī said: "That is: 'so they called out when there was no escape,' that is: at the hour when there is no deliverance and no escape; when he fronted «lā» and delayed «ḥīn», this required the wāw, as the ḥāl requires when it is made a mubtadaʾ and khabar, like when you say 'jāʾa Zaydun rākiban' and then say 'jāʾa wa-huwa rākibun'. So «ḥīn» is an adverbial of His saying «فنادَوْا»." The Shaykh said: "That the origin of this sentence is 'fa-nādaw: ḥīna lā manāṣ', and that «ḥīn» is an adverbial of His saying «فنادَوْا», is a non-Arabic claim on the composition of the Qur'an, and the meaning on its composition is utterly clear." I say: al-Jurjānī does not mean that ḥīn is an adverbial of «نادَوْا» in the construction the Qur'an now has; he means that only in the original meaning and construction, as he likened it to your saying «جاء زيدٌ راكباً» and then «جاء زيدٌ وهو راكب»: «راكباً» in the first construction is a ḥāl, and in the second a khabar of a mubtadaʾ; likewise «ḥīn» was originally an adverbial of the calling, then became the khabar of «lāt» or its ism, according to the disagreement above.
Al-manāṣ: of the pattern mafʿal, from nāṣa yanūṣu, that is: he fled, so it is a maṣdar. One says nāṣahu yanūṣuhu when he escaped him; this is transitive. And nāṣa yanūṣu, that is: he lagged behind; from it nāṣa ʿan qirnihi, that is: he lagged behind from his opponent out of cowardice. Al-Farrāʾ said it, and recited the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
3848 - Is it from remembering Salmā, because she is far from you, that you flee? Then you fall short of her for a while and go forward
Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās said: "nāṣa yanūṣu, that is: he advanced, so it is among the contronyms (aḍdād)." And istanāṣa: he sought the manāṣ. Ḥāritha ibn Zayd said:
3849 - Full of pace when I shorten his rein with my two hands, he sought escape and desired the running of the mishal
One says: nāṣa ilā kadhā yanūṣu nawṣan, that is: he took refuge in it.

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ص وَالْقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ (١) بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي عِزَّةٍ وَشِقَاقٍ (٢) كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ فَنَادَوْا وَلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصٍ (٣)).
The majority read the dāl [Translator's note: i.e. the final dāl of the letter-name صَادْ] with a sukūn; its explanation has already been given.
It has been read with a kasra on it [Translator's note: i.e. صَادِ]. There are two views on it. The first: it is the kasra for the meeting of two sukūns. The second: it is an imperative from صَادَى; صَادَى الشَّيْءَ means: he faced it and matched it, i.e. "match the Qurʾān with your deeds."
It is also read with a fatḥa, i.e. "recite Ṣād" (اتْلُ صَادَ). And it has been said: it was given a vowel because of the meeting of two sukūns.
And (الْقُرْآنُ) is an oath. It has been said: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the oath, which is صَادْ.
As for the answer to the oath, it is omitted, i.e. "the truth has certainly come to you" (لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الْحَقُّ), and the like. It has been said: it is the meaning of:
(بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا), i.e. "By the truth of the Qurʾān, the disbelievers have certainly opposed and been too proud for faith."
It has been said: the answer is «كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا», with the lām omitted, i.e. "how many indeed We destroyed" (لَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا); this is far-fetched, because كَمْ is in the position of an accusative by أَهْلَكْنَا. And it has been said: it is the meaning of this clause, i.e. "We have certainly destroyed many generations."
It has been said: it is His saying [the Exalted]: (إِنْ كُلٌّ إِلَّا كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ). And it has been said: it is His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخَاصُمُ); but between them there is long speech that prevents it from being the answer.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصٍ): the origin is «لَا», to which the tāʾ was added, just as it was added to رُبَّ and ثُمَّ, so that one says رُبَّتَ and ثُمَّتْ.
Most of the Arabs give this tāʾ a fatḥa. As for the pause, some of them pause with the tāʾ, because particles are not a place for change, and some with the hāʾ, as one pauses on قَائِمَة.
As for «حِينَ», the doctrine of Sībawayh is that it is the khabar (predicate) of لَاتَ and its noun (ism) is omitted, because it operates as لَيْسَ does, i.e. "the time is not a time of flight" (لَيْسَ الْحِينُ حِينَ هَرَبٍ). One may not say that it [the noun] is latent (muḍmar), because pronouns are not latent in particles.
Al-Akhfash said: it is the one that operates in the chapter of negation [Translator's note: i.e. the lā of generic negation], so حِين is its noun and its khabar is omitted, i.e. "there is no time of escape for them" (لَا حِينَ مُنَاظِرٌ لَهُمْ) [Translator's note: so in the source; probably مَنَاصٍ is meant], or "[no such] time of theirs" (حِينُهُمْ).
Some of them put what follows it in the nominative and imply an accusative khabar, as one of them said:
فَأَنَا ابْنُ قَيْسٍ لَا بَرَاحُ
("For I am the son of Qays — there is no leaving [the field].")
Abū ʿUbayd said: the tāʾ is joined to حِين, not to لَا; he reported that they say تَحِين and تَلَان.
Some permitted the genitive after «لَاتَ», and cited verses for it; I have dealt with this exhaustively in ʿIlal al-Iʿrāb al-Kabīr.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَانْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا وَاصْبِرُوا عَلَى آلِهَتِكُمْ إِنَّ هَذَا لَشَيْءٌ يُرَادُ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنِ امْشُوا), i.e. "walk on" (امْشُوا) [Translator's note: i.e. أَنْ is explicative], because the meaning is: they set off in speech.
It has been said: it is setting off in the literal sense, and the implied form is: "and they set off saying: Walk on" (وَانْطَلَقُوا قَائِلِينَ: امْشُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمْ لَهُمْ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَلْيَرْتَقُوا فِي الْأَسْبَابِ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلْيَرْتَقُوا): this is speech construed according to the meaning, i.e. "if they claim that, then let them ascend."

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (جُنْدٌ مَا هُنَالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الْأَحْزَابِ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جُنْدٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); «مَا» is redundant (zāʾida), «هُنَالِكَ» is a naʿt (adjective), and «مَهْزُومٌ» is the khabar (predicate).
It is also permissible that «هُنَالِكَ» be an adverbial (ẓarf) for مَهْزُوم.
And (مِنَ الْأَحْزَابِ) may be a naʿt of جُنْد, or be attached (mutaʿalliq) to مَهْزُوم, or be a naʿt of مَهْزُوم.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَثَمُودُ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ وَأَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ أُولَئِكَ الْأَحْزَابُ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُولَئِكَ الْأَحْزَابُ): it may be resumptive; or it may be a khabar (predicate) whose mubtadaʾ (subject) is from His saying (وَعَادٌ), or from «ثَمُودُ», or from His saying, Exalted is He: «وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ».

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا يَنْظُرُ هَؤُلَاءِ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً مَا لَهَا مِنْ فَوَاقٍ (١٥)).
And الْفَوَاق, with a ḍamma and with a fatḥa, are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both.

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا دَاوُدَ ذَا الْأَيْدِ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ (١٧) إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا الْجِبَالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِشْرَاقِ (١٨)).
And (دَاوُدَ) is a badal (substitute).
And (سَخَّرْنَا) has been dealt with in al-Anbiyāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:21-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهَلْ أَتَاكَ نَبَأُ الْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا الْمِحْرَابَ (٢١) إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَى دَاوُدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ قَالُوا لَا تَخَفْ خَصْمَانِ بَغَى بَعْضُنَا عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا تُشْطِطْ وَاهْدِنَا إِلَى سَوَاءِ الصِّرَاطِ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْخَصْمُ): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description; that is why it is neither put in the dual nor in the plural.
The first (إِذْ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) for نَبَأ, and the second is a badal (substitute) from it, or an adverbial for «تَسَوَّرُوا». The pronoun is put in the plural though in reality it refers to two, by way of extended usage, because two is a plurality; His saying, Exalted is He, «خَصْمَانِ» indicates this, the implied form being "we are two disputants" (نَحْنُ خَصْمَانِ).

ukberi-tibyan:23-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ هَذَا أَخِي لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً وَلِيَ نَعْجَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي الْخِطَابِ (٢٣) قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَى نِعَاجِهِ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْخُلَطَاءِ لَيَبْغِي بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَا هُمْ وَظَنَّ دَاوُدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّاهُ فَاسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعًا وَأَنَابَ (٢٤) فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُ ذَلِكَ وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنَا لَزُلْفَى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَعَزَّنِي): with the doubled consonant, i.e. "he overcame me" (غَلَبَنِي).
It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with the undoubled consonant, and the meaning is the same. It has been said: it is from وَعِزَ بِكَذَا, when one commands something; this is far-fetched, because before it there is a verb to which this would be conjoined — so some have stated.
It is also possible that the verb of saying has been omitted, i.e. "so he said: Entrust her to me; and he said: and he overcame me in speech."
And (سُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its direct object.
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): an exception from the same genus, and what it is excepted from is بَعْضُهُمْ; «مَا» is redundant (zāʾida), «هُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «قَلِيلٌ» is its khabar (predicate). It has been said: the implied form is "and they are few among them" (وَهُمْ قَلِيلٌ مِنْهُمْ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتَنَّاهُ): with a doubled nūn, attributing the verb to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and with an undoubled one [Translator's note: i.e. فَتَنَاهُ], attributing it to the two angels.
(رَاكِعًا): an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) . . . [Translator's note: the ellipsis is in the source.]
And (ذَلِكَ) is the object of «غَفَرْنَا». It has been said: it is the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that" (الْأَمْرُ ذَلِكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا دَاوُدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ الْهَوَى فَيُضِلَّكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِمَا نَسُوا يَوْمَ الْحِسَابِ (٢٤)) [Translator's note: so numbered in the source; this verse is 38:26].
(فَيُضِلَّكَ): accusative as the answer [to the prohibition]. It has been said: it is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the prohibition, and the lām was given a fatḥa because of the meeting of two sukūns.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بَاطِلًا ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنَ النَّارِ (٢٧)).
And (بَاطِلًا) has been dealt with in Āl ʿImrān; and «أَمْ» in the two places [Translator's note: in the following verse, 28] is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa).

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (٢٩)).
And (كِتَابٌ), i.e. "this is a Book" (هَذَا كِتَابٌ); and «مُبَارَكٌ» is another adjective (ṣifa).

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَوَهَبْنَا لِدَاوُدَ سُلَيْمَانَ نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ (٣٠)).
(نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ), i.e. Sulaymān; and it has been said: Dāwūd. So the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted; and likewise in the story of Ayyūb.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَشِيِّ الصَّافِنَاتُ الْجِيَادُ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ عُرِضَ): it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) for أَوَّاب; or its governor may be «نِعْمَ»; or the implied form may be "remember" (اذْكُرْ).
And (الْجِيَادُ) is the plural of جَوَاد; and it has been said: of جَيِّد.

ukberi-tibyan:32-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَقَالَ إِنِّي أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي حَتَّى تَوَارَتْ بِالْحِجَابِ (٣٢) رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحًا بِالسُّوقِ وَالْأَعْنَاقِ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ): it is the object of أَحْبَبْتُ, because the meaning of أَحْبَبْتُ is "I preferred" (آثَرْتُ); [it is not taken as its maṣdar] because the maṣdar of أَحْبَبْتُ is الْإِحْبَاب.
It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) with its augment omitted.
Abū ʿAlī said: أَحْبَبْتُ has the meaning of "I sat down", from إِحْبَاب of the camel, which is its kneeling down.
And «حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ» is then a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), annexed to its object.
And (ذِكْرِ رَبِّي): it too is annexed to the object [Translator's note: i.e. "from my remembering my Lord"]. It has been said: to the agent, i.e. "from my Lord's remembering me" (عَنْ أَنْ يَذْكُرَنِي رَبِّي).
The fāʿil (agent) of «تَوَارَتْ» is the sun; it has not been mentioned, but the situation indicates it.
It has been said: the mention of الْإِشْرَاق (sunrise) in the story of Dāwūd, peace be upon him, indicates it.
And (رُدُّوهَا): the pronoun refers to the horses (الْجِيَاد).
And (مَسْحًا) is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It has been said: the implied form is "stroking with a stroking" (يَمْسَحُ مَسْحًا).

ukberi-tibyan:34-37.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَانَ وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ (٣٤) قَالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لَا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ (٣٥) فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ الرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخَاءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ (٣٦) وَالشَّيَاطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّاءٍ وَغَوَّاصٍ (٣٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَسَدًا): it is the object of «أَلْقَيْنَا». It has been said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from an omitted object, i.e. "We cast him"; it has been said: Sulaymān; and it has been said: his child, according to what has come in the exegesis (tafsīr).
And (تَجْرِي) is a ḥāl from الرِّيح.
And (رُخَاءً) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in تَجْرِي, i.e. "gentle" (لَيِّنَةً).
And (حَيْثُ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) for تَجْرِي; and it has been said: for سَخَّرْنَا.
And (الشَّيَاطِينَ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الرِّيح, and «كُلَّ» is a badal (substitute) from them.

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا عَطَاؤُنَا فَامْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ): it has been said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «امْنُنْ» or in «أَمْسِكْ», the meaning being "without being called to account" (غَيْرَ مُحَاسَبٍ).
It has been said: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to عَطَاؤُنَا.
And it has been said: it is a ḥāl from it, i.e. "this is Our gift, abundant" (هَذَا عَطَاؤُنَا وَاسِعًا), because الْحِسَاب has the meaning of "sufficient" (الْكَافِي).

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنَا لَزُلْفَى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنَا لَزُلْفَى): [«زُلْفَى»] is the noun (ism) of إِنَّ, and the khabar (predicate) is «لَهُ»; and what governs «عِنْدَ» is the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَى رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِنُصْبٍ): there are readings of it close in meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَذِكْرَى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ (٤٣)).
And (رَحْمَةً) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاذْكُرْ عِبَادَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصَارِ (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عِبَادَنَا): it is read in the plural, and the names after it are a badal (substitute) from it; and in the singular [Translator's note: i.e. عَبْدَنَا], in which case «إِبْرَاهِيمَ» is a badal from it and what follows is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to عَبْدَنَا.
It may also be a generic noun with the meaning of a plural, so that it is like the first reading.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ (٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِخَالِصَةٍ): it is read with annexation (iḍāfa) [Translator's note: i.e. بِخَالِصَةِ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ]; here it belongs to the category of annexing a thing to what clarifies it, because الْخَالِصَة may be a remembrance or something other than a remembrance.
And (ذِكْرَى) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and «خَالِصَةٍ» is also a maṣdar with the meaning of الْإِخْلَاص (making pure), like الْعَافِيَة.
It has been said: «خَالِصَةٍ» is a maṣdar annexed to its object, i.e. "by their making pure the remembrance of the Abode" (بِإِخْلَاصِهِمْ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ). And it has been said: «خَالِصَةٍ» has the meaning of خُلُوص (being pure), so it is annexed to its agent, i.e. "in that the remembrance of the Abode was purely theirs" (بِأَنْ خَلَصَتْ لَهُمْ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ).
It has been said: «خَالِصَةٍ» is an active participle, its implied form being "by a pure [quality], the remembrance of the Abode" (بِخَالِصٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ), i.e. pure from being mixed with anything else.
It has been read with tanwīn on «خَالِصَةٍ»; then «ذِكْرَى» may be a badal (substitute) from it; or be in the position of an accusative as the object of خَالِصَة, or by an implied «أَعْنِي» (I mean); or be in the position of a nominative as the agent of «خَالِصَة», or on the implied form "it is a remembrance" (هِيَ ذِكْرَى).
As for the annexation of «ذِكْرَى» to «الدَّارِ», it is the annexation of the maṣdar to its object, i.e. "by their remembering the Abode of the Hereafter."
It has been said: in meaning it is an adverbial (ẓarf), i.e. "their being remembered in the abode of this world"; so it is either a direct object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), as in "O thief of the night" (يَا سَارِقَ اللَّيْلَةِ), or by omission of the preposition, as in "I went [to] Syria" (ذَهَبْتُ الشَّامَ).

ukberi-tibyan:49-50.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا ذِكْرٌ وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (٤٩) جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الْأَبْوَابُ (٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ): it is a badal (substitute) from «حُسْنَ مَآبٍ».
And (مُفَتَّحَةً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from جَنَّات, according to those who make it definite by its annexation to عَدْن, which is a proper name, as they said "the Garden of Eternity" (جَنَّةُ الْخُلْدِ) and "the Garden of Refuge" (جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَى).
Others said: it is indefinite, the meaning being "gardens of residence", so «مُفَتَّحَةً» is an adjective.
As for the nominative of (الْأَبْوَابُ), there are three views on it. The first: it is the fāʿil (agent) of «مُفَتَّحَةً» [Translator's note: i.e. in effect its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), مُفَتَّحَة being a passive participle], and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "with the gates of them opened for them" (مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الْأَبْوَابُ مِنْهَا); it was omitted as it was omitted in His saying: (فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى), i.e. "for them". The second: it is a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in (مُفَتَّحَةً), which is the pronoun of the gardens; and «الْأَبْوَابُ» is not foreign to them, because they are part of the garden: you say "the garden was opened" meaning its gates; and of this kind is: (وَفُتِحَتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَابًا).
The third: like the first, except that the alif and lām are a substitute for the returning hāʾ; this is the view of the Kufans, and it is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ وَشَرَابٍ (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُتَّكِئِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive [pronoun] in «لَهُمْ», and the governor is «مُفَتَّحَةً».
It may also be a ḥāl from «الْمُتَّقِينَ», because a report has been made about them before the ḥāl.
It has been said: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَدْعُونَ», and it has come before its governor.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ الْحِسَابِ (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا تُوعَدُونَ): with yāʾ, as third person, the pronoun referring to the God-fearing; and with tāʾ, the implied form being "and it was said to them: this is what you are promised", the meaning being: "this is what you were promised."

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ هَذَا لَرِزْقُنَا مَا لَهُ مِنْ نَفَادٍ (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَالَهُ مِنْ نَفَادٍ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرِّزْق, and the governor is the demonstrative, i.e. "this is Our provision, lasting" (إِنَّ هَذَا لَرِزْقُنَا بَاقِيًا).

ukberi-tibyan:55-56.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ (٥٥) جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ (٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَذَا), i.e. "the matter is this" (الْأَمْرُ هَذَا). Then He began anew and said: «وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ».
And (جَهَنَّمَ) is a badal (substitute) from «شَرَّ».
And (يَصْلَوْنَهَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the [notion of] being settled (al-istiqrār) in His saying, Exalted is He: «لِلطَّاغِينَ».
It has been said: the implied form is "they will burn in Jahannam" (يَصْلَوْنَ جَهَنَّمَ); the verb was omitted because what follows indicates it.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ (٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَذَا): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two views on the khabar (predicate):
The first: (فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ), as in your saying "Zayd — strike him" (زَيْدٌ اضْرِبْهُ).
Some said: this is weak because of the fāʾ, since it does not have the sense of an answer, like the one in His saying: (وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا). As for (حَمِيمٌ) on this view, it may be a badal (substitute) from هَذَا, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is scalding water" (هُوَ حَمِيمٌ), or a second khabar.
The second view: that (حَمِيمٌ) is the khabar of (هَذَا), with (فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ) parenthetical between them.
It has been said: هَذَا is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "let them taste this" (فَلْيَذُوقُوا هَذَا); then He began anew and said (حَمِيمٌ), i.e. "it is scalding water" (هُوَ حَمِيمٌ).
As for (غَسَّاقٌ), it is read with the doubled consonant, like كَفَّار and صَبَّار; and with the undoubled one [Translator's note: i.e. غَسَاقٌ] as a noun for the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), i.e. "possessing darkness" (ذُو غَسَقٍ); or فَعَّال has the meaning of فَاعِل.

ukberi-tibyan:58-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَآخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ أَزْوَاجٌ (٥٨) هَذَا فَوْجٌ مُقْتَحِمٌ مَعَكُمْ لَا مَرْحَبًا بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صَالُوا النَّارِ (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَآخَرُ): it is read in the plural [Translator's note: i.e. وَأُخَرُ], and there are two views on it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
«مِنْ شَكْلِهِ» is a naʿt (adjective) of it, i.e. "of the kind of the scalding water", and «أَزْوَاجٌ» is its khabar (predicate).
The second: the khabar is omitted, i.e. "and they have other [kinds]" (وَلَهُمْ أُخَرُ), and «مِنْ شَكْلِهِ» and «أَزْوَاجٌ» are two adjectives.
It is also permissible that «مِنْ شَكْلِهِ» be an adjective and «أَزْوَاجٌ» be put in the nominative by the preposition-phrase.
The pronoun is masculine because the meaning is "of the kind of what we have mentioned."
It is also read in the singular [Translator's note: i.e. وَآخَرُ], conjoined (maʿṭūf) to حَمِيم; «مِنْ شَكْلِهِ» is a naʿt of it, and «أَزْوَاجٌ» is put in the nominative by the preposition-phrase.
It may also be nominative on the implied form "it is", i.e. the scalding water.
And the other kind is His saying, Exalted is He: (مُقْتَحِمٌ), i.e. [rushing into] the Fire [Translator's note: so in the source].
And (مَعَكُمْ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مُقْتَحِمٌ, or from (فَوْجٌ), because it has been qualified; it may not be an adverbial (ẓarf), because the meaning would be corrupted. It may also be a second naʿt.
And (لَا مَرْحَبًا): it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl, i.e. "this is a troop to whom it is said: No welcome" (هَذَا فَوْجٌ مَقُولًا لَهُ: لَا مَرْحَبًا).
And مَرْحَبًا is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or as a direct object, i.e. "they do not hear [a] welcome" (لَا يَسْمَعُونَ مَرْحَبًا).

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا رَبَّنَا مَنْ قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَذَا فَزِدْهُ عَذَابًا ضِعْفًا فِي النَّارِ (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ قَدَّمَ): it has the meaning of الَّذِي, and «فَزِدْهُ» is the khabar (predicate).
It is also permissible that «مَنْ» be accusative, i.e. "so increase whoever brought forward…" (فَزِدْ مَنْ قَدَّمَ).
It has been said: it is an interrogative expressing magnification; so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and قَدَّمَ is the khabar, and then a new sentence begins; there is weakness in this.
And (ضِعْفًا) is a naʿt (adjective) of عَذَاب, i.e. "doubled" (مُضَاعَفًا).
And (فِي النَّارِ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) for زِدْ.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, i.e. "increase him while he is in the Fire" (زِدْهُ كَائِنًا فِي النَّارِ); or a second naʿt of عَذَاب; or a ḥāl [from it], because it has been qualified.

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا أَمْ زَاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ الْأَبْصَارُ (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ): it is read with a disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), because it is for the interrogative; and with the connecting one (waṣl), on the omission of the interrogative particle, because أَمْ indicates it. It has been said: the first [i.e. the clause on this reading] is a statement, and is in meaning an adjective of رِجَال [Translator's note: in the preceding verse, مَا لَنَا لَا نَرَى رِجَالًا]; and «أَمْ» is interrogative, i.e. "are they missing, or have [the eyes] turned aside?" (أَهُمْ مَفْقُودُونَ أَمْ زَاغَتْ).
And (سِخْرِيًّا) has been dealt with in «al-Muʾminūn».

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ): it is a badal (substitute) from «حَقٌّ», or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is the disputing" (هُوَ تَخَاصُمٌ).
If it were said that it is nominative by حَقّ [Translator's note: i.e. as its agent], that would be far-fetched, because it would then become a clause with no pronoun in it referring back to the noun of «إِنَّ».

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ): it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); or an adjective (ṣifa); or a badal (substitute); or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «الْعَزِيزُ».

ukberi-tibyan:69-70.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا كَانَ لِيَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ بِالْمَلَأِ الْأَعْلَى إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ (٦٩) إِنْ يُوحَى إِلَيَّ إِلَّا أَنَّمَا أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ): it is an adverbial (ẓarf) for عِلْم.
And (أَنَّمَا) is nominative by يُوحَى إِلَيَّ [Translator's note: i.e. as its deputy agent].
It has been said: «إِلَيَّ» stands in the place of the fāʿil (agent), and إنما [Translator's note: so in the source; أَنَّمَا is meant] is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "the warning was revealed to me" (أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ الْإِنْذَارُ), or "that I am a warner" (بِأَنِّي نَذِيرٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي خَالِقٌ بَشَرًا مِنْ طِينٍ (٧١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ), i.e. "remember when He said" (اذْكُرْ إِذْ قَالَ).
(مِنْ طِينٍ): it may be a naʿt (adjective) of بَشَر, or be attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَالِق.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فَالْحَقُّ وَالْحَقَّ أَقُولُ (٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَالْحَقُّ) [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the discussion is of the accusative reading فَالْحَقَّ]: there are two views on its accusative. The first: it is the object of an omitted verb, i.e. "so establish the truth" (فَأَحِقَّ الْحَقَّ), or "so mention the truth" (فَاذْكُرِ الْحَقَّ). The second: on the implied omission of the oath, i.e. "so by the truth, I will surely fill" (فَبِالْحَقِّ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ).
(وَالْحَقَّ أَقُولُ) is then parenthetical between them. Sībawayh rejects that, because it [Translator's note: the preposition of the oath] may not be omitted except with the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
It is also read in the nominative, i.e. "for I am the Truth" (فَأَنَا الْحَقُّ), or "for the truth is from Me" (فَالْحَقُّ مِنِّي).
As for the second «الْحَقُّ», its accusative is by أَقُولُ. It is [also] read [in the nominative], on the implied repetition of the nominative before it, or by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "my saying is the truth" (قَوْلِي الْحَقُّ); on this view «أَقُولُ» is resumptive and joined to what follows it, i.e. "I say: I will surely fill" (أَقُولُ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ).
It has been said: «أَقُولُ» is a khabar (predicate) about it, with the hāʾ omitted, i.e. "I say it" (أَقُولُهُ); this is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ بَعْدَ حِينٍ (٨٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ), i.e. "you will surely know" (لَتَعْرِفُنَّ); it has one object, which is «نَبَأَهُ». It may also be transitive to two objects, the second being «بَعْدَ حِينٍ».

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Ṣād
Meccan
﷽
﴿ص﴾: it has been read with fatḥa, with kasra, and with the dāl made quiescent (sukūn), and this last is the most common reading. Whoever makes it quiescent reads "صادْ" as one of the letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf al-hijāʾ), the dāl being treated as in a pause (waqf); we have explained this under His saying "الـم", I mean the chapter on the letters of the alphabet. Its meaning is "Allah is the Truthful (اَلصّادِقُ اللَّهُ)". It has also been said that it is an oath.
And His saying: ﴿والقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; the meaning is: "I swear by Ṣād, and by the Qur'an possessed of remembrance (أُقْسِمُ بِصادِ، وبِالقُرْآنِ ذِي الذَّكَرِ)". Whoever gives it fatḥa does so in two ways: it may be a fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn), and it may be in the sense of "recite Ṣād (اُتْلُ صادَ)", with "صادَ" being a name of the sūra, a diptote. Whoever gives it kasra does so in two ways: because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, or with kasra in the sense of "confront (ṣādi) the Qur'an with your deeds (صادِ القُرْآنَ بِعَمَلِكَ)", from your saying "صادى، يُصادِي" when one faces and matches [something]; one says "صادَيْتُهُ" when you have faced him.
The answer (jawāb) to His saying ﴿ص والقُرْآنِ﴾ is ﴿إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخاصُمُ أهْلِ النّارِ﴾ [Ṣād: 64]. Some people said: the answer is ﴿كَمْ أهْلَكْنا مِن قَبْلِهِمْ مِن قَرْنٍ﴾ [Ṣād: 3], its meaning being "لَكَمْ أهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهم مِن قَرْنٍ" (how many a generation We indeed destroyed before them); since the speech between the two became long, the lām was omitted.
The meaning of "والقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ" is: "possessed of mention and honour (ذِي الذِّكْرِ والشَّرَفِ)". It has also been said that "ذِي الذِّكْرِ" means: in it are mentioned the stories of the former and the later peoples, and what is needed concerning the lawful and the unlawful.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿أمْ لَهم مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: nothing of that is theirs. ﴿فَلْيَرْتَقُوا في الأسْبابِ﴾, that is: if they claim anything of that, then let them ascend by the means (asbāb) that would bring them to the heaven. It is also possible that it means "let them ascend by these means that have been mentioned, which none but Allah possesses".

zajjaj:11-11.t: Then Allah promised His Prophet, upon him be peace, victory over them, and said: ﴿جُنْدٌ ما هُنالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الأحْزابِ﴾. "ما" is redundant (laghw); the meaning is: "جُنْدٌ هُنالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الأحْزابِ" (a host there, routed, of the confederates).

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿وَفِرْعَوْنُ ذُو الأوْتادِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that Pharaoh had ropes and stakes on which people would perform for him «[Translator's note: «يُلْعَبُ لَهُ عَلَيْها», literally "played on for him".]».

zajjaj:3-3.t:
﴿فَنادَوْا ولاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ﴾: it has come in the exegesis (tafsīr): "and it was no time for calling out (وَلاتَ حِينَ نِداءٍ)". The people of the language said: "and it was no time for escape (وَلاتَ حِينَ مَنجًى)" and "no escaping (لا فَوْتَ)". One says "ناصَهُ، يَنُوصُهُ" when something has escaped him. In the exegesis, "لاتَ حِينَ نِداءٍ" means: "it was no time for a calling out that would save". It is also permissible to read "لاتَ حِينُ مَناصٍ" [with nominative], and the nominative is good.
The pause (waqf) on it is "لاتْ", with tāʾ; al-Kisāʾī pauses on it with hāʾ, "لاهْ", because he makes it the hāʾ of the feminine. The correct pause on it is with tāʾ, and this tāʾ is analogous to the tāʾ in the verb when you say "ذَهَبْتُ، وجَلَسْتُ", and in your saying "رَأيْتُ زَيْدًا ثُمَّتَ عَمْرًا" (I saw Zayd, then ʿAmr). So the tāʾ of particles is equivalent to the tāʾ of verbs, because in both places the tāʾ has entered upon something that is not declined (lā yuʿrab) and is not on the path of nouns.
If someone says: we treat it like their saying "كانَ مِنَ الأمْرِ ذَيْهْ" and "ذَيْهْ" (such-and-such happened), for this is a hāʾ in pause, and this is a hāʾ that has entered upon a noun which is not declined. «[Translator's note: the source gives no explicit reply to this objection.]»
They have also permitted the genitive (khafḍ), saying "لاتَ أوانٍ", and they recited, by Abū Zubayd:
؎طَلَبُوا صُلْحَنا ولاتَ أوانٍ ∗∗∗ فَأجَبْنا أنْ لَيْسَ حِينَ بَقاءِ
(They sought peace with us when it was no longer the time, so we answered that it was no time for survival.)
What Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] recited to us — and so he narrated it — was:
طَلَبُوا صُلْحَنا ولاتَ أوانٌ
and he mentioned that the kasra has also been narrated.
As for the accusative, it is on the basis that it [لات] operates as "لَيْسَ" operates; the meaning is "and the time is not a time of escape (وَلَيْسَ الوَقْتُ حِينَ مَناصٍ)". Whoever puts it in the nominative with it makes "حِينَ" the subject (ism) of "لَيْسَ" and implies the predicate (khabar), in the sense of "there is no time of escape for us (لَيْسَ حِينُ مَنجًى لَنا)". Whoever puts it in the genitive makes it indeclinable (mabnī) with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, just as they said "قَدِ لَكَ" and made it indeclinable on kasra.
The meaning is "it is not the time of our escape and the time of our deliverance (لَيْسَ حِينُ مَناصِنا وحِينُ مَنجانا)". So when he said "وَلاتَ أوانَ", he made it in the sense of "it is not the time of our [proper] time (لَيْسَ حِينَ أوانِنا)"; when the muḍāf ilayhi «[Translator's note: the source says «المضاف» (the muḍāf), though what is dropped from «أوانِنا» is the attached pronoun, i.e. the muḍāf ilayhi.]» was omitted, it was made indeclinable on the pause form, then given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The kasra is anomalous (shādhdh), resembling an error in the view of the Basrans; Sībawayh and al-Khalīl did not narrate the kasra, and what is followed in practice is the accusative and the nominative.
Al-Akhfash said that in "لاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ" its accusative is by "لا", just as you say "لا رَجُلَ في الدّارِ" (there is no man in the house), and the tāʾ entered for the feminine.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقالَ الكافِرُونَ هَذا ساحِرٌ كَذّابٌ﴾, up to His saying: ﴿لَشَيْءٌ عُجابٌ﴾ [Ṣād: 5], in the sense of "wondrous (عَجِيبٌ)". "عُجّابٌ" is also permissible, in the sense of "عَجِيبٌ"; one says "رَجُلٌ كَرِيمٌ، وكُرّامٌ، وكُرامٌ" (a generous man).
This is a report of what a group of the notables of Quraysh said: «When Abū Ṭālib fell ill with the illness in which he died, Abū Jahl ibn Hishām and a group of Quraysh came to visit him, and they complained to him about the Prophet ﷺ and said: He insults our gods and does such-and-such. So Abū Ṭālib reproached him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "I am calling you to a word by which the Arabs will submit to you, and by which the non-Arabs will pay you the jizya." Abū Jahl said: Yes, and ten [more], by way of mockery, meaning: we will say it and ten others with it. So he said: "There is no god but Allah (لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ)." They said: Has he made the gods one God? Then they rose and left their gathering, saying to one another: Walk on and be steadfast for your gods.»

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿وانْطَلَقَ المَلأُ مِنهم أنِ امْشُوا﴾: its meaning is: that is, "walk on (اِمْشُوا)"; its interpretation is: they say "walk on". It is also permissible [to understand it as] "وانْطَلَقَ المَلَأُ مِنهم بِأنِ امْشُوا" (the notables among them went forth with "walk on"), that is, with this saying.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿ما سَمِعْنا بِهَذا في المِلَّةِ الآخِرَةِ﴾ is also a report of what they said, that is: we have not heard of this in Christianity, nor in Judaism, nor in what we found our forefathers upon. ﴿إنْ هَذا إلا اخْتِلاقٌ﴾, that is: nothing but a fabricated saying (taqawwul).

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿أأُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِن بَيْنِنا﴾, that is: how has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us? That is: how has the Qur'an been sent down to Muhammad from among us?! ﴿بَلْ هم في شَكٍّ مِن ذِكْرِي﴾, that is: they say what they hold only while being in doubt.

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ﴾: if someone asks: what is the connection of ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ﴾ with His saying ﴿بَلْ هم في شَكٍّ مِن ذِكْرِي﴾ [Ṣād: 8], or with His saying ﴿أأُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِن بَيْنِنا﴾ [Ṣād: 8]? [The answer is that] this is evidence of their envy of the Prophet ﷺ for the favour of prophethood that Allah gave him. So Allah made known that sovereignty belongs to Him and the message is His to give; He chooses whom He wills, gives sovereignty to whom He wills, and sends down rain and mercy upon whom He wills. So He said: ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ﴾, that is: they do not have that.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿ما لَها مِن فَواقٍ﴾, and "فُواقٍ", with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the fāʾ, that is: "it has no return (ما لَها مِن رُجُوعٍ)". "اَلْفُواقُ" is the interval between two milkings of the she-camel, and it too is derived from [the sense of] returning, because the milk returns to the udder between the two milkings. "أفاقَ مِن مَرَضِهِ" (he recovered from his illness) is from this, that is, he returned to health; so "الفَواقُ" is from this as well.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
﴿وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا﴾: "اَلْقِطُّ" is the share (naṣīb). Its origin is the written sheet (ṣaḥīfa) in which something due to reach a person is written for him. Al-Aʿshā said:
؎وَلا المَلِكُ النُّعْمانُ يَوْمَ لَقِيتُهُ ∗∗∗ بِغِبْطَتِهِ يُعْطِي القُطُوطَ ويَأْفِقُ
(Nor King al-Nuʿmān, on the day I met him in his prosperity, giving out written grants and bestowing generously.)
"يَأْفِقُ" means: he gives in excess (yufḍil). This is the explanation of their saying "عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا", and it is like their saying: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32], to the end of the verse. It has also been said that when they heard that the believer will be given his book in his right hand and the disbeliever will be given his book in his left hand, so that the believer is made happy and the disbeliever is ruined, they said: "Our Lord, hasten for us our share (عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا)".
The derivation of "اَلْقِطُّ" is from "قَطَطْتُ", that is, "I cut (قَطَعْتُ)"; and likewise the share is simply a piece (qiṭʿa) of a thing.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ ذا الأيْدِ﴾: "possessed of strength (ذا القُوَّةِ)". His strength in worship was the most complete strength: he used to fast one day and break his fast one day, and that is the most severe fasting, and he used to pray half the night.
﴿إنَّهُ أوّابٌ﴾: "one who returns to Allah often (رَجّاعٌ إلى اللَّهِ كَثِيرًا)". "اَلْآيِبُ" is the one who returns, and "اَلْأوّابُ" is the one who returns often.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿إنّا سَخَّرْنا الجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِالعَشِيِّ والإشْراقِ﴾: "اَلْإشْراقُ" is the rising of the sun and its shining. One says "شَرِقَتِ الشَّمْسُ" when the sun rises, and "أشْرَقَتْ" when it shines. It has also been said that "شَرِقَتْ" and "أشْرَقَتْ", when it rises, have one meaning; but the first is more common.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿والطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً كُلٌّ لَهُ أوّابٌ﴾: the mountains used to repeat the glorification (tasbīḥ) back, and so did the birds. It is possible that the hāʾ [in لَهُ] refers to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, that is: "all glorify Allah — the birds, the mountains and David glorify Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and repeat the glorification". And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that "كُلٌّ لَّهُ أوّابٌ" means: all of them repeat the glorification with David, answering him; whenever he glorified, the mountains and the birds glorified with him.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
﴿وَشَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ﴾: "وَشَدَّدْنا" [with doubled dāl] is also permissible, but I do not know anyone who read it so. Its meaning is "We strengthened his kingdom". Part of the strengthening of his kingdom was that his sanctuary (miḥrāb) was guarded every night by thirty-three thousand men.
It has also been said that a man sought his help against another man, claiming that he had taken cattle from him. The defendant denied it, so David asked the claimant for evidence (bayyina), but he could not produce it. Then David saw in his sleep that Allah was commanding him to kill the defendant. David held back and said: it is a dream. Then revelation came to him after that that he should kill him. So he summoned him and informed him that Allah had commanded him to kill him. The defendant said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has not taken me to task for this sin; rather, I killed this man's father treacherously. So David killed him. That was among the things by which Allah exalted him and strengthened his kingdom.
﴿وَآتَيْناهُ الحِكْمَةَ وفَصْلَ الخِطابِ﴾: it has been said about this: that he judges by evidence and oath. It has been said about "فَصْلَ الخِطابِ": that he distinguishes between truth and falsehood. And it has been said: [it is the phrase] "أمّا بَعْدُ" (as for what follows), and he was the first to say "أمّا بَعْدُ".

zajjaj:21-21.t:
﴿وَهَلْ أتاكَ نَبَأُ الخَصْمِ إذْ تَسَوَّرُوا المِحْرابَ﴾: "اَلْمِحْرابُ" is the highest room in the house, and likewise it is the highest place in the mosque; "اَلْمِحْرابُ" here is like an upper chamber (ghurfa). The poet said:
؎رَبَّةُ مِحْرابٍ إذا جِئْتُها ∗∗∗ لَمْ ألْقَها أوْ أرْتَقِي سُلَّما
(Mistress of an upper chamber: when I come to her, I cannot meet her unless I climb a ladder.)
"تَسَوَّرُوا" (they climbed over the wall) indicates height.
He said "اَلْخَصْمِ", whose form is the form of the singular, while "تَسَوَّرُوا" is the form of the plural, because your saying "خَصْمٌ" is suitable for the singular, the dual and the plural, the masculine and the feminine. One says "هَذا خَصْمٌ", "هي خَصْمٌ", "هُما خَصْمٌ" and "هم خَصْمٌ". It is suitable for all of that only because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun): you say "خَصَمْتُهُ، أخْصِمُهُ، خَصْمًا". The meaning is "they two are parties to a dispute (هُما ذَوا خَصْمٍ)" and "they are parties to a dispute (هم ذَوُو خَصْمٍ)". If you say "خُصُومٌ", it is permissible, just as you say "هُما عَدْلٌ" and "هُما ذَوا عَدْلٍ"; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَأشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 2]. So the meaning of "هُما عَدْلٌ" is "هُما ذَوا عَدْلٍ" (they two are possessors of justice).
Whatever verbal nouns you have used to describe nouns may be kept singular even if you describe a plural with them, and may be kept masculine even if you describe a feminine with them. You say "هو رِضًى" (he is pleasing), "هُما رِضًى", and likewise "هَذِهِ رِضًى".

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إذْ دَخَلُوا عَلى داوُدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنهُمْ﴾: because they came to him not by the way litigants come, not at their [usual] time, and at a time in which David did not permit anyone to enter upon him; so he found that strange and was alarmed. In fact, two angels were sent to him, who took the form of two men disputing with each other.
﴿قالُوا لا تَخَفْ خَصْمانِ بَغى بَعْضُنا عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾: the reading is with the nominative, and what makes "خَصْمانِ" nominative is "نَحْنُ" (we); the meaning is "we are two litigants (نَحْنُ خَصْمانِ)". Had the speech been "لا تَخَفْ خَصْمَيْنِ بَغى بَعْضُنا عَلى بَعْضٍ", it would be permissible, in the sense of "we have come to you as two litigants (أتَيْناكَ خَصْمَيْنِ)", because he found their coming strange, whereas the coming of litigants was something he was very much used to.
﴿فاحْكم بَيْنَنا بِالحَقِّ ولا تُشْطِطْ﴾, that is: "do not be unjust (لا تَجُرْ)"; one says "أشَطَّ، يُشِطُّ" when one is unjust. It is also read "لا تَشْطُطْ", in the sense of "do not go far from the truth", and likewise "لا تَشْطِطْ", with kasra on the ṭāʾ and fatḥa on the tāʾ, whose meaning is like the meaning of the previous one. The poet said:
؎تَشُطُّ غَدًا دارُ جِيرانِنا ∗∗∗ ولَلدّارُ بَعْدَ غَدٍ أبْعَدُ
(Tomorrow the abode of our neighbours will be far, and the abode the day after tomorrow farther still.)
﴿واهْدِنا إلى سَواءِ الصِّراطِ﴾: to the straight course of the road, that is, "the road of truth".

zajjaj:23-23.t:
﴿تِسْعٌ وتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً﴾: He used the ewe (naʿja) as a metonym (kināya) for a woman. Al-Aʿshā said:
؎فَرَمَيْتُ غُفْلَةَ عَيْنِهِ عَنْ شاتِهِ ∗∗∗ فَأصَبْتُ حَبَّةَ قَلْبِها وطِحالَها
(I shot when his eye was heedless of his ewe, and struck the core of her heart and her spleen.)
By "the ewe (al-shāt)" here he meant the woman.
﴿فَقالَ أكْفِلْنِيها﴾, that is: make me the one who takes charge of her, and you give her up. ﴿وَعَزَّنِي في الخِطابِ﴾: he overcame me in the dispute, that is, he was stronger than me in argument.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
﴿قالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إلى نِعاجِهِ﴾: the meaning is "by his asking for your ewe so that he may add it to his ewes (بِسُؤالِهِ نَعْجَتَكَ لِيَضُمَّها إلى نِعاجِهِ)". ﴿وَإنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الخُلَطاءِ﴾: of the partners; you say "فُلانٌ خَلِيطِي، وشَرِيكِي" (so-and-so is my associate, my partner) with one meaning. ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ وقَلِيلٌ ما هُمْ﴾, that is: "few are they (قَلِيلٌ هُمْ)".
